Three new `inkhaven language export` formats +
three new headless CLIs.

* `--format grammar` — printable grammar
  reference.  TOC + chapter per rule category +
  examples table + cross-references.  Output
  via the typst in-process compiler.
* `--format phrasebook` — Sample-texts chapter
  rendered as a two-column phrasebook (gloss
  left, working language right).
* `--format csv` — round-trip-compatible CSV
  that the existing `--import` path can
  re-ingest.  Closes the import/export loop.
* `inkhaven language test <name>` — headless
  roundtrip-translation drift CLI for CI.
  Walks a corpus of sample texts through
  `Ctrl+B Q` → `Ctrl+B Shift+Q` and reports
  drift > configurable threshold.
* `inkhaven language translate <language>
  <text>` — headless flavour of the in-TUI
  chord.  Shell-pipe friendly.
* `inkhaven language define-rule <language>
  <rule_id> --category <cat>` — open the rule
  template in `$EDITOR` for hand-editing.

Test budget: ~8 (one per export format roundtrip
+ a `language test` drift detector test + CLI
smoke tests).

### 3.2 P6 — Snippet picker placeholders + `bund:` prefix (Q.2 carryover from 1.2.14)

Three picker-based placeholders and one Bund-VM
prefix.  All four need the **async snippet state
machine** that wasn't built in 1.2.14.

* `{char_lookup}` / `{place_lookup}` /
  `{artefact_lookup}` — open the corresponding
  system-book picker; substitute the chosen
  entry's display name on commit.
* `bund:` prefix — when the snippet body starts
  with `bund:`, the rest is interpreted as a
  Bund-VM program; its top-of-stack string
  becomes the expansion.

Implementation lift: new `Modal::SnippetPicker`
variant that wraps an existing
`{char,place,artefact}` picker, returns the
chosen entry to a continuation callback that
completes the expansion.  Bund-VM evaluator
called synchronously (Bund is fast); error
falls back to literal expansion of the source
text.

Test budget: ~8 (one per placeholder + one for
the `bund:` prefix + Bund-error fallback + the
async-state-machine state transitions).

### 3.3 P4-pre — Cross-thread `Store` sharing

Prerequisite for P4 (DB-side health checks) and
for I.4's future hook flow.  Today `Store` is
held by App; the health monitor runs in a
separate tokio task and can't borrow `&Store`.

Options surveyed in §7 of the 1.2.15 proposal:

* `Arc<RwLock<Store>>` — simple, the standard
  pattern.  Reads share, writes exclude.
* IoC channel — TUI asks for check, monitor
  task accumulates pending requests.  More
  ceremony, no real benefit for the
  single-user case.

Going with `Arc<RwLock<Store>>`.  Adds one
field to `App`; monitor task takes an
`Arc<RwLock<Store>>` clone at spawn time.
Tests pin the parity of reads under contention.

Test budget: ~3 (clone semantics, concurrent
read parity, no deadlock under nested-lock
scenarios).

### 3.4 P4 — DB-side health checks

Five real checks landing on top of the H.1-H.3
scaffold.  Each runs at its own cadence, emits
the same `HealthEvent` enum, logs to
`.inkhaven/health.log` like the existing checks.

| Check | Cadence | Auto-repair? |
|-|-|-|
| DuckDB `PRAGMA integrity_check` | 15 min | No — Critical, surface to user |
| HNSW vector parity vs. DB row count | 15 min | Yes — re-embed missing rows |
| Open paragraph textarea vs. on-disk file | 30 sec | Yes via `editor.autosave_resolution_policy` |
| Tree parent-pointer integrity | 30 sec | Yes — re-link by slug |
| Disk free % (< 10 % → Critical) | 5 min | No |

Note: HNSW + textarea + tree checks need access
to the project Store via the P4-pre sharing
work.  Disk free uses a no-deps approach
(walking the filesystem statvfs equivalent via
`std::fs` — available on stable Rust without
sysinfo).

Test budget: ~12 (each check's clean / dirty
case + the auto-repair where applicable).

### 3.5 P1 — Backup + disk safety rails

Two pieces:

* **Disk-space pre-flight** before save /
  assemble / backup operations.  Refuse to
  start under critical-low conditions (< 50 MB
  free + the operation needs > free); fall
  through gracefully with a status message
  instead of trapping a write error half-way.
* **Amber backup-freshness chip** — pair with
  the 1.2.15 health monitor's hard-warn check.
  Show a status-bar chip when the newest
  backup crosses 50 % of `backup.max_age`
  (configurable as `backup.amber_threshold:
  0.5` default).  Gives the user visibility
  BEFORE the hard warning fires.

(Git portion explicitly dropped: out of scope
for 1.2.16 per the user's direction.)

Test budget: ~4 (pre-flight refusal, pre-flight
allow, amber-threshold detection, chip render).

## 4. Theme I.4 — Bund stdlib expansion

Three new categories, gated by the existing
default-deny policy + 1.2.15 trust gate.

### 4.1 `ink.review.*` (REVIEW_WRITE)

* `ink.review.add_comment` — programmatic
  comment creation; takes paragraph UUID +
  start_char + end_char + body + category.
* `ink.review.resolve` — close a comment by ID.
* `ink.review.list` — return every comment in

Category default-deny.  Enables: prepare a

manuscript and inserts structural-feedback
comments en masse.

### 4.2 `ink.thread.*` (STORE_WRITE — existing category)

* `ink.thread.add_waypoint` — append a

* `ink.thread.link_paragraph` — link a waypoint
  to a manuscript paragraph.
* `ink.thread.list` — return every thread as a

Existing STORE_WRITE category — already
default-deny — so no new policy needed.

### 4.3 `ink.workflow.*` (no new category)

* `ink.workflow.chain` — sequence of
  `(prompt, scope_chord, apply_action)` tuples
  applied in order.  Each step waits for the
  previous AI inference to complete (`ink.ai.
  poll`) before firing the next.  Lets a power
  user encode "for every paragraph in chapter
  3, run grammar-check + apply" as a script.

Pure orchestration over existing `ink.ai.*` —
no new permissions.

Test budget: ~8 (one per word + one workflow-

## 6. Theme A.6 — Plot mining

Extends the 1.2.14 threads doctor with broader
deterministic narrative-audit checks.

### 6.1 Detectors

* **Dropped character** — a character mentioned
  in the first 30 % of the manuscript who
  doesn't appear again.  Walks the Characters
  lexicon + paragraph mentions; flags
  characters whose last-mention chapter index
  is below `total_chapters * 0.7`.
* **Unresolved tension** — paragraphs ending in
  question marks / opener clauses ("she
  realised...") that don't have a follow-up
  resolution-style paragraph within N chapters.
  Heuristic — false positives expected; the
  finding's confidence is exposed in the doctor
  output.
* **Pacing collapse** — chapter-word-count CV
  spike (one chapter 3+ stdev from the trailing
  mean).  Could be intentional (an epilogue);
  flagged as Info, not Warning.
* **Stalled thread** — already in the 1.2.14
  thread doctor; surfaced here too for unified
  reading.

### 6.2 Integration

These slot into `inkhaven doctor --scan` as new
classes (kebab-case slugs `dropped-character`,
`unresolved-tension`, etc.).  Severity defaults
to Info (this is structural feedback, not data
loss).  No autofix — these are author-judgment
findings.

### 6.3 The TUI surface

The `Ctrl+B Shift+0` doctor panel inherits the
new classes automatically (they're just more
findings).  An additional "narrative" filter
button (`n` inside the panel) shows only
narrative-audit findings.

Test budget: ~10 (each detector's positive +
negative case + the doctor-panel filter).

## 7. Theme A.5 — Worldbuilding consistency pack

One genre-adjacent specialisation.  Mystery
(A5.1) and historical-fiction (A5.3) packs
deferred to 1.2.17.

### 7.1 Cross-system consistency scan

Walks Characters, Places, Artefacts, Language
entries looking for contradictions in their
metadata + their mentions in prose.

* **Numeric contradictions** — a Character with
  `age: 23` mentioned as "twenty-six" in a
  paragraph; a Place with `population: 5000`
  described as "the largest city, half a
  million souls".  Detected via simple
  number-extraction + comparison.
* **Spatial contradictions** — a Place with
  `north_of: "the river"` described as "south
  of the river" elsewhere.  Walks adjective
  declarations in metadata vs. prose-extracted
  prepositional phrases.
* **Naming inconsistency** — a Character named
  "Aerin Stormbringer" referenced as "Aerin
  Stormbreaker" once.  Edit distance > 0,

### 7.2 Anachronism overlay (deferred from A5.3 historical pack)

## 10. Risks + open questions

* **A.2's "AI critique summary" section is just
  the last AI history entry's first ~100
  chars.**  If history is empty or stale, this
  cell shows "(no recent critique)".  Not
  worth doing anything cleverer for the first
  cut.

* **P6's async snippet state machine adds a
  modal-state transition we haven't had
  before.**  The existing snippet pipeline is
  fully synchronous.  Need to be careful that
  expanding a snippet, popping a picker,
  cancelling the picker, and re-typing don't
  leave the editor in a half-substituted
  state.  Regression test: pop picker → Esc →
  the trigger text remains in the buffer
  (no half-expansion).

* **A.6's "unresolved tension" detector is a
  heuristic.**  Will surface false positives.
  Severity = Info, not Warning, so it doesn't
  trip CI gates; confidence value exposed in
  the doctor output so users can filter.

* **A.5's numeric-contradiction detector
  requires reasonable number extraction from
  prose** ("twenty-six", "5,000", "half a
  million").  We have a number-words crate in
  the transitive tree?  If not, add `numerics`
  or implement a small extractor (English-only
  for now; document the limitation).

* **I.4's `ink.workflow.chain` is the first
  Bund word that does async orchestration.**
  Today the VM is fully sync.  Either we wrap
  the inference call in a `block_on` (risk:
  pause the UI for the duration; acceptable for
  scripted workflows since the user explicitly
  invoked them) or we add a yield mechanism
  (bigger change).  Start with `block_on`;
  document the foreground-blocking behaviour.

* **I.1's lazy tree row materialisation
  interacts with the visited-history +
  bookmark + paragraph-cursor caches.**  Each
  is keyed by UUID, so as long as we never
  return a row whose UUID isn't in the
  hierarchy, those should be safe.  Add a
  property test.

* **Git integration.**  Out of scope per the

## 12. Recommendation

Ship in this order:

1. **T** first — small docs commit; corrects
   the released 1.2.15 documentation.
2. **P5 + P6** next — clean carryovers, ship
   fast.
3. **P4-pre then P4** — `Arc<RwLock<Store>>`
   unlocks the deferred health checks.
4. **P1** — small safety rails, no
   dependencies.
5. **I.4** — opens the scriptable surface for
   power users.
6. **A.2** — the headline; benefits from I.4
   for the `ink.workflow.*` orchestration that
   the dashboard's "export to markdown" can use.
7. **A.6** — narrative audit detectors on top
   of the doctor scan.
8. **A.5** — one worldbuilding-consistency

9. **I.1** — performance pass at the end.

Mid-cycle cut points: if scope runs long, defer
**A.5** (one pack to 1.2.17 is reasonable) or
**A.6's "unresolved tension" detector** (the
heuristic is the part most likely to need
iteration after real-world testing).

The cycle's exit criteria:

* Manuscript intelligence dashboard renders in
  < 200 ms for a 1000-paragraph project.
* Every doctor scan class (including the new
  A.6 + A.5 detectors) ships with an `--autofix`
  path or an explicit "no autofix —
  author-judgment finding" note.
* All five DB-side health checks land + pass
  their regression tests under concurrent
  Store access.
* P4-pre's `Arc<RwLock<Store>>` introduces zero
  deadlocks under the property-test fuzz.
* Performance pass produces a measurable
  improvement on at least three of the five
  benchmark scenarios.

When all five hold, we cut 1.2.16.

# Inkhaven 1.2.17 — TTS Piper transition

**Status:** active scope (locked 2026-06-01)
**Cycle theme:** turn TTS from a macOS-only paper-cut into a
first-class cross-platform feature with auto-downloaded voices.

## Motivation

The 1.2.9 TTS surface (`Ctrl+B S` read-aloud, `Ctrl+B Shift+R`
save-as-audio, `ink.tts.speak` Bund word) is wired through
`/usr/bin/say` on macOS only.  Linux and Windows users
who try the chord get a friendly "TTS unavailable on this
platform" message.  Voice selection is whatever the OS has
already downloaded; no programmatic discovery, no project-
scoped consistency.

Piper ([rhasspy/piper](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper))
gives us a single neural TTS that runs the same on
Linux / macOS / Windows, with high-quality voice models
distributed via Hugging Face under permissive licenses.
The voice models are 25–100 MB ONNX files plus a small JSON
descriptor; both are deterministic on-disk artefacts that fit
inkhaven's project-as-files philosophy.

The 1.2.17 scope is narrow on purpose: one feature, done
properly, with cross-platform parity as a non-negotiable.

## Locked design decisions

These were resolved through brainstorming + question-and-
answer on 2026-06-01.  They constrain the rest of the plan;
re-opening them would require updating every phase below.

1. **`tts.engine` defaults to `"auto"`.**  Inkhaven detects
   the Piper binary at startup and prefers it; falls back to
   the 1.2.9 `system` backend if Piper is unresolvable.  A
   status-bar diagnostic chip surfaces the active engine so
   users can confirm without leaving the TUI.
2. **Piper binary lives at `~/.cache/inkhaven/piper-<plat>/piper`.**
   User-scoped cache (the binary is identical across every
   project, ~4–8 MB).  HJSON override via `tts.binary_path`.
3. **Voices live at `<project>/.inkhaven/voices/`.**  Per-
   project scope so a French-novel project's voices don't
   pollute a Russian project.  Cache size capped by
   `tts.cache_max_voices` (default 5) with LRU eviction.
4. **Voice picker modal binds `Ctrl+B Shift+V`.**  Matches
   the B-pane `Shift+letter` family (F filter words,
   G heatmap, H rhythm).  V was unused.
5. **`.gitignore` is auto-appended.**  On first voice
   download, inkhaven appends `.inkhaven/voices/` to
   `<project>/.gitignore` (creating it if absent).  Voices
   are large opaque blobs; checking them into git is
   universally wrong.  One-time, idempotent, atomic via
   `crate::io_atomic`.

## Architecture

### Engine abstraction

Today `App.tts_say: Say` is a struct holding a `say`-
subprocess handle.  Replace with:

```rust
pub enum TtsEngine {
    System(Say),         // 1.2.9 macOS-only backend, preserved
    Piper(PiperEngine),  // 1.2.17 cross-platform backend
    Disabled,            // master switch off OR no engine resolvable
}

impl TtsEngine {
    pub fn speak(&mut self, text: &str, voice: &str, wpm: Option<u16>) -> Result<()>;
    pub fn speak_to_file(&mut self, text: &str, voice: &str, path: &Path, wpm: Option<u16>) -> Result<()>;
    pub fn is_speaking(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn stop(&mut self);
    pub fn label(&self) -> &'static str;  // for the diagnostic chip
}
```

Existing call sites (`tts_speak_string`, `tts_speak_greeting`,
`tts_speak_goodbye_blocking`, `commit_tts_save_as_audio`,
`ink_tts_speak` Bund word) dispatch through the enum and stay
unchanged in shape.

### `tts.engine` resolution

```rust
fn resolve_engine(cfg: &TtsConfig, project_root: &Path) -> TtsEngine {
    if !cfg.enabled {
        return TtsEngine::Disabled;
    }
    match cfg.engine.as_str() {
        "system" => TtsEngine::System(Say::new()),
        "piper"  => PiperEngine::new(cfg, project_root).into_engine(),
        "auto"   => {
            // Try Piper first; fall back to System.
            if let Ok(piper) = PiperEngine::new(cfg, project_root) {
                TtsEngine::Piper(piper)
            } else if Say::available().is_ok() {
                TtsEngine::System(Say::new())
            } else {
                TtsEngine::Disabled
            }
        }
        other => {
            log::warn!("unknown tts.engine {other:?}; treating as auto");
            // ... same as "auto"
        }
    }
}
```

### HJSON shape (additive)

```hjson
{
  editor: {
    tts: {
      // 1.2.9+ (preserved)
      enabled: false
      voice: "en_US-lessac-medium"   // default flips with engine
      speed: 1.0
      greeting: ""
      goodbye: ""

      // 1.2.17+ (new)
      engine: "auto"                 // "auto" | "piper" | "system"
      voices_dir: ".inkhaven/voices" // relative to project root
      auto_download: true
      catalog_url: "https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/raw/main/voices.json"
      catalog_ttl_hours: 24
      binary_path: null              // null = autoresolve
      auto_download_binary: true
      cache_max_voices: 5
      play_command: null             // null = platform default
      sample_rate_hz: 22050
    }
  }
}
```

Default `voice` flips from `"Milena"` (1.2.9 default — a
macOS `say` voice) to `"en_US-lessac-medium"` (the Piper
catalog's canonical demo voice).  Existing 1.2.9 users who
have `tts.voice: "Milena"` and `tts.engine: "auto"` get the
existing macOS backend (since Piper has no "Milena"); the
T.8 migration prompts them to pick a Piper voice if they
want cross-platform parity.

### On-disk layout

```
<project>/
  .inkhaven/
    voices/
      voices.json                       # catalog cache, 24h TTL
      en_US-lessac-medium.onnx
      en_US-lessac-medium.onnx.json
      ru_RU-irina-medium.onnx
      ru_RU-irina-medium.onnx.json
      .lru                              # access-time index for eviction

~/.cache/inkhaven/
  piper-darwin-arm64/piper              # auto-downloaded binary
  piper-linux-x86_64/piper
  piper-windows-x86_64/piper.exe
```

### Playback dispatch

| Platform | Default `tts.play_command` |
|----------|----------------------------|
| macOS    | `afplay <path>`            |
| Linux    | `paplay <path>` (PulseAudio); fall back to `aplay <path>` (ALSA) |
| Windows  | `powershell -c "(New-Object Media.SoundPlayer '<path>').PlaySync()"` |

User override via `tts.play_command` if needed (mpv / ffplay
/ sox).  No new Rust audio dependency.

### Background work + safety invariants

* Downloads run in tokio tasks (1.2.15 health-monitor
  pattern).  Status-bar progress chip: `[tts: <voice> 73%]`
  using `ChipState::Info` from 1.2.16 P.1.
* SHA256 verification against the catalog manifest before
  the downloaded blob is moved into place.
* Atomic writes via `crate::io_atomic` for every voice
  artefact (.onnx, .onnx.json, voices.json, .lru, the
  binary).
* Path safety via `crate::path_safety::resolve_within` on
  every voice name (defensive against catalog poisoning +
  crafted voice names containing `..`).
* Lock-poisoning recovery on the catalog cache + LRU
  mutex.
* `tokio::process::Command` for Piper subprocess so the
  TUI loop isn't blocked.
* Hard timeout on synthesis (30 s default) so a misbehaving
  Piper invocation doesn't stall the TUI.

## Phase plan

Eight phases, each commit-shipped after green tests.  Phases
sized for one commit each; if a phase grows past ~400 lines
it splits.

### T.1 — Engine abstraction

Replace `App.tts_say: Say` with `App.tts: TtsEngine`.
Dispatch through the enum from all three speak paths +
save-as-audio + the Bund word.  `Piper` variant is a stub
that errors with "Piper backend not yet implemented in
T.1".  Add HJSON fields (with defaults) so the config
shape lands ahead of the implementation that uses them.

* `src/tui/say.rs` → keep, used by `System` variant.
* `src/tui/piper.rs` → new, stub `PiperEngine`.
* `src/tui/tts.rs` → new, `TtsEngine` enum + dispatch.
* `src/config.rs` → extend `TtsConfig`.
* `assert_send_sync<TtsEngine>()` invariant (1.2.16 P.4-pre
  pattern).

**Test budget:** 6–8 unit tests on dispatch + resolution.
No behavioural change vs. 1.2.16 expected on macOS.

### T.2 — Piper binary resolution + auto-download

`resolve_piper_binary(cfg, os, arch) -> Result<PathBuf>`:

1. If `cfg.binary_path` is set + the file is executable,
   use it.
2. Search `PATH` for `piper`.
3. Check `~/.cache/inkhaven/piper-<plat>/piper` for a
   previously-downloaded binary.
4. If `cfg.auto_download_binary`, fetch the latest GitHub
   release matching `(os, arch)`, extract, verify the
   SHA256 from the release notes, install atomically.
5. Else return `BinaryUnresolvable`.

Pure classifier `pick_piper_release_asset(release_json, os,
arch)` extracts the right tarball name for the platform.

* `src/tui/piper/binary.rs` → resolution logic.
* `src/tui/piper/download.rs` → `ureq` download +
  extraction (already in tree for typst).

**Test budget:** 10–12 tests; mock `ureq` for download
flows; real-filesystem tests for resolve order.

### T.3 — Voice catalog fetch + parse + cache

`Catalog::load(voices_dir, catalog_url, ttl) -> Result<Catalog>`:

1. If `voices_dir/voices.json` exists and is younger than
   `ttl`, parse + return.
2. Otherwise fetch from `catalog_url`, write atomically,
   parse + return.
3. On network failure with a cached copy present, return
   the stale copy + log a warning.  No-network must not
   block synthesis when the voice itself is already on
   disk.

Pure parsers `parse_voice_catalog(json) -> Catalog`,
`catalog_voice(catalog, name) -> Option<VoiceMeta>`,
`voice_languages(catalog) -> Vec<String>`.

**Test budget:** 8–10 tests on parse + TTL + stale-fallback.

### T.4 — Voice auto-download

`ensure_voice_downloaded(name, voices_dir, catalog, on_progress) -> Result<PathBuf>`:

1. If both `.onnx` and `.onnx.json` exist + checksums
   match, return.
2. Else stream-download both from the catalog's URLs.
3. Verify SHA256 against the catalog manifest.
4. Atomic-move into place via `io_atomic`.
5. Update `.lru` index.  Run LRU eviction if over
   `cache_max_voices`.
6. On first-ever download, append `.inkhaven/voices/` to
   `<project>/.gitignore` (idempotent).

Progress callback drives the status-bar chip.

* `src/tui/piper/voice.rs` → download + verification.
* `src/tui/piper/lru.rs` → access-time index +
  eviction policy.
* `src/tui/piper/gitignore.rs` → idempotent append.

**Test budget:** 14–16 tests; mock-HTTP for download
flows; property-test path-traversal defence on voice
names.

### T.5 — Piper synthesis + playback

`PiperEngine::speak(text, voice, wpm) -> Result<()>`:

1. Resolve binary (T.2).
2. Ensure voice downloaded (T.4).
3. Spawn piper, pipe text on stdin, capture WAV stdout
   to a temp file under `voices_dir/.synthesis-<uuid>.wav`.
4. Dispatch playback via `tts.play_command` or platform
   default.
5. Return immediately (background plays); next `speak`
   stops the current playback first.

`PiperEngine::speak_to_file(text, voice, path, wpm)`:

* As above but writes the WAV directly to `path` (or
  encodes via ffmpeg if `path` ends in `.mp3` / `.m4a`).
  Existing `commit_tts_save_as_audio` already invokes
  ffmpeg via subprocess; we reuse.

`is_speaking()` / `stop()` track the playback subprocess
PID.

**Test budget:** 8–10 tests; gated by `[ignore]` when
Piper binary isn't on the test runner, with one always-on
test for the WAV-temp-file path-safety check.

### T.6 — Voice picker modal (`Ctrl+B Shift+V`)

`Modal::TtsVoicePicker { catalog, downloaded, selected,
filter, scroll, status }`:

* Lists every voice in the catalog: `<name>  <language>
  <quality>  [downloaded ✓ | available ⬇]`.
* `/<text>` filters by language code or name substring.
* Enter on undownloaded voice → background download with
  progress chip; on downloaded voice → set `tts.voice` +
  persist HJSON.
* `d` on a downloaded voice → remove + update LRU.
* `Esc` closes.

* `src/tui/app/render/modals.rs` → `draw_tts_voice_picker`.
* `src/tui/app.rs` → `App::open_tts_voice_picker` +
  `handle_tts_voice_picker_key`.
* `src/tui/keybind.rs` → `Action::OpenTtsVoicePicker`
  rebindable as `tts.voice_picker`, default chord
  `Ctrl+B Shift+V`.

**Test budget:** 10–12 tests on filter + select + LRU
interaction.

### T.7 — `inkhaven tts` CLI surface

Subcommands:

```
inkhaven tts engine status            # which engine is active + why
inkhaven tts binary status            # piper binary path + checksum
inkhaven tts binary download          # explicit download (else implicit on first speak)
inkhaven tts voice list               # downloaded + available
inkhaven tts voice download <name>    # explicit download
inkhaven tts voice remove <name>      # delete + update LRU
inkhaven tts voice catalog refresh    # bypass TTL
inkhaven tts test "<phrase>" [--voice <name>]   # synth + play
```

Extends the 1.2.9 `inkhaven doctor --tts-test` so it
works against Piper, reporting binary location + voice
path + checksum.

* `src/cli/tts.rs` → new module.
* `src/cli/mod.rs` → wire `TtsCommand`.

**Test budget:** 12–14 tests on subcommand routing +
output shape.

### T.8 — Migration + docs + tutorial 56

* `inkhaven config` (the schema-aware HJSON editor)
  surfaces a one-time prompt when a project has
  `tts.voice: "Milena"` (or any other 1.2.9 default) AND
  `tts.engine: "auto"`: "Piper has no `Milena`.  Pick
  `en_US-lessac-medium` (en) / `ru_RU-irina-medium` (ru)
  / ...".  User can dismiss; we don't auto-overwrite.
* Tutorial 56 — `Documentation/Tutorials/56-tts-piper.md`.
* `Documentation/CONFIGURATION.md` § "1.2.17 — new HJSON
  blocks" with the full `tts.*` reference.
* `Documentation/KEYBINDING.md` row for `Shift+V`.
* `Documentation/KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md` § "1.2.17 — new
  actions".
* `Documentation/RELEASE_NOTES/1.2.17.md` implementation
  log + closing.
* `README.md` "Latest release" section flipped to 1.2.17.

**Test budget:** light — most are docs.  Migration logic
gets 4–6 tests.

## Test budget total

Roughly 80–100 new tests across the eight phases.  The
1.2.16 cycle landed at 758 passing; 1.2.17 should land
around 840–860.

## Risk register

* **Hugging Face availability.**  The catalog and voice
  URLs are external.  Stale-copy fallback (T.3) handles
  network outages; the catalog itself going away would
  require a config knob `tts.catalog_url` swap to a
  community mirror.  Already configurable.
* **Piper releases change tarball naming.**  Pin the
  expected asset-name pattern in
  `pick_piper_release_asset` so a release-naming change
  fails loudly with a clear error rather than silently
  picking the wrong asset.  Test the patterns we
  currently know about.
* **Voice model size on slow connections.**  25–100 MB
  per voice can be painful on metered or slow links.
  The status-bar chip + cancellable downloads (via the
  picker modal's `Esc` while downloading) limit the
  user-impact.  Documented.
* **Project-dir voice cache grows large.**  Mitigated by
  `cache_max_voices: 5` LRU + the doctor `--scan` could
  flag voices that have outgrown LRU (deferred to T.8.b
  if any user reports it).
* **`.gitignore` auto-append surprise.**  Some users
  view `.gitignore` as sacrosanct.  Document the
  behaviour in Tutorial 56 + add `tts.auto_gitignore:
  true` HJSON knob to opt out.
* **Playback command not available on minimal Linux.**
  No `paplay` / `aplay` on truly minimal systems.  Fall-
  through gives a clear "no playback backend found —
  set `tts.play_command` manually" error.

## Out of scope for 1.2.17

These pair with TTS but don't fit the cycle:

* **Audiobook draft (.m4b chapter slicing)** — would need
  ffmpeg pipeline work + a "speak whole book" UX.
  Candidate for 1.2.18.
* **Per-character voice mapping** — assign a Piper voice
  per Characters book entry so dialogue auto-routes to
  that voice on `Ctrl+B S`.  Big UX surface; needs design.
* **Voice cloning / fine-tuning** — Piper supports it but
  the workflow is out-of-scope for an editor.

## Deferred to 1.2.17.b or 1.2.18

Carryovers from 1.2.16 stay where they are in
`Documentation/RELEASE_NOTES/1.2.17.md`; they may slip
again if the TTS scope absorbs the full cycle:

* I.1 — Performance pass.
* A.2.b dashboard sections (POV chip, rhythm gauge,
  filter-words flagged today, recent AI critique).
* A.6.b unresolved-tension detector.
* A.5.b worldbuilding pack additions.
* I.4.b/c Bund stdlib follow-ups.
* M1/M3 security hygiene.
* Language UX polish.
* Genre packs (mystery + historical).

The honest reality: TTS Piper is a substantial cycle on
its own, especially with the cross-platform constraint.
If it ships clean, that's a release.  Pulling more in
trades stability for surface.

## Closing

Single-feature 1.2.17 cycle.  Eight phases, ~80–100 tests,
zero new Rust deps (`ureq` already in tree; playback via
system commands).  Cross-platform parity is the
non-negotiable acceptance criterion: every chord that
works on macOS must work identically on Linux and
Windows.

# Inkhaven 1.2.18 — Performance pass + reader-experience

**Status:** active scope (locked 2026-06-01)
**Cycle theme:** turn the 1.2.17 TTS Piper transition
into something a reader can actually consume, after
first making sure the editor stays fast at 10K
paragraphs.

## Motivation

1.2.15–1.2.17 each shipped substantial user surfaces
(stability, intelligence dashboard, TTS Piper).  The
codebase has grown without a baseline perf measurement
since the early 1.2.x cycles; the I.1 performance pass
was deferred from 1.2.16 and 1.2.17 to keep those
cycles release-ready.

1.2.18 closes that debt first, then layers a
reader-experience headline on top: ePub export +
audiobook draft (.m4b) + reading-time chip + reader-
pace preview.  Reader-experience features hit every
paragraph in a project, so they benefit directly from
I.1's hotspot fixes — the perf work pays for itself
in the same release.

## Locked design decisions

These were resolved through brainstorming + question-
and-answer on 2026-06-01.  They constrain the rest of
the plan.

1. **Benchmarks live under `benches/` with criterion.**
   Standard Rust bench framework; auto-handles warmup
   + statistical analysis + regression reporting.
   Adds `criterion` as a dev-dep (acceptable cost for
   the gates).
2. **CI regression threshold = 20%.**  Generous enough
   that timing noise doesn't trip on every PR; tight
   enough that real regressions surface.  GitHub
   Actions runs the bench suite on PRs and posts
   per-scenario deltas in a comment.
3. **The 10K-paragraph fixture is generator-only.**  A
   `tools/gen-fixture` binary produces ~50 MB of
   synthetic project data under any chosen path.  The
   fixture is NOT committed to the repo (~50 MB
   bloat); CI regenerates it before each bench run
   (~30s overhead).
4. **Cycle scope: I.1 + reader-experience.**  I.1 first
   (fixture + baseline + analysis + 3–4 hotspot fixes
   + CI gates), then the reader-experience phases.  T.6.b
   background voice downloads + T.4.b MD5 verification
   absorbed as side deliveries during the reader-
   experience work (audiobook draft needs non-blocking
   synth anyway).

## Architecture

### Bench harness (criterion-based)

```
benches/
  startup.rs          # cold + warm startup → first-frame
  tree_scroll.rs      # 1000-row Page Down on the 10K fixture
  search.rs           # one semantic + one lexical query
  ai_envelope.rs      # RAG retrieval + prompt build (no LLM call)
  paragraph_save.rs   # save round-trip including io_atomic + embeddings
```

Each bench depends on a pre-generated fixture pointed
at via `INKHAVEN_BENCH_FIXTURE=<path>` env var.  A small
helper (`benches/common.rs`) handles setup +
fixture discovery.

```bash
# CI flow
$ cargo run --release --bin gen-fixture -- /tmp/inkhaven-bench-fixture
$ INKHAVEN_BENCH_FIXTURE=/tmp/inkhaven-bench-fixture \
    cargo bench --bench startup --bench tree_scroll \
                --bench search --bench ai_envelope --bench paragraph_save
$ tools/bench-report.rs --baseline main --threshold 0.20
```

### Fixture generator

`tools/gen-fixture/main.rs` produces:

* 5 user books × 20 chapters × 100 paragraphs = **10K
  paragraphs**.  Per-paragraph word counts sampled from
  a realistic distribution (~mean 450, stdev 150).
* 3 system books: Characters (80 entries), Places (30
  entries), Threads (12 threads with 3–8 waypoints
  each).
* 200 inline comments distributed across paragraphs
  (~2% comment-density, matching real projects).
* Tags assigned at 15% coverage (mostly chapter-level).
* Prose: markov-chain output from a public-domain seed
  corpus (Pride and Prejudice + War of the Peace),
  capped per paragraph to the sampled word count.  Not
  semantically meaningful but vocabulary-realistic
  enough to exercise tokenisation + stemming +
  embeddings.

Output: a fully-formed inkhaven project that opens with
the standard CLI.  Metadata.db + blobs.db + vectors
seeded; embeddings generated by the standard flow (the
bench setup phase, run once, can be slow — the fixture
is reusable across many bench runs).

### CI integration

`.github/workflows/bench.yml` triggered on every PR + on
push to main.  Runs:

1. `gen-fixture` (if not cached).
2. `cargo bench` for each scenario.
3. `bench-report` compares against the latest main
   baseline (stored as a workflow artefact on main).
4. Post-comment on the PR with per-scenario percent
   deltas + a ✓/✗ verdict per scenario.
5. Exit non-zero if any scenario regressed >20%.

## Phase plan

Phases sized so each ships a commit with concrete
artefacts.  Total: ~10 phases (I.1.1–I.1.last + R.1–R.4
+ side items).

### I.1.1 — Fixture generator

* `tools/gen-fixture/main.rs` (new bin).
* Public-domain seed corpus bundled in `tools/gen-fixture/seed/`.
* Tests on the size + shape distribution + idempotence
  (re-running on an existing dir cleans + regenerates).
* CLI: `cargo run --release --bin gen-fixture -- <path>`.

Test budget: 6–8 tests covering shape + counts +
deterministic randomness (seed-based RNG so CI runs are
reproducible).

### I.1.2 — Baseline harness (criterion)

* `Cargo.toml` adds `criterion` as a dev-dep.
* `benches/common.rs` — shared setup, fixture
  discovery via env var.
* `benches/startup.rs` — cold + warm startup time
  (project load → first interactive frame).
* `benches/tree_scroll.rs` — 1000-iteration Page Down
  on the tree pane (no rendering; just state mutations
  + the row materialisation logic).
* `benches/search.rs` — one semantic + one lexical
  query.
* `benches/ai_envelope.rs` — RAG retrieval + prompt
  build (mocked LLM client to skip the network call).
* `benches/paragraph_save.rs` — full save round-trip.
* Documentation in `benches/README.md` covering how to
  run + interpret + add new benches.

Test budget: minimal (criterion handles its own
machinery); 4–6 sanity tests on the common helper.

### I.1.3 — Flamegraph analysis + PERF.md

No code commit per se — investigation phase.  Run
`cargo flamegraph --release` against each scenario,
identify the top-N hotspots, write up findings as
`Documentation/PROPOSALS/PERF.md`:

* Per-scenario flamegraph SVG (committed under
  `Documentation/PROPOSALS/perf-flamegraphs/`).
* Per-hotspot section: function, % of CPU time,
  hypothesis for fix, expected delta.
* Prioritised list driving I.1.4 onward.

### I.1.4 — Lazy tree-row materialisation

Hypothesis: `Hierarchy::load` builds every Row at
startup; for 10K paragraphs that's the obvious blocker
on cold-startup time.  Switch to lazy on-demand
materialisation — only build rows for the currently-
visible viewport + a small lookahead.

Carry: cold-startup bench drops; tree-scroll bench
shouldn't regress.

### I.1.5 — Background embedding refresh

Hypothesis: save-path embedding regeneration blocks the
main thread.  Lift to a tokio worker + an internal
queue; save path returns immediately, embeddings
backfill async.

Carry: paragraph-save bench drops; search bench
shouldn't regress beyond the delay tolerance (a freshly-
saved paragraph might not appear in semantic results for
~500ms).

### I.1.6 — DuckDB write batching

Hypothesis: per-save DuckDB INSERTs vs. batched
transactions.  Defer DuckDB commits with a coalescing
window.

Carry: paragraph-save bench drops; cold-startup might
slightly increase (the load path reads outstanding
batched writes); acceptable tradeoff documented.

### I.1.7 — CI benchmark gates

* `.github/workflows/bench.yml` runs the harness on
  every PR + push-to-main.
* `tools/bench-report.rs` parses criterion JSON output,
  compares against the main baseline, posts a PR
  comment.
* Threshold: 20% regression on any scenario fails the
  build.  Per-scenario deltas always reported regardless
  of pass/fail.

### R.1 — ePub export

`inkhaven assemble --epub <book-slug>` builds a
standards-compliant ePub from the project's typst
output.  Cover image + chapter metadata + nav.xhtml +
content.opf assembled following the standard.

Subprocess `pandoc` for the typst → HTML step (already a
common dep for technical writers; document as a
soft-required external if absent).

### R.2 — Audiobook draft (.m4b)

`inkhaven assemble --audiobook <book-slug>`:

1. Loops chapter ordinals, calling
   `tts::engine.speak_to_file_blocking` per paragraph
   into a per-chapter wav.
2. Concatenates per-chapter wavs via ffmpeg.
3. Wraps as m4b with chapter metadata.

Subprocess `ffmpeg` (assume present; document required
version).

T.6.b background voice downloads absorbed here: the
assemble step downloads any missing voices via the same
tokio infrastructure, with a progress chip the
assemble-stdout reports on.

### R.3 — Reading-time chip

* `editor.reading_time_chip: true` HJSON toggle (default
  on if `editor.tts.enabled`).
* Status-bar chip showing total + remaining read time
  at the configured wpm (default 200wpm).
* Doctor scan class `paragraph-too-long` (read time >
  5min) optional.

### R.4 — Reader-pace preview

`Ctrl+B Shift+E` opens a reader-pace preview modal.
Slow-scrolls the open paragraph + adjacent ones at the
configured wpm.  Useful for catching pacing problems
that aren't visible at editor-typing speed.

### Side deliveries

These ride alongside the R.* phases without their own
phase numbers:

* **T.4.b MD5 verification** — when voices are
  downloaded as part of the audiobook assemble, verify
  the MD5 from the catalog.  Subprocess `md5sum` /
  `md5 -q` / `certutil` per platform.
* **T.6.b background voice downloads** — see R.2.

## Test budget total

Roughly 60–80 new tests across the cycle.  The 1.2.17
cycle landed at 955 passing; 1.2.18 should land around
1015–1035.

## Risk register

* **Bench flakiness.**  Timing measurements vary with
  CPU + disk load.  Mitigate: criterion's statistical
  analysis + 20% threshold + averaging over 100
  iterations per scenario.
* **Fixture realism.**  Synthetic prose may not match
  real performance characteristics.  Mitigate: per-
  paragraph word-count distribution sampled from a
  real corpus; comment + tag + thread density tuned
  to real projects' averages.
* **ePub compatibility.**  ePub readers vary in
  strictness.  Mitigate: validate output with
  `epubcheck` in CI; document the readers we tested.
* **m4b assembly cost.**  10K paragraphs × ~3s
  synthesis = ~8 hours.  Mitigate: parallel synthesis
  (limited by CPU); document expected wall-clock time.
* **Background-download cancellation.**  Tokio task
  cancellation needs care to avoid orphan curl
  processes.  Mitigate: explicit `kill_on_drop`
  on the curl child handle.

## Out of scope for 1.2.18

* **Multi-paragraph AI envelope** — tempting but
  belongs in an AI-maturity cycle (1.2.19?).
* **Character voice consistency pass** — same.
* **AI streaming into editor** — needs undo-semantics
  design; defer.
* **Hot-reload prompts.hjson** — small enough to slip
  in if time permits but not committed scope.

## Closing

I.1 first.  Reader experience second.  Side
deliveries for the TTS Piper carryovers.

Honest about the bench-flakiness risk + the m4b
wall-clock cost.  Goal: every metric in the 5-scenario
suite is either flat or down by end of cycle; ePub +
audiobook ship as user-facing headlines that make the
project something a reader (not just a writer) can
consume.

# Inkhaven 1.2.19 — Revision & continuity (multilingual)

**Status:** active scope (locked 2026-06-03)
**Cycle theme:** the draft-3-to-final grind — catch the
continuity errors, echoes, and contradictions that breed
during revision, in every language inkhaven supports.

## Motivation

Inkhaven is already rich on first-draft craft: the
manuscript intelligence dashboard, narrative-audit doctor
scans (dropped-character, pacing-collapse, stalled-thread,
naming-inconsistency), the Threads book, inline comments,
style-warning overlays, AI critique.

What it doesn't yet help with is **revision** — where
serious authors spend most of their time.  By draft 3,
continuity errors breed: a character's eye colour drifts,
a timeline contradicts itself, a vivid metaphor gets
reused eight pages later, a tension is set up and never
paid off.  Inkhaven has the right bones for this (the
Characters book, the doctor-scan infrastructure, the AI
envelope, the multilingual NLP stack) but only scratches
the surface today.

1.2.19 builds the revision layer — and builds it
**multilingual from the start**, because inkhaven's users
write in English, Russian, French, German, Spanish, and
invented languages, and a continuity checker that only
works in English would be useless to half of them.

## Locked design decisions

Resolved through brainstorming + the multilingual design
pass on 2026-06-03.

1. **Theme is revision & continuity.**  Four detectors +
   one finishing-line export.  Absorbs the deferred A.5.b
   (numeric/spatial contradictions) and A.6.b
   (unresolved-tension) carryovers.
2. **Multilingual via the three-tier model** (below).
   Most multilingual support is *inherited* from the
   existing Snowball / stop-word / whatlang / embedding
   stack; only the Tier-3 quantity lexicons are genuinely
   new per-language work.
3. **First-class multilingual support ships for the five
   supported languages** (en / ru / fr / de / es).  Other
   languages get graceful degradation + a `bootstrap-*`
   CLI to seed the missing lexicons, never silent garbage.
4. **The new detectors are `doctor --scan` classes** —
   Info severity, no autofix, author-judgment findings —
   consistent with the 1.2.16 narrative-audit classes.
   Surfaced identically in the CLI + the `Ctrl+B Shift+0`
   panel.
5. **Standard manuscript-format export is included** as
   the tangible finishing-line deliverable, pairing with
   the 1.2.18 ePub + audiobook exports.

## The three-tier multilingual model

Each continuity feature touches language differently, so
each gets a different multilingual mechanism.  This is
what keeps the cost bounded — most of it is inherited.

| Tier | Mechanism | Multilingual cost | Features |
|------|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| **1 — AI-driven** | Per-language prompt fragments (the 1.2.11 resolver, `iso_from_long`) | Write per-language prompt seeds | Continuity bible (C.3), unresolved-tension (C.4) |
| **2 — Stemmer/stop-word** | Existing Snowball (`parse_stemmer_language`, 18 langs) + stop-words + UAX-#29, keyed on `language` | ~free (same plumbing as the concordance) | Echo detector (C.1) |
| **3 — Lexicon** | New per-language quantity lexicons (number-words, units, directions) | The real new work | Numeric/temporal/spatial contradictions (C.2) |

The **language source of truth** is already settled: the
project `language` field, or per-paragraph `whatlang` when
`editor.prompt_language_mode = "paragraph_detected"`.
Every continuity feature inherits that — no new
language-selection config surface.

### Tier 1 — AI features

Multilingual for free via the existing prompt resolver.
The AI works in whatever language its prompt + context
are in; the resolver already picks per-language fragments.

* The new prompts (fact-extraction, tension-classifier)
  are `prompts.hjson` entries with per-language fragments,
  seeded by extending `bootstrap-prompts`.
* **Critical constraint:** fact *comparison* (is "green
  eyes" in ch.3 contradicted by ch.17?) must use
  **multilingual embeddings or the AI**, never string
  matching — in morphologically rich languages an
  attribute surfaces in many forms (Russian: `зелёные
  глаза` / `зелёными глазами` / `зелёных глаз`).  The
  vector store already holds MultilingualE5 embeddings, so
  cross-inflection (and cross-language, for bilingual
  editions) matching comes from cosine similarity.

### Tier 2 — Stemmer/stop-word features

The echo detector is "concordance machinery + a sliding
window + a distinctiveness threshold," so it's
multilingual by reuse: tokenise (UAX-#29) → stem
(Snowball) → drop stop-words → flag distinctive stems
reused within N paragraphs.

* **Distinctiveness without a per-language frequency
  corpus:** a stem is "distinctive" relative to *this
  manuscript's own* concordance distribution (rare overall
  but clustered) — a manuscript-relative measure that's
  language-agnostic by construction.  No frequency tables
  to ship.
* **Degradation:** languages outside the 18 Snowball set
  (Japanese, Chinese) fall back to exact-surface-form
  matching, documented — the same way the lexicon overlay
  already degrades.

### Tier 3 — Lexicon features

Where multilingual genuinely costs something, because
extraction is lexicon-bound.

* Digits are language-agnostic (`3 days`); number-words
  are per-language (`three` / `три` / `trois` / `drei` /
  `tres`).  Units + directions likewise.
* **Solution — a "continuity lexicon" bundled like the
  stop-word/filter-word seeds**, with a new `inkhaven
  bootstrap-continuity <lang>` CLI (mirroring
  `bootstrap-sdt` / `bootstrap-prompts`) that LLM-seeds
  number-words + units + directions, editable in HJSON.
* **Once normalised to `(value, unit)`, the contradiction
  logic is language-agnostic:** `3 days later` then `after
  a week` → `3d` vs `7d` ordering conflict, regardless of
  source language.
* **Ship** lexicons for en/ru/fr/de/es; other languages
  get a clear skip message ("no continuity lexicon for
  `<lang>` — run `inkhaven bootstrap-continuity <lang>`").

### Cross-cutting

* **Mixed-language manuscripts** (the bilingual
  split-view workflow): under `paragraph_detected`, each
  paragraph's check uses whatlang to pick the right
  stemmer/lexicon — the same per-paragraph detection the
  prompts already use.
* **Invented languages** (the Language system book): no
  Snowball stemmer for Klingon.  Invented-language
  passages fall back to exact-form matching against the
  language's declared alphabet (the Language book's `Meta`
  chapter), and contradiction detection uses the invented
  language's own dictionary.  Documented as Language-book
  integration, not a gap.

## Phase plan

Six phases.  Front-loads the lowest-new-language-cost
detector (echo) to validate the doctor-scan + overlay
integration, then the lexicon-heavy numeric work, then the
AI features, then the export, then docs.  Each phase
ships a commit after green tests.

### C.1 — Echo / repetition-at-distance detector

**Tier 2.**  A new `doctor --scan` class
`echo-repetition` + an opt-in editor overlay.  A
distinctive stem (rare in the manuscript's own
distribution, non-stop-word) reused within an N-paragraph
window is flagged: "`suddenly` appears 3× in this chapter"
or "the metaphor `glass harbor` recurs 6 paragraphs
later."

* Reuses `parse_stemmer_language` + the concordance's
  tokeniser + per-language stop-word lists.
* `editor.echo_window` (default 5 paragraphs) +
  `editor.echo_min_distinctiveness` config knobs.
* Overlay toggle pairs with the existing `Ctrl+B Shift+F`
  style-warning infrastructure.
* Multilingual immediately across all 18 Snowball
  languages; exact-form fallback otherwise.

**Test budget:** 12–14.  Per-language fixtures (en/ru/fr)
asserting the right stemmer collapses inflected echoes;
distinctiveness threshold; window boundary; stop-word
exclusion; exact-form fallback for an unsupported
language.

### C.2 — Continuity lexicon + numeric/temporal/spatial contradictions

**Tier 3 (the real multilingual work).**  Closes the
deferred A.5.b.

* **Continuity-lexicon loader** — per-language
  number-words (1–100 + scales), temporal units
  (sec/min/hour/day/week/month/year), spatial units
  (league/mile/km/…), directions (N/S/E/W).  HJSON,
  bundled for en/ru/fr/de/es.
* **`inkhaven bootstrap-continuity <lang>`** — LLM-seeds
  the lexicon for a new language, mirroring
  `bootstrap-sdt`.
* **`doctor --scan` class `numeric-contradiction`** —
  extracts `(value, unit)` quantities per chapter,
  normalises, flags ordering/arithmetic conflicts
  ("3 days later" → "after a week"; "200 leagues north"
  → "200 leagues south"; ages that don't add up).
* Pure normalisation + comparison (language-agnostic once
  extracted) → heavily testable.

**Test budget:** 16–18.  Lexicon parse; per-language
number-word + unit extraction (en/ru/fr/de/es); the pure
contradiction classifier (temporal ordering, spatial
direction, arithmetic); the "no lexicon" skip path.

### C.3 — Continuity bible / character fact extraction (headline)

**Tier 1 (AI) + embeddings.**  The cycle headline.

* **Fact extraction** — a new AI envelope walks the
  manuscript and extracts per-character established facts
  (appearance, relationships, possessions, origin) into
  structured HJSON in the Characters book.  Per-language
  extraction prompt (seeded via `bootstrap-prompts`).
* **Contradiction flagging** — `doctor --scan` class
  `continuity-drift`: compares each character's facts
  across chapters via **embedding similarity** (not string
  match — handles inflection + cross-language), flags
  divergent attributes ("ch.3: green eyes; ch.17: brown").
* **TUI surface** — a continuity-bible view
  (`Ctrl+V Shift+B`? — verify free) showing each
  character's extracted facts + any flagged drift.

**Test budget:** 12–14.  Fact-schema round-trip;
embedding-similarity contradiction classifier (with
fixture vectors, no live model); per-language prompt
selection; the Characters-book write path.

### C.4 — Unresolved-tension detector

**Tier 1 (AI).**  Closes the deferred A.6.b.

* `doctor --scan` class `unresolved-tension`: a
  small LLM classifier tags whether a paragraph
  *introduces* or *resolves* a tension/question/goal;
  flags introduced tensions with no downstream
  resolution.
* Per-language classifier prompt (seeded).
* Needs real-manuscript calibration before the
  false-positive rate is predictable — ships behind a
  `doctor --scan --class unresolved-tension` opt-in
  rather than the default scan set, with the calibration
  caveat documented.

**Test budget:** 8–10.  Classifier-result aggregation;
introduce-without-resolve detection; per-language prompt
selection; the opt-in gating.

### X.1 — Standard manuscript-format export

The finishing-line deliverable.  `inkhaven manuscript`
(or `build --format manuscript`) emits a submission-ready
document in **Shunn standard manuscript format**:
double-spaced, 12pt monospace, title page with contact +
rounded word count, running header (`Surname / TITLE /
page`), scene breaks as `#`, chapters starting a third
down the page.

* Mostly language-neutral (it's formatting), but
  **word-count rounding** + **scene-break detection** are
  language-aware (reuse the existing scene-break detector
  + word counter).
* Output as typst (compiles to PDF via the existing
  pipeline) + a plain `.docx`-friendly variant if cheap.

**Test budget:** 8–10.  Title-page word-count rounding;
header composition; scene-break → `#` conversion; chapter
page-break placement.

### D.1 — Docs

* Tutorial: "Revision & continuity — the continuity
  bible, echo + contradiction detectors" (C.1–C.4).
* Tutorial: "Submitting your manuscript — standard format
  export" (X.1).
* `CONFIGURATION.md` — the new `editor.echo_*` +
  continuity-lexicon blocks.
* `KEYBINDING.md` + `KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md` — the
  continuity-bible chord.
* A multilingual-coverage table: which detector works in
  which language, and the `bootstrap-continuity` path for
  the rest.
* `RELEASE_NOTES/1.2.19.md` implementation log.

## Test budget total

Roughly 70–85 new tests.  1.2.18 landed at 1053; 1.2.19
should land around 1120–1140.

## Risk register

* **AI false-positive rate** (C.3, C.4).  Continuity
  drift + unresolved tension are judgment calls; an
  over-eager flag is noise.  Mitigate: embedding-
  similarity *threshold* tuning for C.3; opt-in gating +
  documented calibration caveat for C.4.  Both are Info
  severity, no autofix — the author decides.
* **Lexicon coverage gaps** (C.2).  A missing number-word
  silently drops a quantity.  Mitigate: the bundled
  en/ru/fr/de/es lexicons are reviewed against a fixture
  corpus; unknown languages skip with a clear message
  rather than half-working.
* **Morphological inflection** (all tiers).  The whole
  reason fact comparison uses embeddings, not strings.
  Risk: embedding similarity conflates *similar* facts
  ("blue eyes" vs "blue-grey eyes") as contradictions or
  misses real ones.  Mitigate: threshold tuning + the
  finding shows both source quotes so the author judges.
* **Echo distinctiveness tuning** (C.1).  Too low → every
  common verb flagged; too high → real echoes missed.
  Mitigate: manuscript-relative measure + a tunable
  threshold + per-language fixture validation.
* **Invented-language coverage.**  No stemmer; exact-form
  fallback is coarse.  Documented as a known limitation +
  Language-book integration point, not a silent gap.

## Out of scope for 1.2.19

* **Anachronism overlay** (the other half of A.5.b) —
  needs period-vocabulary lexicons, a different lexicon
  beast; defer to 1.2.19.b or the genre-packs cycle.
* **Character voice consistency** (the dialogue-&-voice
  theme) — belongs to its own cycle.
* **Query/synopsis AI helpers + front/back matter** (the
  finishing theme) — X.1 covers the concrete export; the
  rest is a separate cycle.

## Closing

Revision is where the book actually gets made, and it's
where inkhaven has the most headroom.  1.2.19 builds the
revision layer — continuity bible, echo detector, numeric
contradictions, unresolved tension — plus the
submission-format export that gets the finished book out
the door.

Multilingual is designed in, not bolted on: three tiers,
most of it inherited from the Snowball / stop-word /
whatlang / embedding stack inkhaven already ships, with
the genuine per-language work (Tier-3 quantity lexicons)
following the established `bootstrap-*` seed pattern and
shipping first-class for en/ru/fr/de/es.  No feature is
English-only; every one either works across all 18
Snowball languages, rides the per-language prompt
resolver, or degrades gracefully with a clear path to
full coverage.

# 3.0.0 · P1 Stability Audit — Findings Ledger

**Date:** 2026-08-05, on `2.7.0-dev`. **Method:** 7-partition parallel adversarial full-source audit (first full audit since pre-1.9; whole 2.x arc). **Scope:** 304K LOC / 609 modules.

## Headline

The codebase is **fundamentally sound**. Across 304K lines the audit found **zero Critical**, **4 High**, **~8 Medium**, **~5 Low** — and verified the highest-stakes surfaces clean: the **Bund sandbox policy is airtight** (aliases resolve to the denied stub, every registered word is classified, no `STORE_READ` word touches the LLM, fs is project-confined), **UTF-8/byte-boundary discipline is airtight** (multilingual prose can't panic-slice), the **panic surface is almost entirely clean** (the ~2,092 `unwrap`s are overwhelmingly test-only or provably guarded), **untrusted-input parsers are proptested + capped**, and **manuscript saves are atomic and write the focused doc**. The `calc.factorial` DoS from the pre-1.9 audit is confirmed fixed.

The findings cluster into **four themes**, each with a fix pattern already used elsewhere in the tree. None is a coherence crisis; this is a modest, well-characterized punch-list.

## Remediation status (P2)

- ✅ **H1, H2, H3, M4** — fixed & verified (commit `ec4ef804`, tests 2904, warning-free).
- ✅ **H4** — fixed & verified (commit `f35e992e`, tests 2904, warning-free).

## Themes

1. **Cost-rail bypass (systemic).** ~half the advisory LLM "slow tracks" call `collect_blocking` directly instead of the gated `slow_llm_call` rail, so they're invisible to `inkhaven cost` and skip the soft-cap/daily-cap preflight. 4. **Per-frame hot-path cost.** Two TUI draw paths recompute each frame instead of using the established `content_hash` cache (Output-pane DB query; style-warning pass).

# Inkhaven 3.0.0 — Stabilization & Feature Freeze Plan

**Status:** planning (2026-08-05, on `2.7.0-dev`). Chosen approach: **audit-first, then decide consolidation depth.**
**Supersedes:** the 2.7.0 BONDS direction — shelved. A feature freeze is the wrong moment to add a new analytical axis.

## Thesis — why this release is different

3.0.0 is not a feature. It is the promotion of the accreted 2.x surface to a **stable, maintained milestone**, after which work is restricted to bugs and changes to *existing* features. The economics invert:

> Today, surface debt is cheap — a chord remap, a CLI rename, a dead-module deletion cost nothing. **After the freeze, surface churn is expensive or forbidden** (it breaks the one user's muscle memory and contradicts the stability a major bump promises).

Therefore the pre-cut priority is **not polish** — it is doing everything that is *harder or impossible after the freeze* first. Bug-fixing is the post-freeze job; it must not be front-loaded. Surface-shape, schema, and coherence decisions are the opposite: this is the last cheap window.

## The surface being frozen (grounded 2026-08-05)

| Signal | Number | Freeze implication |
|---|---|---|
| Rust source | 304K lines, 609 modules | Large frozen surface; needs systematic audit, not spot checks |
| Analytical intelligences | ~25 + 7 inner readers | The dominant risk is *coherence*, not any single bug |
| Panic surfaces (non-test) | ~2,092 `unwrap()` · 196 `expect()` · 60 `panic!` · 6 `unreachable!` | The 1.2.15 "no panic surfaces" bar needs a triage pass |
| `allow(dead_code)` | 147 sites | Finish-or-cut before freeze — frozen dead code is maintained forever |
| Per-feature DuckDB schemas | ~26 stores | Each is a committed schema; all must be versioned + migratable |
| Chord space | meta_sub `Ctrl+B Shift+*` fully exhausted; one weak `Ctrl+V Shift+O` slot left | Any chord rationalization must happen at 3.0.0 or never |
| `TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK` | 7 | Trivial — close them all |
| Docs / tutorials / companion books | 26 / 116 / 10 | The freeze contract — must match final scope |

Last full-source audit was **pre-1.9** (`hardening-audit-1.9`, `premajor-audit`). The **entire 2.x arc** — SEMNET → GRAPHMIND → CHORUS → SENTINEL → LECTOR → REDLINE → CHRONICLE → KEN — has never been audited as a whole.

## Phases

### 3.0-P0 · Ambition — DECIDED: audit-first
Run P1 before committing to consolidation depth. The audit's findings (bug density, dead-code reality, schema state, coherence gaps) determine whether P2 is a full consolidation milestone or a minimal stabilize-and-freeze.

### 3.0-P1 · Correctness & stability audit — *the #1 freeze-blocker, and the next action*
A multi-agent adversarial full-source sweep (the `premajor-audit` pattern), partitioned so no agent's context overflows. Dimensions:

1. **Panic-surface triage.** Classify the ~2,350 `unwrap/expect/panic/unreachable` sites into *reachable* (I/O, parsing, indexing, arithmetic overflow, user/untrusted input) vs. *provably-safe* (post-check, static regex, owned-mutex-with-poison-recovery). Fix the reachable ones; leave the safe ones. Output: a ranked defect ledger, not 2,350 line edits.
2. **DoS / resource exhaustion** at book scale — unbounded loops, whole-file reads, quadratic passes, large-input parsers (revisit `premajor-audit` items: `calc.factorial`, non-ASCII import RTF/md/PDF).
3. **Silent data-loss** — atomic `io_atomic` writes everywhere prose/config/store is written; snapshot + backup integrity; store crash-safe write *ordering* (blob-before-meta); poison recovery.
4. **Schema durability** — confirm all ~26 DuckDB stores carry the `_inkhaven_schema` version anchor and migrate cleanly forward; no schema is frozen without a version.

**Deliverable:** a single findings ledger, most-severe-first, each item {file:line, class, failure scenario, fix}. This ledger is the input to the P0 consolidation decision and to the P2/bug backlog.

### 3.0-P2 · Surface consolidation — *the last cheap window (scope set by P1)*
Only as deep as P1 justifies. Candidate work, each item independently go/no-go:
- **Chord rationalization** — the map is saturated; if it needs remapping for learnability, now or never.
- **CLI verb coherence** — consistent naming/nesting across ~40+ subcommands.
- **Config completeness** — every block in `CONFIGURATION.md`; defaults preserve behavior; no orphan knobs.
- **Bund surface** — `every_registered_word_is_classified` green across all 35 stdlib modules; namespace consistency.
- **Dead-code prune** — the 147 `allow(dead_code)`: finish or delete.
- **Honest feature-cut pass** — with ~1 user, does every intelligence earn a permanent maintenance seat? Retire what doesn't *before* committing to it forever.

### 3.0-P3 · Documentation as the freeze contract
- Every feature: doc + tutorial + `KEYBINDING` + `CONFIGURATION` coverage (audit gaps vs. 116 tutorials).
- The 10 companion books re-audited to final scope; PDFs regenerated (the `1.6.6 books` ritual).

# ARG-1 — The argument outline (first slice) | | | |---|---| | **RFC** | ARG-1 | | **Title** | A read-only claim → support outline, with two structural gaps | | **Status** | Proposed — the first, deliberately modest slice of the argument-map idea | | **New dependency** | none | | **Audience** | nonfiction authors | ## The idea The full argument-map — claims, support, objections, rebuttals, and the links between them, as a navigable graph — is a large, AI-heavy, UX-heavy build. This RFC is its **smallest honest first step**: an AI pass that, for a chapter, produces a **claim → support outline** and flags the **two cheapest structural gaps**, surfaced as findings. No graph, no objection tracking, no cross-chapter reasoning. The goal is to prove the extraction is *reliable* before investing in the map view. It is the nonfiction cousin of the fiction story-graph (`Ctrl+V W`), but this slice delivers a list, not a graph. ## The two gaps (only these, for now) 1. **Unsupported central claim** — a load-bearing assertion in the chapter that the text backs with no evidence, reasoning, or citation. 2. **Orphan citation** — a `@key` cited in the chapter that supports no identified claim (a citation that reads as decorative). Both are cheap because they need only the chapter's own prose and its own `@keys` — no external truth, no cross-chapter graph. ## Grounded reuse (nothing new to invent) Exactly the pipeline NF-CITE's `--ai` track already uses: - `AiClient::from_config` / `resolve_provider` / `facts_scan::run_blocking` (the blocking LLM call). - `book_walk::chapter_raw_prose` + `audiobook::typst_to_plain` — the chapter text. - `sources::extract_cite_keys(prose)` — the `@keys` cited in the chapter. - `sources::BibEntry` (resolved from the Sources book) — to describe each cited key to the model so it can judge orphans. - The Output-pane finding machinery (`kinds`, `emit`, `with_source_paragraph`) — already used by NF-CITE / fact-check / docs verify. ## Design ### Command `inkhaven argue [--book-name ] [--provider

] [--json]`. Per chapter it: 1. Builds the chapter's plain prose and the list of `@keys` it cites, each paired with its Sources description (`Author (Year) — Title`). 2. Asks the model to extract the argument. **The model must quote claim text from the chapter** (no inventing), and mark each claim's support as a cited `@key`, a reasoning phrase found in the text, or `NONE`. 3. Parses a parse-stable, line-oriented format: ``` CLAIM ||| ||| <@key / reasoning / NONE> ORPHAN ||| <@key> ||| ``` ### Output - **The outline** — for each chapter, its claims and their support (printed, or `--json` for tooling): ``` argue — chapter "The Numbers" • Deaths from war fell across the period. ← @pinker2011 • The decline is not an artefact of population. ← reasoning • Peace is self-reinforcing. ← (no support) ⚠ unsupported orphan citation: @keegan1993 supports no claim ``` - **The two gaps as findings** — each unsupported claim and each orphan citation becomes an Output-pane finding (`kinds::ARGUMENT`, a `argument` source group), anchored to the chapter, so a later TUI chord / background pass can surface them in place. The CLI also prints them and exits non-zero when any gap is found (a pre-review gate). **Chord (when added):** `Ctrl+V Shift+A` (A = Argument) — a free slot in the Ctrl+V family, sitting with the other nonfiction chords: `Ctrl+V @` (cite picker) and `Ctrl+V Shift+C` (the Sourcing pass). All nonfiction reader/check chords live under `Ctrl+V`. ### Keeping it honest (the reliability bar this slice must clear) - **No claim without a quote.** The prompt forbids paraphrase — a `CLAIM` line that does not appear (fuzzily) in the chapter is dropped at parse time. This is the guard against the model hallucinating an argument the author never made. - **Conservative on "central."** The prompt asks only for *load-bearing* claims (a handful per chapter), not every sentence — noise kills a checker. - **Orphans judged only against cited keys**, which are extracted deterministically, so the model can't invent a citation. - Ships behind `--ai` semantics (opt-in, costs tokens); zero-AI paths are unaffected. ## Phases - **P0** — `kinds::ARGUMENT` + an `argument` Output-pane source group + glyph. - **P1** — `src/argue.rs` (pure): the finding model (`ArgClaim { claim, support, supported }`, `OrphanCite`), the parser (`parse_argument(raw) -> (Vec, Vec)`), and the quote-verification drop. Tested. - **P2** — `src/cli/argue.rs`: per-chapter prose + cited-source context, the prompt, the LLM call, the outline render (text/JSON), the gap findings + non-zero exit. - **P3** — Docs: a short note in the nonfiction chapter. ## Non-goals (this slice) - The **graph / map UI** — this is a list. (The map view is the eventual ARG-2+.) - **Objections & rebuttals**, and their tracking. - **Cross-chapter** argument structure (a claim supported in a later chapter). - Any **auto-fix** — Inkhaven flags; the author reasons. - A deterministic tier — argument extraction is inherently semantic, so this slice is AI-only (unlike NF-CITE, which has a deterministic fast track). ## Why this is the right first step It reuses the entire NF-CITE `--ai` pipeline, adds only a prompt + a parser + two gap rules, and produces something an author can act on today — while the quote-verification guard forces the model to stay tied to the text. If it proves reliable, the map view (and objections, and cross-chapter links) become worth building on top; if it does not, we've spent a prompt and a parser, not a graph engine.

# AUDIENCE-1.1 — Utopian / philosophical / theological readers (plan, 1.4.7)

A small additive extension of AUDIENCE-1: three more bundled Inner-Socrates
personas and three more genres for authors whose work is neither plain fiction
nor empirical nonfiction. **No new categories, no new storage, no new modules.**
Builds directly on the AUDIENCE-1 machinery (1.4.6).

## Why these three don't fit the existing nine

| Author | Why the current personas miscalibrate |
|---|---|
| **Philosophy** | `expert-reviewer` is an *empiricist* ("evidence must support the claim, causal language for correlational evidence"). Philosophy lives on logical structure — the unstated premise, the equivocation, the unaddressed counterexample, the valid-but-unsound argument — not empirical evidence. |
| **Theology** | The sharpest case. Demanding "where's your evidence?" is category-wrong for claims grounded in revelation and tradition. The right reader probes **internal coherence, fidelity to source, and the scope of each claim** (revealed vs. reasoned) — never empirical proof. Needs explicit non-empiricist priming or it becomes a hostile skeptic. |
| **Utopia** | Genuinely **hybrid** — fiction (narrative, scenes) *and* an argument about society. The nonfiction personas mute the narrative categories, which is wrong here. The right reader keeps dramatization / temporal-density **live** while heavily weighting "what does this society assume about human nature?" and "what cost does the utopia elide?" |

The existing 5 Slow prose categories cover all three — philosophical/theological
probing is assumption-surfacing + framing + significance + implicit-comparison +
tension. So no new categories (that stays AUDIENCE-2). The genre framing is
LLM-instruction, not lexical matching → multilingual for free.

## The three personas

- **`philosophical-reader`** ("The Dialectician") — treatise. Mutes narrative.
  Heavy on assumption-surfacing (unstated premises) + framing (equivocation,
  definitional scope) + implicit-comparison (counterarguments) + tension
  (contradiction).
- **`theological-reader`** — theology. Mutes narrative. **Non-empiricist** — its
  voice explicitly respects revelation/tradition as grounds, probing coherence,
  fidelity, and scope rather than demanding proof; modal/hedging fast categories
  attenuated so it doesn't hammer conviction as overclaiming.
- **`utopian-architect`** — utopian/dystopian fiction. **Hybrid**: the narrative
  categories are left at default (NOT muted) so it still reads as fiction, while
  assumption-surfacing + implicit-comparison are weighted hard (the society as a
  designed argument; the elided cost; the foreclosed alternative).

## The three genres

Added to both `slow_genre_context()` (interrogator framing) and `genre_fragment()`
(Editor craft), same key set:
- `utopian` / `utopia` / `dystopian`
- `philosophy` / `philosophical`
- `theology` / `theological` / `religious`

## Phase map

- **B-P0 — Three personas (pure).** Add to `bundled()` (9 → 12). Tests:
  12 distinct; philosophical/theological mute the narrative categories;
  **utopian-architect does NOT mute them** (the hybrid invariant); emphasis
  sheets; theological-reader attenuates the empirical fast categories.
- **B-P1 — Three genres (pure).** Add to `slow_genre_context()` +
  `genre_fragment()`. Tests: each resolves in both functions; aliases; the
  fiction default for `None`/unknown still holds.
- **B-P2 — Docs → cut 1.4.7.** INNER_SOCRATES persona table (12), CONFIGURATION
  genre list, Tutorial 90 (or a short 91) updated. Cut 1.4.7.

## Non-goals

New categories (e.g. `logical_gap`, `citation_needed`) — AUDIENCE-2. Per-book
persona routing — AUDIENCE-2. Rewriting any of the existing 9 personas.

Test baseline 1904 (1.4.6); target ≥ ~1918.

# BONDS-1 — implementation plan (grounded, file-by-file)

*Companion to `BONDS-1_PLAN.md`. Every anchor verified against the tree on
2026-08-22. Phases BD-P0→BD-P7; value core = P1+P2+P3. BONDS is a near-1:1
mirror of KEN (`src/ken/`) — this plan is written as "copy KEN's X at `file:line`,
change Y."*

---

## Grounded substrate (what BONDS builds on — almost all of it exists)

**The KEN module is the whole template** — `src/ken/` (5 files, declared `mod ken;`
in `src/main.rs:66`). BONDS = `src/bonds/` + `mod bonds;`. Shared types in
`src/ken/mod.rs`; the run entry is `ken::check::run`, NOT in mod.rs.

- **Reading-order key** — `ScenePos { chapter_ord: u32, scene_index: u32 }`
  (`ken/mod.rs:26`, derives `Ord` → reading order for free). **BONDS reuses it**
  (re-export from `ken` or lift to a shared `scene` mod).
- **The paragraph/scene walk** — `ken::walk::book_paras(layout, h, book) ->
  Vec<ParaRef>` (`ken/walk.rs:29`); `ParaRef { id, at: ScenePos, tags: Vec<String>,
  text: String, declared_pov: Option<String> }` (`walk.rs:16`). Scenes split on
  `manuscript::is_scene_break`; `declared_pov` is the scene's `pov:` tag stamped on
  every para (`walk.rs:70`). Skips `content_type=="jinja"`. **BONDS reuses this
  verbatim** — it is already the generic manuscript walk.
- **Tags are free-form** — `Node.tags: Vec<String>` (`store/node.rs:179`, "free-form
  strings, case preserved"). Prefixed tags parse via `str::strip_prefix` (KEN:
  `tag.strip_prefix("know:")` / `"secret:"` `grants.rs:37,42`; `"pov:"` `walk.rs:71`).
  **`rel:` needs ZERO schema change** — no tag enum exists.
- **Co-presence evidence** — two overlapping sources KEN already wires:
  1. *Scene-derived cast* (primary, no timeline needed): the characters "present"
     in a `ScenePos` = its `declared_pov` + dialogue-attributed speakers
     (`dialogue::detect_spans`+`attribute_spans`, used by `ken::check::detect_uses`
     `check.rs:43`) + roster-name mentions via `drift::mentions` (whole-word,
     multilingual). This is exactly KEN's use-detection machinery, repurposed to
     "who shares this scene."
  2. *Timeline participants* (precise reinforcement): `TlEvent.characters:
     Vec<Uuid>` from `timeline_context::gather_events(h)` (`timeline_context.rs:91`),
     mapped to `ScenePos` via `linked_paragraphs` (KEN does this in
     `grants::grants_from_events` `grants.rs:88`). This is the same signal the 3.0.2
     participant-list fix made populatable.
  → BONDS's per-scene cast = union of (1) and (2). It works on `rel:` tags + prose
  alone; a populated timeline sharpens it.
- **Character roster (name↔UUID)** — `continuity_intel::introduce::roster(h,
  SYSTEM_TAG_CHARACTERS) -> Vec<(Uuid, String)>` (`introduce.rs:140`;
  `SYSTEM_TAG_CHARACTERS` = `store/mod.rs:93`). Names-only:
  `dialogue::pipeline::character_names(h)` (`pipeline.rs:39`). **Limitation: no alias
  field** — a character is one roster node, name = title. `rel:<A>:<B>` names must
  match roster titles (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized via
  `grants::normalize_topic` `grants.rs:24`); alias/nickname resolution is a
  non-goal for v1 (note in help).
- **The KEN driver to mirror** — `ken::grants::build_grants(layout, h, book) ->
  (Vec<Grant>, Vec<KnowledgeItem>, Vec<ParaRef>)` (`grants.rs:131`): one walk + tag
  parse + roster + `gather_events`. BONDS's `build_bonds` is the same four calls.

**The worklist bridge** — `cli/editorial.rs::collect(project, book_name, only,
include_deferred) -> Result<EditorialReport>` (`:22`). Readers run inside the
`if let Ok(cfg)…store…h` guard (`:64`); KEN's block is `:154-160`
(`resolve_user_book` → `ken::check::run` → `editorial::from_knowledge_finding`).
`EditorialFinding { category: String, severity, location: Location{chapter:
Option<String>, paragraph: Option<Uuid>, char_range, path}, message, hint, source:
&'static str, autofixable }` (`editorial.rs:97`). Converter template
`from_knowledge_finding` (`editorial.rs:621`). Promotion `response_kind(category)`
(`editorial.rs:174`): Decision arm `:183-185`, default `_ => Brief` `:189`.

**The surfaces** — CLI `Command::Knowledge { book_name, json, deep, max_cost }`
(`cli/mod.rs:1423`, dispatch `:6893`); dashboard `Action::OpenKnowledge`
(`keybind.rs:150`) → `Modal::Knowledge { rows, anchors, cursor }` (`modal.rs:954`)
→ `open_knowledge`/`build_knowledge_rows`/`knowledge_handle_key`
(`app.rs:16379/16392/16445`) → `draw_knowledge_modal` (`render/modals.rs:6628`);
Bund `src/scripting/stdlib/knowledge.rs` (`ink.knowledge.{grants,findings,check}`,
policy rows `policy.rs:245`); config — KEN has **none** (reads only `cfg.language`),
so `bonds:` is net-new, modeled on `ContinuityConfig` (`config.rs:4398`).

## Open design decisions (resolve at build; defaults chosen)
1. **Co-presence source** — scene-derived cast (POV + dialogue + mentions) UNION
   timeline participants. *Default: both* (works without a populated timeline;
   sharper with one). Simpler v1 fallback: timeline-only (exact KEN parity) if the
   scene-derived cast proves noisy in testing.
2. **CLI shape** — flat `inkhaven bonds --json --deep --strict` (KEN mirror).
   *Default: flat* (drop the `check` subcommand from the PLAN's prose; it added
   surface with no benefit — KEN has none).
3. **`rel:` tag placement** — manuscript paragraph tags, scene-scoped like `pov:`
   (a `rel:` in a scene declares that pair's state at that ScenePos). *Default: yes.*
   A one-shot baseline in the Characters bible is a possible P1 add if wanted.
4. **Alias resolution** — none (roster title match only). *Default: exact-ish
   (normalized, case-insensitive); document the limitation.* Fuzzy-name via
   `drift::mentions` is a later enhancement.
5. **`unearned_shift` severity/response** — Break → Decision. Others → Notice →
   Brief. *Default as stated.*

## Effort
Value core (P0-P3) is the bulk and is ~1:1 with KEN's core, which is a few hundred
lines + tests. P4-P5 are mechanical wiring (each anchor above is a small edit).
P6 is the smallest phase (one prompt + the shared `slow_llm_call`). Total surface is
smaller than KEN's original build because the walk, roster, timeline, collect bridge,
dashboard-modal pattern, and Bund pattern all already exist — BONDS mostly *composes*
them.
