# Inkhaven 1.10.0 — The Cartographer

_The worldbuilder learns to draw. 1.10 adds an interactive map editor — place towns,
draw rivers, mark regions, and check them against the physics, all from the terminal —
plus seed exploration and a real painted map on capable terminals. Every edit is still
an ordinary `world.hjson` change; the tool measures, validates, and records._

## The interactive map editor (MAPED, Tier 1)

Cycle the worldbuilder's right pane to **Map** and press **`e`** to edit. A crosshair
moves over the compiled world (`hjkl`/arrows, `Shift` for a single cell) with a readout
of the coordinate, biome, and elevation under it. Then the tools:

- **`t`** place a town/settlement · **`n`** a named landmark → drawn `⌂`, written to
  `geography.landmarks[]`.
- **`r`** draw a river: move to the source and `Enter`, to the mouth and `Enter`, then
  name it → drawn `≈`, written to `hydrology.rivers[]`. The course is **validated as you
  draw** — "runs uphill", "mouth above the shoreline", "off the map".
- **`g`** place a region, its biome auto-filled from the cell under the cursor → drawn
  `§`, written to `geography.regions[]`.
- **`d`** delete the feature under the cursor.
- **`/mapcheck`** checks the whole map layer against the compiled world — a town in the
  ocean, an off-map coordinate, a region in the sea — flags each offending cell `!`, and
  **`f`** jumps the cursor from one issue to the next.

Every placement is a pending edit: review the batch with `/diff`, commit atomically with
`/write`. Because these are ordinary `world.hjson` declarations, the compiler honours
them (a declared river carves its course) and they appear on the plakat raster too.

## Worlds you can see and explore

- **`/roll [n]`** — the compile is seed-deterministic, so one declaration implies a whole
  space of worlds. `/roll` compiles *n* candidates on derived seeds and compares them
  (continents · sea % · population · climate · ★); **`/adopt <seed>`** sets one.
- **The raster map** — on image-capable terminals (kitty / iTerm2 / sixel), `/map` paints
  the real plakat-rendered map in the Map pane; elsewhere the ASCII biome map stands in.

## Sessions, promotion, and export

- **`/switch <name>`** — switch between named worldbuilder sessions in-place (each keeps
  its own pending delta and journey).
- **Research pane** — `j`/`k` over hits, `a` promotes a passage to a `fact:world`.
- **`/export --pdf`** — render the world dossier to PDF in-process via Typst (all prose
  is emitted as string literals, so any language or punctuation is safe).

## Compatibility

No new dependencies. Every change is additive and backward-compatible: `geography.regions[]`
gains an optional anchor cell (legacy descriptive regions still parse); the pending-delta
engine gains a `RemoveAt` op. Nothing changes the existing compiler, fact-checker, or any
project. Compiles warning-free. Test suite → 2720.

Every prior release lives under
[`Documentation/RELEASE_NOTES/`](.).

# Inkhaven 1.10.1 — The Cartographer Draws More

_1.10.0 gave the worldbuilder a map editor for the human layer — towns, landmarks,
rivers, regions, and the map-check. 1.10.1 finishes it: **roads**, **terrain sculpting**,
**mouse support**, and a full companion-book chapter. Every mark is still an ordinary
`world.hjson` edit._

## Roads

Press `o` in the Map pane's edit mode and connect two named landmarks — move to the
first and `Enter`, to the second and `Enter`. The road lands in `geography.roads[]` and,
because it references landmarks the map already knows, draws between them (`=`) both in
the worldbuilder and on the **plakat raster** — declared roads now emit as `RoadSpec`s
alongside the trade-derived ones.

## Terrain sculpting

Press `+` to raise the land under a soft brush and `-` to lower it (`,`/`.` size it). The
map re-shades live as you sculpt — `~` sea, `.` lowland, `^` hills, `A` peaks — so you
can raise a range or carve a bay and watch it appear. `/terrain` writes the sculpted
heightmap as a grayscale **DEM** under `assets/maps/` and points `geology.dem` at it; a
`realworld compile` (DEM-aware) then rebuilds the whole world — climate, rivers,
settlements — from your land.

_Known follow-up: the worldbuilder's own `/compile` previews the sculpt and writes the
DEM but stays procedural; the terrain takes full effect through `realworld compile`. A
DEM-aware worldbuilder compile is planned._

## Mouse

If your terminal supports it, a left-click in the Map pane focuses it, enters edit mode,
and drops the cursor on the clicked cell — click to point, then place with the single
keys. Mouse capture is enabled only for the worldbuilder, so the research and linguistic
companions keep their native selection and scroll.

## Documentation

*Building the World with Inkhaven* gains **Chapter 21, "The Map Editor,"** with five
faithful terminal screens (the cursor, placing a town, drawing a river, sculpting a
mountain range, and `/mapcheck` flagging a town in the sea). The `WORLDBUILDING.md` and
`KEYBINDING.md` references carry the full map-editor key and command tables.

## Compatibility

No new dependencies. All changes are additive and backward-compatible: `geography.roads[]`
is new, `geology.dem` was already supported by the compiler, and mouse capture is scoped
to the worldbuilder. Compiles warning-free. Test suite → 2723.

Every prior release lives under
[`Documentation/RELEASE_NOTES/`](.).

# v1.2.1 — bdslib absorbed · Bund scripting · data-driven keymap

Largest single release since 1.1. Three intertwined themes:

1. **Crates.io readiness** — the last two vendored path-deps
   (`bdslib`, `tree-sitter-typst`) are now absorbed into the
   inkhaven source tree. `cargo publish` works.
2. **Bund scripting** — Vladimir's `bundcore` stack VM is wired
   in as a first-class extension surface. Hook points, an
   `ink.*` stdlib, sandbox policy, `.bund` Script nodes, runtime
   keymap rebinding.
3. **Data-driven keymap** — `Ctrl+B` and `Ctrl+Z` sub-chords are
   no longer hardcoded match arms; they live in a table that
   HJSON and Bund can both rewrite.

## Headline changes

### Storage layer absorbed in-tree

The bdslib dependency that owned `metadata.db`, `blobs.db`, and
`vectors/` is gone. The slice inkhaven actually used (~11
methods of `DocumentStorage`) lives at `src/storage/`:

- `engine.rs` — DuckDB pool + JsonStorage + BlobStorage
- `vector.rs` — vecstore HNSW wrapper with a `dirty` flag so
  background syncs no-op when nothing's changed
- `embedding.rs` — fastembed model wrapper
- `document.rs` — the 11-method API surface
- `fingerprint.rs` — `json_fingerprint`

On-disk shape is **byte-compatible** with 1.0–1.1 projects.
Existing `frequency.db` is harmlessly ignored.

- **998 → 635 crates** in `Cargo.lock` (Tantivy, augurs,
  bundcore-shard, etc. — none of it inkhaven ever touched).
- **66 MB → 63 MB** release binary.

### Tree-sitter-typst absorbed in-tree

Same pattern, smaller scope. The grammar's C sources live at
`src/grammar/`; `build.rs` compiles them via `cc`. With this and
bdslib absorbed, **no path-deps remain** and the crate is
`cargo publish`-ready.

### Bund scripting

Bund is now embedded as inkhaven's user-customisation surface.
See [`Documentation/Bund/`](../Bund/README.md) for the tutorial.

- **Adam VM** — process-wide singleton, lazily initialised on the
  first eval, holds state across calls.
- **`inkhaven bund "<code>"`** CLI subcommand for one-shot
  evaluation.
- **Six read-only `ink.*` stdlib words**:
  - `ink.node.list`, `ink.node.get`, `ink.node.children`
  - `ink.paragraph.text`
  - `ink.search.text`
  - `ink.snapshot.list`
- **Sandbox policy** in `scripting:` HJSON stanza —
  `disabled_categories` / `disabled_words` / `enabled_words` /
  `enabled_categories` / `no_default_deny`. Defaults deny
  `fs_write` / `net` / `shell` / `code_eval` / `keymap`.
- **Bootstrap script** — `scripting.bootstrap: '''…'''` runs
  once after the VM is built.
- **Five hook points** in `Store::*`:
  - `hook.on_create  ( uuid kind -- )`
  - `hook.on_save    ( uuid -- )`
  - `hook.on_rename  ( uuid new_title -- )`
  - `hook.on_snapshot ( parent_uuid snap_uuid -- )`
  - `hook.on_delete  ( uuid -- )` (per id in deleted subtree)
- **Recursion guard** caps hook depth at 4 (thread-local
  counter, forward-looking for write-side ink.* words).

### `NodeKind::Script` + Scripts system book

Bund scripts are first-class tree nodes:

- **`.bund` files** on disk under `books/<...>/`
- **Tree-pane glyph**: `λ` (mauve, Catppuccin)
- **Auto-loaded** at project open — every Script node's body is
  `bund.eval`'d into Adam after the inline bootstrap, so user
  hook lambdas come online without any HJSON wiring
- **Scripts** is the 8th system book (between Typst and Help),
  the default home for project-global hooks
- **Editor open / save** routes through the same `load_paragraph`
  / `update_paragraph_content` path as `.typ` nodes
- **CLI**: `inkhaven add script "title" --parent scripts`
- **TUI**: `Ctrl+Z N` opens Add modal pre-pointed at Scripts

### Bund chord prefix `Ctrl+Z`

Parallel to `Ctrl+B`. Three default sub-chords:

| Chord | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+Z R` | Run the open `.bund` buffer against Adam |
| `Ctrl+Z N` | New script under Scripts book |
| `Ctrl+Z E` | One-shot eval modal — type expression, see result |

`Ctrl+Z` is configurable via `keys.bund_prefix` (set to empty
to disable for tmux users). tui-textarea's default undo (which
also lived on Ctrl+Z) is on **Ctrl+U** in this codebase, so the
prefix doesn't fight a meaningful builtin.

### Data-driven keymap with HJSON + Bund rebinding

The ~40 chord-action mappings under `Ctrl+B` and `Ctrl+Z` moved
from hardcoded `match key.code` arms into a runtime-mutable
binding table. Two channels rewrite it:

**HJSON overlay** — `keys.bindings`:

```hjson
keys: {
  bindings: [
    { chord: "Ctrl+b y", action: "tree.morph_type" }
    { chord: "Ctrl+b w", action: "none" }                  // disable
    { chord: "Ctrl+z m", action: "bund.run_buffer" }
  ]
}
```

**Bund runtime** — four `ink.key.*` words (default-denied via
the `keymap` policy category):

```bund
"Ctrl+b y" "tree.morph_type" ink.key.bind
"Ctrl+b j" { "jot!" println } ink.key.bind_lambda
"Ctrl+b y" ink.key.unbind
ink.key.list
```

See [`Documentation/KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md`](../KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md)
for the full action table and both channels.

### New chord: `Ctrl+B M` — morph type

Cycle a leaf node's flavour:

```
Paragraph(typst) → Paragraph(hjson) → Script(bund) → back
```

Renames the file on disk (`.typ` ↔ `.hjson` ↔ `.bund`), stamps
new kind/content_type, reopens the buffer with the right
highlighter. Works from both Tree and Editor panes; preserves
the user's focus across the reopen.

### Per-kind tree glyphs

- `¶` Paragraph (typst)
- `❴` Paragraph (hjson)
- `λ` Script (bund)
- `▣` Image
- `►` currently-open in editor

Replaces the previous "all leaves render as `¶`" behaviour
where HJSON paragraphs and Scripts rendered as branch-arrow
glyphs (a real bug — Scripts fell through the `_ =>` case).

### Bund syntax highlighter

Hand-rolled tokeniser at `src/tui/bund_highlight.rs`. Wired
into the editor for any node with `content_type="bund"`:

- `//` line comments → dim grey
- `"…"` strings → green (cross-line state for unterminated)
- `42` / `3.14` / `-7` numbers → peach
- `{` / `}` lambda braces → mauve (matches tree row colour)
- `register` / `println` / `if` / `drop` / …  ~40 keywords → cyan
- `ink.*` / `hook.*` namespace → function colour

### Auto-generated status-bar hints

Pressing `Ctrl+B` or `Ctrl+Z` now displays a hint built from the
live binding table. User overlays (HJSON or `ink.key.*`) appear
in the hint automatically — no more out-of-sync hardcoded strings.

### Background sync — dirty flag + DuckDB CHECKPOINT

- `VectorEngine` now tracks a `dirty: AtomicBool`. Background
  sync (`sync_interval_seconds`, **default 600s** up from 60s)
  is a no-op when no writes have happened since the last flush.
- New `DocumentStorage::checkpoint()` runs DuckDB `CHECKPOINT;`
  against `metadata.db` + `blobs.db`. Wired into the same
  background tick and into TUI shutdown via
  `App::shutdown_flush`.
- Net result: idle editor produces zero disk traffic; long
  sessions don't accumulate WAL.

## New configuration

```hjson
keys: {
  bund_prefix:        Ctrl+z          // new
  bindings:           []              // new — see KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md
}

scripting: {                          // entirely new stanza
  disabled_categories: []
  disabled_words:      []
  enabled_words:       []
  enabled_categories:  []
  no_default_deny:     false
  bootstrap:           ""
}

sync_interval_seconds: 600            // was 60
```

## New CLI subcommands

- `inkhaven bund "<code>"` — evaluate a Bund expression against
  Adam, print result. Optionally `--project <path>` to register
  the store so `ink.*` words can see it.
- `inkhaven add script "title" --parent scripts` — create a
  `.bund` Script node from the shell.

## New documentation

- [`Documentation/Bund/BUND_TUTORIAL.md`](../Bund/BUND_TUTORIAL.md) — afternoon-length intro to Bund
- [`Documentation/Bund/README.md`](../Bund/README.md) — Bund overview + index
- [`Documentation/KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md`](../KEYS_REASSIGNMENT.md) — full action table, HJSON + Bund rebinding channels
- [`Documentation/RELEASE_NOTES/1.2.1.md`](1.2.1.md) — this document

## Breaking changes

- **`Ctrl+Z` is no longer free.** It's the Bund-meta prefix now.
  tui-textarea's default undo binding is shadowed; undo has
  always been on `Ctrl+U` in this codebase, so this only affects
  external chord muscle memory. Set `keys.bund_prefix: ""` in
  HJSON to disable and recover `Ctrl+Z` for your terminal
  multiplexer.
- **`sync_interval_seconds` default went 60s → 600s.** Projects
  with an explicit value are unchanged; defaulting projects see a
  10× longer interval. The interval is now a no-op when the index
  is clean, so the bigger number costs nothing.
- **bdslib path-dep removed from `Cargo.toml`.** Anyone who
  pinned `bdslib` for their own tooling needs to redirect to
  github.com/vulogov/bdslib directly.
- **`frequency.db`** in existing projects is now read-only
  (inkhaven no longer writes to it). Leave it on disk or delete —
  inkhaven is indifferent.

## Migration checklist

1. **Upgrade**: `cargo install inkhaven` or `cargo binstall inkhaven` (binaries attached to this release).
2. **Try a Bund expression**: `inkhaven bund "40 2 +"` should print `42`.
3. **Inside a project**: `inkhaven --project <path> bund 'ink.node.list'` — should JSON-dump every node.
4. **Open the TUI**: `Ctrl+B M` should cycle the cursor row's leaf type. `Ctrl+B` shows the new auto-generated hint string.
5. **Read** [`Documentation/Bund/BUND_TUTORIAL.md`](../Bund/BUND_TUTORIAL.md) if you want to write hooks or rebind chords.

## Release stats

The bdslib + tree-sitter-typst absorptions were ~2k LoC of net
deletions each; the Bund integration is ~1.5k LoC of net new
code.

Suite: 144 / 144 tests, no failures.

# Inkhaven 1.2.10 — standalone editors for `inkhaven.hjson` and `prompts.hjson`

1.2.10 turns two of inkhaven's HJSON files —
`inkhaven.hjson` (project config) and
`prompts.hjson` (prompt library) — into
first-class editing surfaces with dedicated
TUIs.

  * **`inkhaven config -p <dir>`** — schema-aware
    editor for the project's `inkhaven.hjson`.
    Auto-derived schema from the Rust `Config`
    struct.  Typed widgets (bool / int / float /
    string / colour with live preview / path /
    enum / list).  Build-time `///` doc-comment
    extraction so every field has docs in the
    help pane.  Comment-preserving surgical save

### Phase 2 — typed widgets + comment-preserving save (shipped)

`inkhaven config` becomes editable.  The full editing
loop:

  * `Enter` on a leaf (or `e` from anywhere) opens
    a typed widget for that field.  Phase 2 ships
    four widget kinds:
      * `bool` — `Space` / `t` / `f` toggles;
        `y` / `n` snap; `Enter` commits.
      * `int` — digit / sign / Backspace input;
        `↑` / `↓` increment/decrement; bounds-
        check on commit.
      * `float` — same shape with `.` / `e` / `E`
        accepted; rejects NaN / infinity.
      * `string` — free text; multibyte clean.
    Anything else (color / path / enum / list /
    nested map) shows an "edit via Ctrl+B 0 HJSON
    editor" fallback — richer pickers ship later.
  * `r` resets the focused leaf to its built-in
    default — useful for trying a value, deciding
    you preferred the default, and rolling back
    without typing.
  * Every staged edit lights the leaf with a red
    `✱ STAGED` chip + bumps the top-bar
    `N changed` counter.

The save half is the technical centrepiece —
**comment-preserving surgical text rewrite**:

  * New module `src/config_tui/hjson_index.rs`: a
    hand-rolled HJSON walker (~470 LOC) that
    records, for every leaf in the source text, the
    byte range of its value, the byte range of any
    leading-comment block attached to it, plus
    the open / close brace positions of every
    stanza.  Tolerates `#` line comments, `//` line
    comments, `/* */` block comments, quoted +
    unquoted strings, multi-line `'''` strings,
    arrays (recorded as opaque spans), implicit
    top-level objects, trailing commas, and
    arbitrary nesting depth.  Blank-line gap rule:
    comments are detached from a key by any blank
    line between them.
  * New module `src/config_tui/save.rs`: diffs the
    schema tree's `current` against the on-disk
    values, classifies each change as **splice**
    (existing path) or **append** (new path), then
    rewrites the source byte-string in
    descending-offset order so earlier splices
    don't shift later ones.  Appends batch by
    parent stanza and insert just inside the
    closing `}`.  Unknown / user-added fields
    aren't touched — they survive by virtue of
    falling outside every recorded byte range.
    Comments survive for the same reason.
  * Render pipeline: bool / int / float values
    re-emit unquoted; strings re-emit unquoted
    when they're plain identifiers (no whitespace
    / commas / braces / comment markers / reserved
    words / numeric-lookalikes), else quoted with
    proper escaping.

`Ctrl+S` save flow:

  1. **Confirmation modal** lists every staged
     edit with its splice/append kind, path, and
     new value.  `y` / `Enter` commits; `n` / `Esc`
     cancels.
  2. **Atomic write**: contents → `inkhaven.hjson.tmp`
     → `rename(.tmp → inkhaven.hjson)`.
  3. **Backup snapshot**: a copy of the post-save
     contents lands in
     `<project>/.config-backups/inkhaven_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.hjson`.
     ISO date order; `.config-backups/` created on
     first save.
  4. **Schema reload**: the schema + index +
     original-values map all re-read from the
     freshly-written file so the next save diffs
     against current disk state.
  5. **Restart-required overlay**: top-bar chip
     paints purple `restart required` from this
     point until exit, plus the same banner shows
     in the post-save confirmation modal.

Discard-confirm modal triggers on `Esc` / `Ctrl+Q`
when there are unsaved changes.

### Phase 4 — known-map-path support for `llm.providers` (shipped)

The first half of the proposal's Q9 work: user-
added LLM providers in the live HJSON now show up
in the config tree as first-class entries, ready to
edit.  Previously they were dumped into the
"unknown sub-fields preserved as-is" footer of the
detail pane — visible but un-editable.

How it works:

  * A small hand-rolled registry
    `KNOWN_MAP_PATHS: &[&str]` lists every config
    path whose direct children use dynamic keys
    (`HashMap<String, T>` in the Rust schema).
    Phase 4 ships a single entry: `llm.providers`.
  * When the schema builder hits a known map
    path, any live-HJSON key that isn't in the
    defaults gets a first-class tree child built
    from the template of any existing default
    entry — recursively, so every leaf inside the
    new entry gets its own SchemaNode.  Those
    leaves are then editable via the Phase 2
    typed widgets, inspectable via Ctrl+I,
    annotatable via Ctrl+A, etc.
  * The whole user-added stanza is force-marked
    `ValueSource::Configured` (it came entirely
    from the live HJSON, never a default).
  * Typos inside a user-added entry — e.g. an
    `api_token` field when the template has
    `api_key_env` — still flow into the
    `unknowns` collection.  Map-shape recognition
    expands what counts as a *valid map entry*,
    not what counts as a *valid field name
    inside one*.
  * The detail pane labels known map paths
    "map of named entries · N entries" so the
    UX cue lands.

## Implementation log

### A1 — AI sentence-rhythm rewrite (`Ctrl+B Shift+M`)

Pairs with the existing `Ctrl+B Shift+H`
sentence-rhythm gauge.  Where the gauge says
MONOTONE, the rewrite asks the configured LLM to
mix short and long sentences while preserving the
author's voice, tone, named characters, dialogue,
em-dashes, and paragraph breaks.

Prompt resolution follows the standard inkhaven
pattern (`grammar-check` style precedence):

  1. Paragraph in the project's `Prompts` system
     book with slug or title
     `sentence-rhythm-rewrite` /
     `sentence rhythm rewrite`.
  2. Entry in the project's `prompts.hjson`
     library.
  3. Embedded multilingual fallback —
     `sentence_rhythm_rewrite_default_prompt(language)`
     in `src/tui/app.rs`.  Language-aware: the
     prompt explicitly names the project's
     `language` field so the rewrite lands in
     the same language (the model wouldn't
     translate but for the strong directive).

Behaviour:

  * `Ctrl+B Shift+M` in editor scope spawns the
    inference; the streaming response goes into
    the AI pane (the user can watch it land in
    real time).
  * The chord ALSO fires from inside the
    `Ctrl+B Shift+H` rhythm-gauge modal — the
    natural diagnose-then-rewrite path: open the
    gauge, see MONOTONE, press the chord, watch
    the rewrite stream.  The gauge dismisses
    automatically as the inference spawns
    (otherwise it would sit stuck on a stale
    verdict while the AI pane lit up behind it).
    Implemented two-part: (a) the rhythm-modal
    handler intercepts the meta-prefix
    (`Ctrl+B`) and arms `meta_pending` after
    closing the modal, so the normal meta
    dispatch resolves `Shift+M` →
    `AiRewriteRhythm` on the next key; (b)
    `start_sentence_rhythm_rewrite` also
    defensively dismisses any lingering
    `Modal::SentenceRhythm` so the rewrite UX
    is coherent regardless of entry point.
    Generalises: any meta-action is now
    reachable from inside the gauge.
  * When the stream completes, an AI diff modal
    pops **automatically** — the user doesn't
    need to press a chord to trigger review.
    Side-by-side: original on the left,
    rewrite on the right, ↑↓ / PgUp / PgDn /
    Home / End scroll.
  * `a` / `Enter` accept: a snapshot of the
    pre-rewrite buffer is created with
    annotation `Sentence rhythm rewrite` (so
    F6 surfaces it as a discoverable history
    entry), THEN the buffer is replaced.
  * `r` reject: modal closes, buffer untouched.

Implementation notes:

  * New `App.pending_rhythm_rewrite: bool` flag
    set by `start_sentence_rhythm_rewrite` and
    cleared by `pump_inference` on transition
    to Done (or Error).  When set + Done +
    non-empty response, `pump_inference`
    auto-opens the diff modal via the new
    `open_ai_diff_review_with_snapshot` helper.
  * `Modal::AiDiffReview` gains a
    `post_accept_snapshot: Option<String>`
    field.  When `Some`, the accept handler
    (in `ai_diff_review_handle_key`) calls
    the new `snapshot_open_paragraph_with_annotation`
    helper BEFORE `apply_ai_diff_accepted` so
    the pre-rewrite state is preserved.
  * The snapshot helper lives in
    `src/tui/app/snapshot_impl.rs` next to
    `commit_snapshot_annotation` and reuses the
    same `store.create_snapshot_annotated` API
    F5 already uses.

**AI diff pane wraps long lines.**  Until now the
side-by-side diff truncated content past the column
boundary — a single long sentence on either side
became unreadable.  The renderer now wraps each
diff row at column width, prepending the diff
marker (`- ` / `+ ` / `  `) on the first wrapped
row and indenting continuation rows by two columns
so a wrapped sentence reads as one visually
continuous block.  Left and right wrap
independently, but the shorter side is padded with
empty rows so paired diff entries stay vertically
aligned — the side-by-side guarantee is preserved.
Implementation: new `wrap_diff_row` helper in
`src/tui/app/render/modals.rs`; new
`Modal::AiDiffReview.wrapped_total` field written by
the renderer each frame and read by the key handler
to clamp Down / PgDn / End against the post-wrap
row count.  Scroll counts wrapped rows, not source
diff lines.

### Concordance: jump-to-occurrence on Enter

Carryover from 1.2.10.  The `Ctrl+B Shift+L`
concordance modal was read-only — users could see
that the word `walk` occurs 47 times across the
project but had no way to land in the editor on
any of them.  Now: pressing **Enter** on the
selected row closes the modal and navigates to the
first sample's source paragraph at the
corresponding editor line.

Implementation notes:

  * `concordance_jump_to_selection` in
    `src/tui/app.rs`.  Pulls `(slug_path, line_no,
    headword)` out of the first sample of the
    selected entry, resolves the slug path to a
    paragraph node via
    `Hierarchy::find_by_path` (exact inverse of
    `slug_path` used at index-build time), opens
    via the existing `open_paragraph_by_uuid`,
    then jumps the textarea cursor via
    `tui_textarea::CursorMove::Jump`.
  * **Heading-offset translation.**  The
    concordance index is built over
    *heading-stripped* paragraph bodies (so
    `line_no` is 1-based within the prose).  The
    editor displays the *raw* paragraph
    (including the `= title` heading line and
    any blank lines after it).  Naively jumping
    to row `line_no - 1` would land on the
    wrong line.  The jump function replays the
    same heading-strip logic on the live
    textarea, computes the prefix offset, and
    adds it to `line_no - 1` so the cursor
    lands on the right row regardless of the
    paragraph's heading shape.
  * **Graceful failure modes.**  Source
    paragraph no longer exists (rename / delete
    after index was built) — status reports
    `concordance: source paragraph
    <slug_path> no longer exists`, modal stays
    open.  Selected entry has zero samples
    (shouldn't happen — index dedup keeps at
    least one — but defensive) — status
    reports the empty case, modal stays open.
    Open-paragraph failure — status surfaces
    the underlying error, modal already
    closed.
  * Plain `Enter` only; `Ctrl+Enter` and
    `Alt+Enter` fall through to the filter
    input (which today no-ops them, the
    desired behaviour).
  * **System books excluded from the corpus.**
    `open_concordance` now skips any paragraph
    whose ancestor chain contains a node with
    `system_tag.is_some()` — Prompts,
    Characters, Places, Lore, Help, Notes,
    Artefacts, Typst, Scripts.  Two reasons:
    (1) those books are metadata /
    scaffolding, not prose, so they dilute
    the lexical signal (the keybind
    description has always promised "the
    words actually carrying the prose's
    weight").  (2) System-book paragraphs
    are stored only in bdslib (the prompts
    editor never writes `.typ` files), so an
    Enter-jump to one would fail with
    `read …: No such file or directory`
    inside `load_paragraph`.  Filtering them
    out at index time eliminates the broken
    nav case entirely and tightens the
    concordance to actual manuscript prose.

### Show-don't-tell: per-language built-ins + `bootstrap` CLI

Carryover from 1.2.9.  Until now the show-don't-tell
overlay (`editor.style_warnings.show_dont_tell`)
only had built-in word lists for English; Russian,
French, German, and Spanish projects saw nothing
until the user filled in HJSON by hand.  Two
changes land together:

**Built-in lists for RU/FR/DE/ES.**
`built_in_linking_verbs` / `built_in_emotion_adjectives`
/ `built_in_manner_adverbs` / `built_in_cognition_verbs`
in `src/config.rs` now return curated lemmas for
all four languages.  Conservative + dictionary-
shape — the major emotion families (anger /
sadness / fear / joy / fatigue / surprise / shame)
plus the obvious copula / cognition verbs.  Per-
genre or per-corpus tuning is the LLM bootstrap's
job (below), not the built-ins'.  Snowball
stemming at match time means a handful of canonical
forms cover the inflection space.

**`inkhaven show-dont-tell bootstrap <lang>`.**
New CLI subcommand that uses the configured LLM as
a one-shot vocabulary curator.  Reads
`inkhaven.hjson` for the LLM provider, asks for the
four lists in the requested language, parses the
JSON response, and emits a copy-paste-ready HJSON
snippet on stdout.  **Never writes to
`inkhaven.hjson` automatically** — mirrors
`doctor --filter-words-snippet`: the author
reviews the snippet and pastes what they like.

Implementation notes:

  * `src/cli/show_dont_tell.rs`.  Streams the
    response (dots to stderr for progress so the
    HJSON on stdout stays pipe-clean), strips
    optional markdown code fences, brace-balanced
    JSON extraction so stray model chatter
    doesn't kill the parse.  Four unit tests lock
    the parser against the obvious failure modes
    (chatter wrapping, nested braces in string
    values, fenced output, plain garbage).
  * **Strict JSON contract.**  The system prompt
    instructs the model to emit ONE JSON object
    with four arrays and no other text;
    `extract_json_object` walks a brace-balanced
    range so an example object embedded in
    explanatory prose still parses correctly.  On
    parse failure the raw response is dumped on
    stderr and the command exits non-zero —
    debug + retry is one keypress.
  * **Optional `--genre` hint.**  Folded into the
    user prompt so the model picks vocabulary at
    the right register ("literary fiction",
    "thriller", "YA fantasy", …).  Empty by
    default — the genre-neutral built-ins ship
    so nobody *has* to run this.
  * **Why not always-on AI detection?**  Considered
    and rejected.  The overlay updates as the
    user types; running an LLM per keystroke is
    fatal on latency (~1-3s per call), expensive
    on tokens, and breaks offline use — a core
    value of a terminal editor.  Using the LLM
    as a one-shot curator gives the multilingual
    coverage without paying the always-on cost,
    and the existing `Ctrl+B Shift+T` AI
    show-don't-tell scan remains the deep-
    analysis layer for context-sensitive cases.
  * Test `sdt_unsupported_language_falls_back_quiet`
    updated to use `"klingon"` (or any other
    language inkhaven doesn't ship lists for)
    since German now has built-ins — the
    semantic the test locks (empty config +
    no built-ins → `is_empty()` detector) is
    preserved.

**`--update` flag for in-place HJSON merge.**  By
default `bootstrap` prints to stdout and touches
nothing.  With `--update`, the LLM-discovered lists
are merged into `<project>/inkhaven.hjson` directly:
union with the existing per-language entries
(case-insensitive dedup, existing order preserved at
the head, new arrivals appended), then spliced into
the file via the shared
`config_tui::apply_in_place_edits` helper.  Comments
and formatting around untouched leaves survive;
parent stanzas missing from the HJSON are filled in
on append.  A versioned backup of the **pre-patch**
file lands under `<project>/.config-backups/` first,
so rolling back is one `cp` away.  The atomic write
(.tmp + rename) means an interrupted run cannot
truncate `inkhaven.hjson`.

Implementation notes:

  * `config_tui::apply_in_place_edits` is the new
    public surface — a small wrapper around the
    existing config-TUI splice machinery
    (`hjson_index::parse` → `save::apply_edits` →
    `save::write_atomic` + `save::write_backup`).
    Hides the four private submodules so the CLI
    doesn't need to know about `Edit` / `EditKind`
    / `HjsonIndex` internals.  Returns
    `InPlacePatchOutcome { config_path, backup }`
    so callers can report both paths on success.
  * `merge` in `src/cli/show_dont_tell.rs` is the
    actual union: trims whitespace, drops empties,
    lowercases for the dedup key, preserves the
    pushing order.  Locked by two unit tests
    (`merge_preserves_existing_order_and_dedups_case_insensitively`,
    `merge_handles_empty_existing`).
  * **Both modes print the snippet to stdout.**
    `--update` also dumps the merged snippet so
    the user can see what landed — convenient for
    `tee`-style audit logs and for confirming
    visually that the merge produced what was
    expected.
  * **Multi-line pretty-print for string arrays.**
    The splice renderer in `src/config_tui/save.rs`
    used to dump arrays as compact one-line JSON
    (`["a","b","c",…]`).  A 50-entry SDT list on
    one line is unreadable.  Now: arrays of
    strings break to multi-line when they're
    longer than 3 elements or wider than 60
    chars — one element per line, indented to
    `line_indent + 2`, closing `]` flush at
    `line_indent` so it sits under the leaf's
    key.  The line-indent comes from a new
    `line_indent_at_offset` helper that walks
    back to the previous newline and counts
    leading whitespace, so the multi-line render
    matches whatever indentation the user's
    HJSON uses.  Short arrays + mixed-type
    arrays + non-string arrays stay compact.
    Five new unit tests lock the behaviour
    (`render_array_short_stays_compact`,
    `render_array_long_breaks_multiline`,
    `render_array_mixed_types_falls_back_compact`,
    `line_indent_at_offset_walks_back_to_previous_newline`,
    `splice_long_string_array_lands_multiline`).

### Multilingual prompts — Phase D (polish)

Closes the design from the proposal.  Two pieces:

**Phase C correctness fix.**
`detect_paragraph_language` previously consulted
`cfg.editor.prompt_language_mode` directly, which
meant the Phase C session override (`Ctrl+B Shift+N`)
into `paragraph_detected` was ignored when HJSON
said `book_defined`.  Function now uses
`effective_prompt_language_mode()` — runtime
override wins, otherwise HJSON.  The Phase C
status-bar echo on toggle was already correct; this
just makes the underlying detector actually fire
when the user asks for it.

**Cache-invalidation hooks for the whatlang cache.**
`OpenedDoc.detected_language` is now refreshed at the
moments where the body changes enough to plausibly
flip the dominant-language signal:

  * **`save_current`** — calls
    `maybe_redetect_paragraph_language()` after the
    on-disk write + bookkeeping.  The "maybe"
    variant guards on a length-delta against the
    cached `detected_language_length`: only fires
    `detect_paragraph_language()` when the
    non-whitespace char delta meets or exceeds
    `editor.prompt_language_detection_min_chars`
    (default 50).  Saves cost on small edits while
    catching the multi-paragraph rewrites that
    actually matter.
  * **`apply_ai_diff_accepted`** — the AI diff
    modal's accept handler replaces the buffer
    wholesale; calls `detect_paragraph_language()`
    unconditionally (no delta-guard needed when
    every char might be new).
  * **`apply_inference`** — AI critique / replace
    paths that insert text into the buffer.
    Routes through `maybe_redetect_paragraph_language`
    (length-delta guard) — a `Top`/`Bottom`
    paste of a short AI suggestion usually
    doesn't move the needle, but a `Replace`
    can.
  * **External file-change reload** —
    `pump_external_reload` (file mtime drift)
    swaps the buffer with the on-disk content;
    calls `detect_paragraph_language()`
    unconditionally.

`maybe_redetect_paragraph_language` lives next to
`detect_paragraph_language` in `src/tui/app.rs`;
both short-circuit when the effective mode is
`book_defined`, so the new hooks are free for
projects that haven't opted into paragraph
detection.

**Surfacing in config TUI** — already lands as part
of Phase A: the `editor.prompt_language_mode` enum
was registered in `src/config_tui/schema.rs` with
the variants `book_defined` / `paragraph_detected`,
so the config-TUI picker surfaces it automatically
without further wiring.

**Documentation in the Help system book.**  Skipped
deliberately — the Help book is for user-imported
documentation (Typst reference, project notes); it
doesn't have an inkhaven-feature catalogue section
that would naturally absorb a Ctrl+B Shift+N entry.
The chord is discoverable via `KEYBINDING.md`,
`Ctrl+B Shift+/` (the runtime help modal — auto-
populated from the keybind action descriptions),
and the AI pane's `lang=` chip, which the user
sees on every render.

The headline AI feature: translate the open

* **`Ctrl+B Q`** in editor scope — the
  `ai.translate_to_invented` action.  Composes a
  prompt envelope from the target language's
  Dictionary / Grammar / Phonology / Sample-texts
  chapters and streams the LLM's response into
  the AI pane via the shared `Inference`
  machinery (same plumbing the show-don't-tell
  scan + rhythm rewrite use).

* **Language resolution** — MVP rule:
  * Zero Language sub-books → status error
    pointing the user at
    `inkhaven language init <name>`.
  * Exactly one → translate directly into it.
  * Two or more → translate into the first by
    canonical order + warn in the status bar
    (`warn: N languages defined; targeting
    \`<name>\` — per-language chord is Phase C.2`).

  The per-language sub-letter chord
  (`Ctrl+B Q Q` for Quenya, `Ctrl+B Q D` for
  Drow) lands in Phase C.2 — needs the picker
  modal plumbing for ambiguity disambiguation.

* **Prompt envelope** composer in `compose_translation_prompt`
  walks the target sub-book's chapters and assembles
  seven sections:

  1. **System prompt** — explains the LLM's role
     as a translator using the author's grammar +
     dictionary as authoritative; asks for
     translation + per-token gloss + applied
     rules + confidence flags.
  2. **Language overview** — the `Meta/overview`
     body (alphabet, family, reading direction).
  3. **Grammar rules** — every paragraph under
     `Grammar` joined with `---` separators.
  4. **Phonology rules** — every paragraph under
     `Phonology` joined the same way.
  5. **Dictionary** — **RAG-filtered**.  Walks
     every entry in `Dictionary` (the §6 parser
     from Phase B.2 extracts `translation`),
     keeps only entries whose translation appears
     in the source text.  Single-word
     translations match via Unicode word
     tokenisation (`UnicodeSegmentation`);
     multi-word translations (phrasal entries
     like `"of the king"`) need substring match
     on the lowercased body.  Falls back to a
     hint message when no entries match — the LLM
     translates by analogy and flags missing
     vocabulary in the response.
  6. **Sample texts** — first 3 paragraphs under
     `Sample texts`, as register / few-shot
     anchors.
  7. **User prompt** — source paragraph title +
     body.

  Each dictionary entry renders compactly:
  ```
  * `aiya` (interjection): hail — _Aiya Eärendil!_ [forms: plural=aiyar, emphatic=aiyala]
  ```

  At literary scale a typical paragraph (1-3K
  source tokens, ~5-15 relevant dictionary
  entries, ~3-6 grammar rules) lands the envelope
  around 4-8 K tokens — well within any modern
  model's window.

* **Response handling** — for the MVP, the LLM
  output streams into the AI pane.  The user
  reads it there and can copy/paste relevant
  bits back into the editor.  Phase C.2 adds:

    grammar?".
  * `Ctrl+B G` insert response at cursor (the
    chord already exists for general AI output;
    needs envelope-aware extraction to grab just
    the translation, not the gloss table).
  * Inline gloss-table renderer in the AI pane.
  * Per-language sub-letter disambiguation
    (`Ctrl+B Q Q`) via a picker modal.

### Language book — Phase D (doctor + export)

Two CLI features round out the 1.2.13 Language-
book work: a health report and a three-format
exporter.  Both run headless — no UI integration
— so they slot into authoring scripts +
publishing pipelines without spinning up the
TUI.

* **`inkhaven language doctor <name>`** — health
  report for one language sub-book.  Walks every
  chapter, parses each entry's HJSON (via the
  Phase B.2 parser), and emits a structured
  summary:

  * **Overview** — name, kind, family, ISO code,
    alphabet entry count, reading direction
    (all from `Meta/overview`).  `MISSING or
    unparseable` when the body has no HJSON
    block.
  * **Chapter counts** — parseable dictionary
    entries (with unparseable count flagged
    separately so pre-Phase-B authoring is
    visible), grammar rules, phonology rules,
    sample texts.
  * **Dictionary coverage** — entries with
    examples (% of total), entries with
    inflection paradigms (% of total),
    missing-paradigm count flagged with the hint
    that the lexicon overlay won't catch
    inflected forms for those words.
  * **Manuscript gap analysis** — unique words
    (≥2 characters) in user-book prose, how
    many appear as dictionary translations,
    coverage percentage, and a sample of up to
    15 uncovered words sorted alphabetically.
    Walks the hierarchy filtering out every
    system book (Notes / Places / Characters /
    Artefacts / Prompts / Language / Typst) so
    the gap analysis sees only manuscript
    prose, not author reference material.

  Exit code is always 0 — the report is
  informational, not a pass/fail gate.

* **`inkhaven language export <name> --format
  <fmt> --output <path>`** — three formats land
  in Phase D:

  * **`--format json`** (default) — full
    structured dump.  Top-level keys: `language`,
    `meta`, `dictionary` (sorted by lemma),
    `grammar`, `phonology`, `sample_texts`.
    Pretty-printed for human inspection +
    downstream `jq` ergonomics.  Streams to
    stdout when `--output` is omitted.
  * **`--format anki`** — CSV deck importable
    by Anki / SuperMemo / Mochi.  Columns:
    `word`, `translation`, `type`, `example`,
    `inflection` (semicolon-joined `key=value`
    pairs).  RFC 4180-style quoting kicks in
    when a field contains `,`, `"`, or
    newline.  Streams to stdout when
    `--output` is omitted.
  * **`--format dictionary-twocol`** — A4
    two-column printable Typst dictionary.
    Title centred at the top (`Quenya
    dictionary`), italic subtitle for kind +
    family when authored, then alphabet
    bucket headers (`— A —`, `— B —`, …) with
    each bucket's entries underneath: bold
    headword, italic POS, translation,
    optionally an indented italic example, and
    a small-font `forms — key: value, …`
    paradigm line.  Requires `--output
    <path.typ>` — the Typst renderer doesn't
    stream.

  Entries are sorted by lowercased lemma so
  every format produces a stable diff across
  runs (helpful for version control of
  generated artefacts).

  Author-supplied text passes through a small
  Typst escape (`*`, `_`, `#`, `[`, `]`, `\`
  get backslashed) so dictionary content can't
  trigger Typst's emphasis / code / link
  semantics.  Authors with adversarial input
  (raw Typst inside translations) should use
  the `json` format instead.

  `render_anki_emits_header_row`,
  `render_anki_renders_entry_row`,
  `render_dictionary_twocol_groups_by_alphabet`.

# Inkhaven 1.2.14 — plot intelligence + inline comments + quick wins

1.2.13 was the **Language book** release — a
first-class invented-language workbench with
five-chapter sub-books (Meta / Dictionary /
Grammar / Phonology / Sample texts), HJSON-
fronted entries, lexicon overlay + status chip
in the manuscript editor, AI translation flow
with `Ctrl+B Q` / `Ctrl+B Shift+Q`, full CLI
surface (init, add-word, --import CSV with --new
/ --force, remove-word, list, doctor with --json,
export), and two tutorials (49 + 50) with a
worked Tira sample CSV.

1.2.14 picks up two new themes plus a sweep of
small quick-wins, in three groups:

* **Theme A — Plot / narrative intelligence.**
  New `Threads` system book, surfaced via
  `Ctrl+V Shift+H` (picker + 5-thread swim-lane
  weave view), `Ctrl+V Shift+A` (AI thread audit),
  `Ctrl+V Shift+D` (deterministic thread doctor),
  and the `inkhaven thread` CLI (`add` / `list` /
  `doctor` / `export --format json|csv|markdown`).
  Threads tie waypoints to manuscript paragraphs
  so dropped payoffs and dormant arcs surface
  before the reader sees them.

* **Theme C — Inline comments.**  Sidecar JSON
  storage so `<paragraph>.comments.json` travels
  with the prose in git and diffs cleanly.
  `Ctrl+V c` adds a span-anchored comment (char-

  renders the span with `theme.comment_span_modifier`

  plus a `(N/M in ¶)` dense indicator; panel chords
  include `Enter` open + jump cursor, `r` resolve,
  `R` toggle resolved-filter, `d` delete, `/`
  filter, `a` AI digest (categorised across
  STRUCTURAL / PROSE / FACTUAL / QUESTION).  Full
  CLI surface: `inkhaven comments list / resolve /
  reopen / delete / export`.

* **Quick wins.**  Project templates (`inkhaven
  init <path> --template <name>` + `inkhaven
  template list`) shipping 14 scaffolds, including
  5 Russian (novel, повесть, научная фантастика,
  лор, утопия) + 3 international (epic-fantasy,

## Implementation log

### Threads system book — Phase A.1 (foundation)

Lays the groundwork for the plot-intelligence
tooling described in
`Documentation/PROPOSALS/1.2.14_PLAN.md`.  Phase
A.1 is the storage + scaffold layer only — no
weave view (A.2), no AI thread audit (A.3).

* **`SYSTEM_TAG_THREADS = "threads"`** added to
  `src/store/mod.rs`.  Top-level `Threads` system
  book auto-creates on next project open (or
  upgrade from a pre-1.2.14 project) alongside the
  existing system books.  Lands at canonical order
  index 6 — after Artefacts, before Language — so
  the worldbuilding cluster (Places / Characters /
  Artefacts / Threads / Language) groups together
  in the tree.  Existing user books shift up by 1
  if they collided with the slot; the heal-pass
  at the end of `ensure_system_books` mops up.

* **`inkhaven thread add <name>`** CLI subcommand.
  Creates a Paragraph under the Threads system
  book, seeds the body with the full commented
  HJSON template per proposal §3.1 (identity:
  `title` / `status` / `weight` pre-filled from
  the CLI flags; arc shape: `opening` /
  `midpoint` / `payoff`; connections:
  `characters` / `places` / `artefacts` /
  `related_threads`; metadata: `tension` /
  `register` / `notes`).  Sets `content_type =
  "hjson"` so the editor renders with syntax
  highlighting + the paragraph status bar shows
  `[hjson]`.  Disk-write + bdslib-write follow
  the canonical two-step pattern from Language
  entries.  Rejects duplicates by case-insensitive
  title.

  ```
  $ inkhaven thread add "inheritance subplot" \
      --status develop --weight subplot
  added thread `inheritance subplot` to Threads (develop · subplot)
    open Threads/inheritance subplot in the editor to fill opening / midpoint / payoff
  ```

* **`inkhaven thread list`** CLI subcommand.
  Walks the Threads subtree, parses each entry's
  HJSON summary fields, prints a column-aligned
  table:

  ```

    name                  status    weight  tension   ch  pl  art
    ----------------------------------------------------------
    inheritance subplot   develop  subplot        7    2   1    0
    redemption arc        develop    major        5    1   0    1
  ```

  `--status` / `--weight` flags filter case-
  insensitively.

### Threads — Phase A.3 (AI thread audit)

The headline AI feature of the plot-intelligence
theme.  Reads every Thread paragraph's HJSON +
runs a structural blind-spots pre-pass + walks
the cursor's scope, then asks the LLM to score
each scope paragraph against the thread
inventory and call out drift.

* **`Ctrl+V Shift+A`** (action:
  `ai.thread_audit`) — fires the audit from any
  pane.

* **Scope resolution from the F9 AiMode chip:**
  * `AiMode::Book` / `Chapter` / `Subchapter`
    → walk up from the cursor (open paragraph
    when there is one, otherwise the tree-pane
    cursor) until a node of that kind is found.
  * `AiMode::Paragraph` / `Selection` / `None`
    → fall back to the cursor's containing
    Chapter.  Auditing a single paragraph is too
    narrow to be useful; the chapter is the
    smallest meaningful unit.
  * System-tagged books are skipped (auditing
    the Threads book against itself is a
    no-op).

* **Blind-spots pre-pass** — computed BEFORE the
  LLM ever runs so the model has hard evidence
  rather than guessing from prose alone.  Three
  detectors:
  * **Dormant in scope** — thread has links
    elsewhere in the project but zero in the
    cursor scope.  Flags arcs the section is
    neglecting.
  * **Payoff unfired** — thread status is
    `payoff` but no paragraph in the project
    links to it.  Surfaces declared payoffs the
    author hasn't actually written yet.
  * **Zero links** — thread status is past
    `setup` but the project contains zero
    references.  Catches the "I declared this
    thread, but never followed through" gap.

* **Prompt envelope** composer reads:
  * Every Thread paragraph's full HJSON body
    (title / status / weight / arc shape /
    connections / tension / register / notes).
  * The blind-spots list with the kind label
    for each.
  * Every paragraph in the scope (title + body +
    outgoing-link count).
  * A system prompt that asks for four-part
    output:
    1. Per-paragraph thread scoring (advances /
       touches incidentally / should advance
       but doesn't).
    2. Confirm or refute each blind spot.
    3. Flag threads whose declared status looks
       wrong given the manuscript evidence
       (e.g. `setup` with many incidental
       touches; `payoff` without the payoff
       landed).
    4. One-paragraph summary of the scope's
       narrative health.

* **Streaming** — runs through the shared
  `spawn_chat_stream` + `Inference` machinery
  (same plumbing every other AI flow uses).
  Focus jumps to the AI pane; the response
  streams in.  Standard `I` / `T` / `B` apply
  chords work for selectively pulling sections
  of the audit into a Notes paragraph.

  glue (HJSON parsing covered by Phase A.1;
  hierarchy walking covered by existing tree
  tests; envelope composition has no isolatable

### Comments — Phase C.1 (sidecar storage + Ctrl+V c)

Inline comments anchored to character spans in
manuscript prose.  Span anchoring, sidecar JSON
storage that travels with the .typ in git, a
multi-line editor modal, and a status-bar chip
when the cursor lands in a commented span.

* **`Ctrl+V c`** (action: `view.add_comment`) —
  fires from the editor.  Resolves the anchor
  span:
  * **With selection** — anchor is the
    selection's character range, normalised
    so a reverse selection (end before start)
    still produces a `(start, end)` pair where
    `start < end`.
  * **No selection** — anchor is the word at
    the cursor, walked outward via Unicode
    `is_alphanumeric() || '_' || '\''`
    boundaries.  When the cursor is on a blank
    line or whitespace, the chord errors with
    "place cursor on a word OR select a span".

* **`Modal::CommentEditor`** — multi-line
  `tui-textarea` body with a header line
  showing the anchor span snippet ("on:
  \"…\"") so the author sees what they're
  commenting on.  Chords:
  * `Ctrl+S` — commit.
  * `Ctrl+C` — cancel unconditionally.
  * `Esc` — cancel when the buffer is empty;
    otherwise no-op (prevents accidental loss
    of long-typed comments).
  * Everything else is forwarded to the
    textarea so the author can type / navigate
    normally.

* **Sidecar JSON storage** — each paragraph's
  comments live in a sidecar file alongside
  the `.typ`:

  ```
  books/manuscript/chapter-1/03-rain.typ
  books/manuscript/chapter-1/03-rain.comments.json
  ```

  Schema version 1:

  ```json
  {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "comments": [
      {
        "id": "...",
        "char_start": 412,
        "char_end": 487,
        "author": "vladimir",
        "created_at": "2026-06-01T10:23:00Z",
        "resolved": false,
        "resolved_at": null,
        "text": "…",
        "replies": []
      }
    ]
  }
  ```

  * **Character offsets**, not byte — UTF-8
    boundary edits don't corrupt anchoring.
  * **Stable UUID** per comment so an AI digest
    or beta-reader export survives author
    edits to surrounding prose.
  * **Pretty-printed** JSON for git-friendly
    diffs.
  * **Empty comments list** → sidecar removed
    (no littering the project with empty JSON
    files).
  * **`replies: []`** reserved for Phase C.2
    threading.

* **Author resolution** — `editor.comment_author`
  HJSON field overrides; falls through to
  `$USER` → `$LOGNAME` → `$HOSTNAME` →
  `"anonymous"`.  Set per-project when the
  inferred author is wrong (shared workstation,
  system account) or when multi-author
  attribution matters.

### Q.2 — snippet expansion (HJSON-driven)

`editor.snippets` HJSON stanza maps trigger
strings to expansion bodies.  When the editor
sees a "non-word" character (whitespace,
sentence-ending punctuation, closing bracket,
newline, tab) typed immediately after a
configured trigger, the trigger is replaced
inline with the resolved expansion; the
triggering non-word char stays so `\dt `
becomes `<date> ` with the space intact.

**HJSON shape:**

```hjson
editor: {
  snippets: {
    enabled: true
    triggers: {
      "\\dt":   "{today}"
      "\\time": "{now}"
      "\\sig":  "— {author}"
      "\\tk":   "[[{paragraph_slug}]]"
      "\\sel":  "<<{selection}>>"
      "\\dts":  "{today:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S}"
    }
  }
}
```

`enabled` defaults to `true`; an empty
`triggers` map means no expansion fires.

**Placeholders** resolved in expansion bodies:

| Placeholder | Replaced with |
|-|-|
| `{today}` | Today's date `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `{today:%FMT}` | Today's date in the chrono format string |
| `{now}` | Current time `HH:MM` |
| `{now:%FMT}` | Current time in the chrono format string |
| `{paragraph_title}` | The open paragraph's display title |
| `{paragraph_slug}` | The open paragraph's slug |
| `{selection}` | The active selection text (empty when none) |
| `{author}` | Resolved comment author (mirror of `editor.comment_author`) |

Unknown placeholders pass through verbatim
(`{nonexistent}` stays `{nonexistent}`) so
typos are visible to the author.  Unmatched
braces also pass through.

**Trigger matching:**
* Longest-match wins (so `\dts` beats `\dt`
  when both could fire).
* Case-sensitive substring at the END of the
  text before the firing char.
* Trigger characters typed without a firing
  non-word character don't expand — they
  accumulate until the user commits with a
  space / period / Enter / Tab / etc.

**Wiring:**
* `tui::snippets` module — `ExpansionContext`,
  `find_trigger`, `expand_placeholders`,
  `is_expansion_trigger_char`.
* `App::maybe_expand_snippet` (new method on
  `tui::app::editor_impl`) fires from
  `handle_editor_key_inner` AFTER the textarea
  processes the trigger char.  Short-circuits
  on: snippets disabled, no triggers, no
  paragraph open, read-only paragraph, cursor
  at column 0, no trigger match.
* `read_selection_text` helper extracts the
  selection into the `{selection}` placeholder
  (single-line + multi-line both handled).
* Trigger replacement uses `start_selection`
  + `move_cursor(Back)` × N + `cut` +
  `set_yank_text` + `paste` — the canonical
  "replace" pattern used elsewhere in the
  crate.

**Deferred to Phase Q.2.1:**
* `{cursor}` — re-position cursor after
  expansion (multi-position logic).
* Picker-based placeholders: `{char_lookup}`,
  `{place_lookup}`, `{artefact_lookup}`.
* `bund:` prefix — route the expansion body
  through the embedded Bund VM for
  context-aware expansion.

**Phase Q.2 tests** — 11 new:
* `find_trigger_matches_at_end` /
  `_returns_none_when_no_match` /
  `_prefers_longer_match`
* `expand_static_placeholders` /

# Inkhaven 1.2.15 — Stability + Self-Healing

1.2.14 was the **plot intelligence + inline
comments + quick wins** release — a new `Threads`
system book with swim-lane weave view (`Ctrl+V
Shift+H`), AI thread audit (`Shift+A`), and
deterministic thread doctor (`Shift+D`); inline
sidecar comments with span anchoring + project-
wide panel + AI digest (`Ctrl+V c` / `Shift+C`);
14 init templates including 5 Russian and 3
international new (epic-fantasy / mystery /
french-novel); HJSON snippet expansion with 8
placeholders incl. `{cursor}` split-paste; AI
continuation drafting (`Ctrl+V d`); inline
footnote insertion (`Ctrl+V f`); project word-
count goal modal with 30-day projection
(`Ctrl+V Shift+G`); style-transfer rewrite
(`Ctrl+V y`).  Three new CLI surfaces: `thread`,
`comments`, `template`.  Tests 565 → 637 (+72).

**1.2.15 is a stability release.**  Four themes
land:

* **Theme S — Stability sweep.**  Catalogue
  every panic site (`.unwrap()` / `.expect()` /
  `panic!()` / `unreachable!()` / index-into-
  slice / poisoned-lock unwrap) in hot paths;
  replace with `Result` plumbing or graceful
  degradation.  Five sub-phases by module group.
* **Theme H — Background health monitor.**
  Tokio task running periodic integrity checks
  on the DB / Tantivy index / HNSW vectors /
  textarea-vs-disk sync / tree parent-pointer
  integrity.  Status-bar `health` chip.  Safe
  auto-repair (idempotent, never touches user
  content) + per-class HJSON knobs.
* **Theme D — Doctor scan + autofix.**  Project-
  wide problem catalogue (zero-byte files,
  orphan paragraphs, corrupt sidecars, dangling
  wiki-links, orphan thread waypoints, DB/disk
  hash mismatches).  `inkhaven doctor --autofix`
  with per-class confirmation; new TUI modal
  (`Ctrl+B Shift+?` or `Shift+0`).
* **Theme R — Crash report writer + recovery.**
  Custom panic hook flushes dirty buffers to
  `.inkhaven-rescue` files, dumps panic
  context + project state + recent action ring
  to `inkhaven-crash-<ts>.hjson` in cwd, then
  exits cleanly.  New `inkhaven recover
  <crash.hjson>` CLI lifts unsaved buffers back
  on restart.

Goal: zero panics from the hot path, zero data
loss across crashes, every project-wide
inconsistency either auto-fixed or surfaced.
Goal is asymptotic — the cycle's concrete exit
criteria are spelled out in §9 of the proposal.

See `Documentation/PROPOSALS/1.2.15_PLAN.md`
for the full phase shape, test targets (target:
637 → ≥ 700, +63 new regression tests), and risk
register.

Phase G (Git / backup safety rails — uncommitted-
changes warning, backup-freshness chip, disk-
space gate) is out of scope for 1.2.15 and
deferred to 1.2.16.

## Planned themes

### Carryovers from 1.2.14

#### Snippet expansion — picker placeholders + bund: prefix

The Q.2 snippet system ships with 8 built-in
placeholders that resolve synchronously inside
`expand_placeholders`.  Three placeholders + one
prefix were deferred because they need to pause
the synchronous expansion pipeline for an async
event:

  * **`{char_lookup}` / `{place_lookup}` /
    `{artefact_lookup}`** — open the corresponding
    system-book picker and substitute the chosen
    entry's display name (or wiki-link target,
    depending on the surrounding text).  Needs a
    pending-snippet state machine: the editor
    stashes the partial expansion, opens the picker
    modal, and resumes the substitution on commit.
  * **`bund:` prefix** — when the snippet body
    starts with `bund:`, the rest is interpreted
    as a Bund-VM program whose output (top of stack
    as string) becomes the expansion.  Needs a Bund
    interpreter handle on the snippet expansion
    path plus error handling for non-stringable
    results.  Pairs naturally with the existing
    `ink.*` stdlib (`ink.fs.read_file`,
    `ink.editor.*`).

  Both unlock advanced authoring flows but require
  the same underlying mechanism — once the async
  state machine lands, all four arrive together.

## Implementation log

### Theme R — Crash report writer + recovery (R.1 + R.2)

**R.1** — new `src/crash` module: `CrashContext`
singleton + `install_panic_hook()` chained to the
default Rust hook + atomic-write helper + global
terminal-restore slot the TUI sets/clears around
its raw-mode session.

* `CrashReport` struct (version, panic context,
  project context, rescued buffers, recent action
  ring of last 50 user actions, environment
  fingerprint, process stats).  HJSON
  serialization; panic message truncated at 4 KB.
* `actions::ActionRecord` + `ActionRing` —
  capped chronological ring with structural
  detail strings.
* `rescue::DirtyMirror` + `flush_dirty_buffers` —
  writes every dirty buffer to
  `<original>.inkhaven-rescue` atomically; per-
  file errors recorded as `RescueOutcome` and
  don't abort the rest of the flush.

Wiring: `main.rs` installs the hook before any
code that might panic; TUI registers a terminal-
restore closure on raw-mode enter; `App`
maintains the dirty-buffer mirror via a 2 s
debounce in the main loop; `save_current` clears
mirrors on dirty → clean transitions; `run_action`
pushes an `action.<Variant>` record on every
dispatched action.

14 new tests covering atomic-write, action-ring
rotation, HJSON roundtrip, rescue flush, error
handling.

**R.2** — new `inkhaven recover <crash.hjson>`
CLI.  Walks the rescued-buffer manifest; per-buffer
prompt accepts `y` / `N` / `diff`.  On apply:
copies the current on-disk file to
`<original>.pre-recover-<UTC>` then atomically
replaces it with the rescue bytes via
`io_atomic::write`.  `--yes` skips prompts;
`--keep` retains files in cwd after apply
(default moves them to
`<project>/.inkhaven/recovered/`).

4 new tests covering: empty-report flow,
identical-content short-circuit, full apply path
with backup verification, `--keep` retention.

Five sub-phases, 62 panic sites + 2 latent
out-of-bounds crashes + 5 non-atomic critical-
data writes + 4 lock-poisoning sites neutralised.

**S.1** — sweep `src/tui/app/**`.  43
`unreachable!()` arms in the `draw_modal` match
collapsed into a single graceful catch-all that
logs and returns instead of panicking on an

### Phase S.6 — Security hardening

Post-proposal addition driven by a security
audit.  Audit catalogued 4 risk classes; all
patched in 1.2.15.

New `src/path_safety.rs` — `resolve_within(root,
candidate)` rejects absolute paths and `..`
traversal; `resolve_within_or_absolute` permits
absolute paths for config fields with documented
intent.  9 tests.

**H3 — recover CLI path traversal.**  Crash-
report `paragraph_rel_path` validated via
`resolve_within_str` before joining onto the
project root.  Crafted reports with
`paragraph_rel_path: "../../etc/passwd"` rejected
with a security error.

**H4 — HJSON config path traversal.**
`prompts_file` (in `src/project.rs`) and
`artefacts_directory` (in `src/store/mod.rs`)
filtered for `..` escapes in relative paths.
Absolute paths still honoured per documented
intent.  Rejections fall back to safe defaults
with a warning log.

**H2 — `ink.fs.*` sandbox.**  `ink.fs.read` /
`ink.fs.write` now confine paths to the project
root by default via `resolve_within_str`.  Writes
upgraded to atomic via `crate::io_atomic::write`.
New `scripting.fs_unsandboxed: bool` policy
opt-out for trusted-use cases (default false).

**H1 — Script auto-load trust gate.**  New
`scripting.trust_decision` HJSON field: `"ask"`
(default) requires `<project>/.inkhaven/trust`
with a `trust` marker line; `"trust"` runs
unconditionally; `"deny"` never runs.  File-based
gate (not interactive prompt) so it works in
both TUI and CLI flows.  7 tests covering
explicit/file/case/unknown-value paths.

Audit findings not yet addressed (deferred):

* **M1** — recent-action ring in crash report may

  Mitigation: review report before sharing

* **M3** — script-initiated `ink.input` modals
  could mimic legitimate prompts.  Mitigation:

Three checks now run from the tokio monitor
task, against the cloned `Store`:

### Phase T.2 — Binary resolution + auto-download library

Converts `tui::piper` from a single file into a
directory module with three submodules: `mod.rs`
(types + diagnostic messages),
`binary.rs` (resolution), `download.rs` (HTTP +
extract).

* **`PiperUnavailable`** expanded with seven
  variants: `BinaryNotFound`,
  `UnsupportedPlatform`, `AssetNotFound`,
  `DownloadFailed`, `ExtractFailed`,
  `ChecksumMismatch` (reserved for T.4.b),
  `VoicesDirInvalid` (reserved for T.4).  Each

  the recovery action.
* **`Platform::detect`** maps
  `std::env::consts::{OS, ARCH}` to one of six
  supported `(PiperOs, PiperArch)` tuples
  (darwin / linux / windows × x86_64 /

* **`pick_piper_release_asset`** —
  priority-ordered matcher tolerant of

### Phase T.3 — Voice catalog

`Catalog` + `VoiceMeta` + `CatalogFile`
modelled after Piper's
`voices.json` shape: top-level map of voice
key → metadata (language code / family / native
+ English name / quality tier / files map of
relative-path → `{size_bytes, md5_digest}`).

* **`parse_voice_catalog`** — pure parser,
  tolerant of missing optional fields, drops
  voices without `language.code` (we can't
  classify them).
* **`Catalog::load_with_clock`** implements the
  freshness-first policy:
    1. Fresh cache (mtime within ttl) → parse +
       return, no network.
    2. Else fetch via `fetch_json` closure,
       parse, write atomically via
       `crate::io_atomic`, return fresh.
    3. On network failure with a cached copy
       present, parse the stale copy + return
       with `stale: true` + a
       `tracing::warn!`.  Synthesis with
       already-downloaded voices must not
       break when the network goes away.
    4. On network failure with no cache,
       surface the original error.
* **`Catalog::voice`** does canonical-key
  lookup then alias fallback;
  **`languages()`** dedupes + sorts;
  **`voices_for_language`** sorts by quality
  tier descending then key ascending.
* **`VoiceMeta::onnx_url` / `onnx_json_url`**
  join the catalog's relative paths to the
  Hugging Face base URL so T.4 has clean
  download sources.

27 new tests, 819 → 846 passing.

### Phase T.4 — Voice auto-download

Two submodules:

* **`lru.rs`** — `LruIndex` with newest-first
  vec backing, plain-text `<voices_dir>/.lru`
  format (`<voice-key> <iso8601>`), tolerant
  load + atomic save via `crate::io_atomic`.
  `touch` inserts-or-moves to the front;
  `evict_beyond(max)` returns evicted keys;
  `max == 0` is a documented no-op so a typo
  can't wipe the cache.
* **`voice.rs`** — `ensure_voice_downloaded`
  orchestrates:
    1. `voice_files_present` — both `.onnx`
       and `.onnx.json` on disk + non-empty.
       A zero-byte file from an interrupted
       transfer does NOT count as present
       (defends against the old "curl killed,
       0-byte placeholder" failure mode).
    2. `fetch_to_file` twice into
       `<voice_key>.onnx.part` /
       `.onnx.json.part` staging files.  Second
       failure cleans up the first.
    3. Atomic install via
       `crate::io_atomic` for both files.
    4. LRU touch + `evict_beyond` — each
       evicted voice's files are removed.
    5. First-ever-download `.gitignore` append
       (`.inkhaven/voices/`), idempotent.

Path safety: `safe_voice_filename` rejects keys
containing `/`, `\`, `..`, NUL, empty, leading
`.`.  Tested against `../../etc/passwd` voice
keys.

MD5 verification deferred to T.4.b — catalog
field exposed via
`CatalogFile::md5_digest`; ONNX runtime + HTTPS
provide reasonable trust for cycle 1.

41 new tests, 846 → 887 passing.

pipeline + playback dispatch:

* **`synth_to_wav`** spawns the resolved Piper
  binary with `--model` + `--output_file` +

### Phase T.2.a — Whole-tree install bugfix

Discovered when actually exercising Piper
end-to-end: `install_binary` from T.2 copied
only the `piper` executable + dropped the rest
of the extracted tarball (`espeak-ng-data/`
with 400 phoneme tables, `piper_phonemize`

would launch but fail at first phonemization.

the new install step wipes the target dir,

self-wipe the source.

## Implementation log

### I.1 — Performance pass

The performance debt deferred from 1.2.16 + 1.2.17.
Method: build a deterministic fixture, measure,
profile, fix the hotspots the data points at, gate
against regression.

**I.1.1 — Fixture generator.**  Hidden `inkhaven
gen-fixture <path>` produces a deterministic synthetic
project (default 5 books × 20 chapters × 100
paragraphs = 10K paragraphs).  19-line xorshift PRNG +
a 90-sentence hand-curated prose pool with recurring
named entities — vocabulary-realistic enough to
exercise tokenisation, Snowball stemming, embeddings,
and concordance.  Mirrors the TUI save contract
(`io_atomic::write` to disk, then `update_paragraph_content`
for the bdslib copy + re-embed).

**I.1.2 — Criterion bench harness.**  `benches/`
(criterion dev-dep) with subprocess-style `startup` +
`search` scenarios driven against a gen-fixture
project via `INKHAVEN_BENCH_FIXTURE`.  Shared helpers
in `benches/common.rs`; full how-to in
`benches/README.md`.

**I.1.3 — Hotspot analysis.**  A true sampling
flamegraph needs dtrace, which macOS SIP blocks
without sudo — so I.1.3 used timing-instrumented phase
profiling instead (env-gated `INKHAVEN_PERF_TRACE`
checkpoints + a hidden `inkhaven _bench-load`).  The
data **overturned the proposal's hypotheses** and
redirected the fixes.  Two findings dominated, written
up in `Documentation/PROPOSALS/PERF.md`:

  1. **Eager embedding-engine load = 470 ms = 92 % of
     cold start**, project-size-independent.
     `Store::open` built the fastembed model
     unconditionally, even for `inkhaven list`.
  2. **`Hierarchy::flatten` was O(n²)** —
     `children_of` did a full scan per node.  18×
     nodes → 318× time ≈ 18².  Projected ~760 ms/call
     at 10K, on the tree-render path.

  (The proposal's feared `hierarchy.load` cost was a
  non-issue at 6.8 ms; ruled out by measurement.)

**I.1.4 — Lazy embedding-engine init.**
`EmbeddingEngine::new` now stores its construction
params + defers the ONNX load to the first `embed` /
`embed_batch`.  Measured, warm, 2046-node fixture:
`store.open.embedding_engine` 469.62 ms → 0.03 ms;
`total_cold_load` 507 ms → 36 ms; `inkhaven list`
subprocess 486 ms → 85.6 ms.

**I.1.5 — parent→children index.**  `Hierarchy` builds
a `HashMap<Option<Uuid>, Vec<Uuid>>` once in `load`
(O(n) pass over the already-sorted order vec, buckets
pre-sorted with no per-bucket sort).  `children_of`
becomes an O(k) lookup; `flatten` collapses to O(n).
`flatten` 31.98 ms → 0.05 ms (640×) at 2k; projected
~0.25 ms vs ~760 ms at 10K.  `has_children` /
`next_order` / `collect_subtree` / `find_by_path` all
faster for free.  No invalidation logic — `Hierarchy`
is immutable after construction.

**I.1.6 — DuckDB write batching.**  Deferred per the
data: it's the save path (not profiled by the
read-path `_bench-load`), a smaller win than #1/#2,
and wants its own `_bench-save` instrument first.

**I.1.7 — CI regression gate.**  `inkhaven
_bench-report` (15 unit tests) compares two criterion
trees, emits a markdown delta table, exits 2 past a
20 % regression.  `.github/workflows/bench.yml`
publishes a `bench-baseline` artifact on main + fails
PRs on regression.  The threshold is deliberately
loose — the regressions worth gating (re-eager-load,
re-O(n²)) are order-of-magnitude, robust to
shared-runner noise.

### R — Reader experience

Turning the manuscript into something a reader
consumes, not just a writer edits.

**R.1 — ePub export.**  `inkhaven epub` builds a
standards-compliant EPUB 3 container directly via the
in-tree `zip` crate + an in-house typst → XHTML
converter — no pandoc, zero new dependencies.  One
XHTML per chapter, `content.opf` + `nav.xhtml` +
`toc.ncx` + stylesheet.  The converter handles
headings, `_emph_`, `*strong*`, `#footnote[…]`, and
blank-line blocks; paragraph org-titles + chapter
prefixes are stripped for clean reading.  Verified:
every XML member parses well-formed, mimetype is the
stored first entry.

**R.2 — Audiobook (.m4b).**  `inkhaven audiobook`
synthesises a chapter-marked `.m4b` — per-chapter TTS
via the 1.2.17 engine, `ffprobe` for durations, an
ffmpeg metadata file accumulating chapter timestamps,
`ffmpeg` for the concat + AAC mux.  Added
`TtsEngine::audio_extension` (macOS `say -o` rejects
`.wav` + wants `.aiff`; Piper writes `.wav`) — caught
in end-to-end testing.  Verified with ffmpeg 8.1.1: a
real `.m4b` with two correctly-timed chapter markers,
AAC audio, MP4 container.  ffmpeg + ffprobe are
documented required externals.

**R.3 — Reading-time chip.**  `editor.reading_time_chip`
(default off) shows a status-bar `📖 <remaining> /
<total>` chip for the current book at
`editor.reading_wpm` (default 200) — remaining counts
from the open paragraph to the book's end.  Cheap O(n)
walk (the I.1.5 index keeps it linear).

**R.4 — Reader-pace preview.**  `Ctrl+B Shift+E` opens
a teleprompter that advances a word-by-word highlight
through the open paragraph at `reading_wpm`, so the
author experiences pacing at a reader's speed.  The
highlight position is computed from elapsed time each
frame (robust to tick granularity); the main loop
fast-ticks at 40 ms while playing, 200 ms when paused.
Space pause/resume (elapsed carries across cycles),
←→ step, r restart, Esc close.

### Closing

Both halves of the locked scope shipped: the I.1
performance pass (I.1.1–I.1.7, two algorithmic wins
that took cold start 507 ms → 36 ms and `flatten`
O(n²) → O(n)) and the reader-experience headline

reader-pace preview).

Documented; fixtures use noun cases. 12 tests. ### C.2 — Continuity lexicon + numeric/temporal/spatial contradictions **Tier 3 (lexicon — the genuine new per-language work).** Closes A.5.b's numeric/spatial half. `src/continuity.rs` — a `ContinuityLexicon` (number-words + scales + temporal units→seconds + spatial units→metres + directions), bundled for **English / French / Spanish**; `extract_quantities` parses digits, number-words, hyphenated compounds (`twenty-five`), and ` ` pairs into normalised `Quantity` values; `detect_contradictions` runs two narrow checks — spatial direction reversal (opposite cardinal + equal magnitude in a window) and proximate temporal mismatch (different durations same/adjacent sentence). Directions are only extracted attached to a magnitude, never bare — sidestepping the Spanish `este` = east/this ambiguity *and* the "walked north then south" false positive. Languages without a bundled lexicon (Russian, German, …) skip cleanly; the `bootstrap-continuity` seed CLI is a follow-up. Wired as `numeric-contradiction` (Info, no autofix). 18 tests. ### C.3 — Continuity bible (the headline) **Tier 1 (AI) + Tier 2 (stemmer comparison).** `src/continuity_bible.rs` + `src/cli/continuity.rs` — `inkhaven continuity extract` runs an AI pass (per-language prompt) recording each character's established facts to `/.inkhaven/continuity.json`; `detect_drift` groups facts by (character, attribute) and flags attributes whose stemmer-normalised values disagree across chapters; `continuity-drift` doctor class surfaces them. `inkhaven continuity list` dumps the bible. The stemmer comparison means inflected restatements ("green eyes" / "green eye", ru `зелёные` / `зелёными`) don't false-flag while genuine drift (green vs brown, `зелёные` vs `карие`) does. Embedding-based synonym-aware comparison ("green" vs "emerald", cross-language) is a C.3.b refinement; within a single-language manuscript — the common case — the stemmer comparison is sound. 14 tests (the live AI call is the only manual-verify boundary; prompt + parse are tested). ### C.4 — Unresolved-tension detector (opt-in) **Tier 1 (AI) + Tier 2.** Closes A.6.b. `src/tension.rs` + `src/cli/tension.rs` — `inkhaven tension scan` tags each chapter's introduced + resolved tensions to `/.inkhaven/tensions.json`; `detect_unresolved` flags an introduced tension when no downstream resolution (chapter index ≥ it) shares a significant stem with its topic. The matcher is *generous* about counting a tension resolved → biased toward fewer false "unresolved" flags. This scan is **opt-in** — the new `ScanClass::is_opt_in()` makes the default-run guard (`selected.map_or(!c.is_opt_in(), …)`) skip `unresolved-tension` unless explicitly `--class`-selected, because tension is a judgment call and the AI tagging is approximate. 13 tests. ### X.1 — Standard manuscript-format export `src/manuscript.rs` + `src/cli/manuscript.rs` — `inkhaven manuscript` emits a submission-ready **Shunn standard manuscript format** typst document: 12pt Courier double-spaced, 1in margins, a title page (contact top-left, rounded word count top-right, title a third down), a running `Surname / KEYWORD / page` header from page 2, chapters on fresh pages, scene breaks as a centred `#`, a `# # #` end marker, prose typst-escaped. `round_word_count` does the Shunn rounding (nearest 100 under 25k, nearest 1000 for novels); `header_keyword` derives the header word. Verified end-to-end: the exported `.typ` compiles to a valid PDF with typst — proof the format is structurally correct, not just string-matched. 11 tests. ### Closing The whole revision-&-continuity feature set shipped: four multilingual detectors (echo, numeric/temporal/ spatial contradictions, continuity bible, unresolved tension) + the Shunn manuscript export. Each detector lands on a different multilingual tier — stemmer, lexicon, AI — exactly as the three-tier plan designed, with no feature English-only: each either works across all 18 Snowball languages, rides the per-language prompt resolver, or degrades gracefully with a clear path to full coverage. A.5.b (numeric/spatial) + A.6.b (unresolved tension) are now closed. Tests grew from 1053 (cycle open) to 1121 — net +159 across the cycle. No new Rust dependencies; the detectors reuse the existing Snowball / stop-word / whatlang / AI / typst stack.
