# Inkhaven 1.2.20 — Consolidation, hardening & global themes

The 1.2.19 revision cycle moved fast and left a duplication audit behind
it. 1.2.20 pays that down — fix the bugs the audit surfaced, collapse the
copy-paste into shared helpers, then spend the headroom on the
highest-value polish carryovers. The cheapest time to consolidate the
stemmer / book-walk / AI-stream foundations is *before* the next feature
cycle stacks more copies on them.

It isn't all internal: the cycle also ships three things a writer sees
directly — a **live echo overlay** in the editor, **EPUB cover images**,
and **user-global config** with **15 ready-made colour schemes**.

Tests 1121 → 1160. One new Rust dependency (`fs2`, for the disk
pre-flight — a tiny cross-platform free-space wrapper); everything else
reuses the existing stack.

## What a writer sees

### Live echo overlay (`Ctrl+B Shift+K`)

The `echo-repetition` doctor scan from 1.2.19 now has an inline companion.
Toggle it and every occurrence in the open paragraph of a word echoing
across nearby paragraphs of the chapter is underlined — you catch a reused
distinctive word *as you write*, not at scan time.

The hard part of an echo signal is that it's cross-paragraph (unlike a
filter word you can't decide it from the current line). The overlay reads
the chapter's paragraphs — the open one **live**, so unsaved edits count —
runs the same detector the scan uses, and underlines the words whose echo
window covers the open paragraph. Two-level caching keeps it free: siblings
are re-read only on paragraph navigation, and the echo pass is skipped
while the open text is unchanged, so there's no per-keystroke I/O.

It paints in its own colour (`theme.style_warning_echo_fg`, a muted purple
by default) — deliberately distinct from the repeated-phrase magenta so a
cross-paragraph echo and a within-paragraph repeat never read as the same
finding. Master switch `editor.echo_overlay`; reuses the `editor.echo_*`
tunables; multilingual via the Snowball stemmer (`ё`→`е`-folded for
Russian). New [Tutorial 61](../Tutorials/61-echo-overlay-and-long-paragraphs.md).

### EPUB cover images

`inkhaven epub` now embeds a cover by convention. Drop a `cover.png` (or
`cover.jpg` / `cover.jpeg`) next to `inkhaven.hjson` and it ships — no flag,
no config key:

```text
$ inkhaven epub --book-name "My Novel"
Exporting `My Novel` → EPUB (12 chapters)…
  embedding cover (image/png, 184 KB)
EPUB: my-novel.epub (12 chapters · 424 KB)
```

The cover becomes the reader's library thumbnail (EPUB 3 `cover-image`
property, with an EPUB 2 `<meta name="cover">` for older readers) and the
book's opening page. An empty or unreadable file is skipped with a warning
rather than failing the export; no cover file keeps the text-only output
byte-identical.

### User-global config + 15 colour schemes

Some preferences are yours, not the project's — your colours, your
keybindings. 1.2.20 adds a **config cascade**: after a project's
`inkhaven.hjson` is read, Inkhaven layers your global override files on top,
so a personal preference applies to *every* project without per-project
edits.

Precedence, lowest → highest: built-in defaults → project `inkhaven.hjson`
→ `~/.config/inkhaven/config.hjson` → `~/.config/inkhaven/conf/*.hjson`
(sorted). The global files are **partial** (only the keys you set override)
and **win over the project** — deliberate, because `inkhaven init` writes a
full config, so a project-wins cascade would mask your global colours
entirely. A malformed global file is skipped with a warning (it never
bricks every project); a malformed project file stays fatal. Honours
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.

(Research note: HJSON has no `include` directive and `serde-hjson` adds
none, so a textual include preprocessor would have been fragile — the
value-merge cascade is both simpler and more robust.)

To make it immediately useful, the repo ships **`color_styles/`** — the 15
most popular classic, dark, and light schemes as drop-in `theme` overrides:

- **Dark** — Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox Dark, Solarized Dark, Tokyo Night,
  Monokai, One Dark, Material Ocean, Catppuccin Mocha (the built-in
  default).
- **Light** — Solarized Light, Gruvbox Light, GitHub Light, Catppuccin
  Latte, One Light, Ayu Light.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/inkhaven/conf
cp color_styles/nord.hjson ~/.config/inkhaven/conf/   # Nord, every project
```

New [Tutorial 62](../Tutorials/62-global-config-and-themes.md) +
[`color_styles/README.md`](../../color_styles/README.md).

## Hardening

- **`paragraph-too-long` doctor class** — `inkhaven doctor --scan` flags a
  paragraph whose read time at `editor.reading_wpm` exceeds
  `editor.paragraph_long_secs` (default 180s ≈ 600 words). Info, no autofix
  — a wall of text can be a deliberate breathless effect.
- **Low-disk pre-flight** — the TUI warns at startup when the project's
  volume has less than `editor.disk_warn_mb` free (default 100 MiB), before
  a long session or export. Atomic writes already fail safely on a full
  disk; this is the proactive half.
- **Uncommitted-changes quit guard** — on exit, if the project is a git
  repo with uncommitted changes, a confirm modal asks before quitting
  (`editor.warn_uncommitted_on_exit`, default on). The open buffer
  autosaves first, so the check reflects your latest edits.

## The bug the audit found

**Russian `ё`-fold in three older surfaces.** The 1.2.19 detectors fold
`ё`→`е` before Snowball stemming (the Russian algorithm treats the two as
unified). Three older surfaces stemmed Russian *without* the fold and so
mis-grouped any `ё`-word: the concordance (`пошёл` wouldn't group with
`пошла`), the style-warning overlays, and the character/place name
highlighter (`Фёдор`, `Алёша` failed to light up). All nine production stem
sites now route through one shared helper that always folds — so it can't
silently regress again.

## Consolidation (internal)

Six duplication categories from the audit collapsed into shared helpers,
each net-negative LOC with the same public behaviour (except the `ё`-fold,
the one intended change): a shared `text::normalize_stem` (fold + stem,
fixes the bug above), `cli::resolve_user_book` (was copied 6×),
`cli::book_walk` for filesystem chapter-prose collection (5 near-identical
walks), `ai::stream::collect_blocking` (5 inlined drain loops), a shared
`typst_prose` strip/split, and one home for `is_scene_break`. Where two
copies had genuinely diverged, only the truly-identical subset was unified
and the boundary documented, rather than forcing a false merge.

## Config keys added

| Key | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor.echo_overlay` | `false` | Start the live echo overlay on. |
| `theme.style_warning_echo_fg` | `#b48ead` | Echo-overlay colour. |
| `theme.style_warning_echo_modifier` | `""` | Echo-overlay text modifier. |
| `editor.paragraph_long_secs` | `180` | Read-time threshold for `paragraph-too-long`. |
| `editor.disk_warn_mb` | `100` | Low-disk pre-flight threshold (MiB). |
| `editor.warn_uncommitted_on_exit` | `true` | Confirm before quitting a dirty git repo. |

Plus the user-global override layer (`~/.config/inkhaven/`) — see
[`CONFIGURATION.md` → "Global overrides"](../CONFIGURATION.md#global-overrides-1220).

_Theme: pay down the debt the 1.2.19 revision cycle
exposed.  No new headline feature — fix the bugs the

into shared helpers, then burn down the highest-value
polish carryovers.  The cheapest time to consolidate

## Phase B — Bugs surfaced by the audit

### B.1 — Russian `ё`-fold missing in three stem surfaces

**The bug.**  1.2.19's revision detectors (`echo`,
`tension`, `continuity_bible`) fold `ё` → `е` before
Snowball stemming, because the Russian algorithm treats
the two as unified and real text uses them
interchangeably.  Three *older* surfaces stem Russian
**without** that fold and so mis-group any `ё`-word:

* `tui/concordance.rs` (`Ctrl+B Shift+L` concordance
  modal) — lines 187, 216.  `пошёл` won't group with
  `пошла`; `зелёный` splits from `зелёные`.
* `tui/style_warnings.rs` (filter-word + repeated-phrase
  overlays) — lines 104, 165, 252.  Filter words and
  repeated phrases containing `ё` silently miss.
* `tui/lexicon.rs` (character / place **name**
  highlighter) — line ~145.  A name like `Алёша`,
  `Фёдор`, `Пётр`, `Семёнов` fails to light up when the
  buffer and the name-list disagree on `ё`/`е` spelling.
  (The module's own doc comment advertises Russian
  inflection matching — this is a correctness gap in a
  shipped feature.)

**The fix.**  Route all six stem sites through the
single shared normalize helper introduced in **D.1**,
which always folds.  B.1 ships the *behaviour* fix; D.1
is the *structural* change that guarantees it can't
regress.  Lands together.

**Tests.**  A Russian regression test per surface: a
`ё`-word and its `е`-spelled inflection must land on the
same stem key / fire the same overlay / highlight the
same name.

### B.2 — Chapter-walk drift audit

The ~8 chapter-prose collectors (see D.3) have already
diverged: `epub` skips Image nodes, `audiobook` strips
footnotes, `manuscript` does neither, and the
subchapter-recursion branch exists in some walks but not
others.  Before D.3 unifies them, enumerate the
intended behaviour (recurse subchapters? strip
footnotes? include image alt-text?) so the consolidated
helper is a deliberate superset, not whichever copy
happened to win.  Output: a short decision table in the
implementation log; the unified helper in D.3 implements
it.

## Phase U — User-global config layering

### U.1 — config cascade (`~/.config/inkhaven`) (landed)

Research outcome: HJSON has no `include`/`import` directive and
`serde-hjson` adds none; a textual include preprocessor would be
fragile.  Implemented the user's fallback instead — a config
**cascade** via deep value-merge, which is strictly better than an
include.

`Config::load_layered(project_path)` layers, lowest → highest:
built-in defaults → project `inkhaven.hjson` →
`~/.config/inkhaven/config.hjson` → `~/.config/inkhaven/conf/*.hjson`
(sorted).  The global files are **partial** (only the keys present
override) and **win over the project** — deliberately, because
`inkhaven init` writes a *full* config, so a project-wins cascade
would mask the user's global preferences.

Mechanism: each HJSON file parses to a `serde_json::Value`
(`serde_hjson::from_str::<Value>`), the values deep-merge
(`merge_value`: objects merge key-by-key, everything else replaces),
and the merged value deserialises once into `Config` — starting from
`to_value(Config::default())` so the result is always complete.
Global dir honours `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, else `~/.config`.  A malformed
*global* file is skipped with a WARN (never bricks every project); a
malformed *project* file stays fatal, like `load`.

Wired through all 47 project-context `Config::load(&layout.config_path())`
sites (TUI startup + every CLI command) → `load_layered`.  The pure
`load` stays for the in-app config-editor reload, `init`, and the
prompts/tts paths (raw-file semantics; also keeps the test suite
hermetic — `load_layered_from` takes an injected dir so tests never
touch the real `~/.config`).  11 unit tests (merge, file discovery +
ordering, global-wins, fall-through, conf precedence, malformed-skip,
partial-project).  CONFIGURATION.md gains a "Global overrides"
section.  Suite 1148 → 1159.

# Inkhaven 1.2.21 — The Facts book

Early on, an author collects research in **Notes** and **Research**. But
the *invariants* of a world — it's equatorial, no winter; the capital is
three days' ride inland; the war ended a generation ago — are a different
kind of thing: the ground truth every chapter must stay consistent with.
1.2.21 gives them a dedicated **Facts** system book and wires the AI to
treat it as the authoritative reference, end to end: collect facts,
interrogate them, check prose against them, and sweep the whole
manuscript for contradictions.

Tests 1160 → 1169. Zero new Rust dependencies — Facts reuses the existing
store, embeddings, AI-stream, and wiki-link stack. One new tutorial
([63](../Tutorials/63-facts-and-fact-checking.md)).

## The Facts book

Every project now has a **Facts** system book alongside Notes and
Research — free-form prose, no schema. Write a paragraph per fact (or per
topic). Don't want to start from blank? **`inkhaven facts init`** scaffolds
the usual categories (Climate, Geography, Seasons, Chronology, Culture,
Rules) as fill-in-the-blank paragraphs — idempotent, and `--genre
fantasy|scifi|mystery|historical` appends genre-specific categories
(magic system, FTL/physics, suspects & alibis, anachronism watch, …).

## Writing against your facts

**Facts AI scope (`F9`).** The AI scope cycle gains a **Facts** stop
(after Book). Enter it and the chat seeds a fact-analysis session: every
fact loaded as a visible prologue, the model framed as a grounded
fact-checker. It's *sticky* (stays active across follow-ups) and always
runs **Local** (your facts are the ground truth, regardless of F10). Edit
the Facts book and re-cycling F9 **refreshes** the loaded set.

**Fact-check chord (`Ctrl+B Shift+X`).** A one-shot check of the open
paragraph against the Facts book — the scope is locked to the local
paragraph, the verdict streams in as `claim | fact | detail` lines, and
**`Ctrl+B Shift+J`** then cycles the findings, jumping the editor cursor
to each flagged claim. If you've wiki-linked the scene to particular
facts (`Ctrl+V A`), those lead the grounding.

**Facts search (`Ctrl+B Shift+S`).** A semantic-search modal — type a
query, mark the matching facts, and send just those into a targeted Facts
chat. The scalable path for a large Facts book: ground in the relevant
handful instead of the whole book.

## Sweeping the manuscript

**`inkhaven facts scan`** walks every chapter, retrieves the facts
relevant to each (semantic search, so a big Facts book stays cheap), and
flags contradictions — written to `.inkhaven/facts_scan.json`. `facts
list` re-dumps; `--json` on either feeds a CI gate.

**`inkhaven facts extract`** solves the cold-start: an AI pass reads the
manuscript, proposes the world-facts the prose implicitly establishes,
and — after an interactive `y/N/a/q` review (deduped against what you
already have) — writes the accepted ones into the Facts book. `--dry-run`
to preview, `--yes` to accept all.

## Provenance and dependents

A Fact is just a paragraph, so it joins the wiki-link system across books:
`Ctrl+V A` links a Fact to its **Notes/Research** source (provenance) or a
scene to the facts it relies on; `Ctrl+V K` on a Fact shows every scene
that depends on it (dependents to re-check when a fact changes). An opt-in
status-bar chip (`editor.show_facts_chip`) shows the Facts-book entry
count at a glance.

## Multilingual

Every AI surface — the Facts-scope framing, the fact-check, the scan, and
the extract prompts — ships in English, Russian, German, French, and
Spanish, selected by the project's `language`.

## Config keys added

| Key | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor.show_facts_chip` | `false` | Show the `⚑N` Facts-count chip in the status bar. |

New CLI: `inkhaven facts scan` / `list` / `extract` / `init`. New chords:
`Ctrl+B Shift+X` (fact-check), `Ctrl+B Shift+S` (Facts search), `Ctrl+B
Shift+J` (next finding); `F9` gains a **Facts** scope. See
[`KEYBINDING.md`](../KEYBINDING.md) and
[Tutorial 63](../Tutorials/63-facts-and-fact-checking.md).

# Inkhaven 1.2.21 — The Facts book

_Theme: a first-class home for the **facts** a book's world
runs on — climate, geography, seasons, distances,
chronology — and the AI plumbing to write against them and
check prose for contradictions._

Early on, an author collects research in the **Notes** and
**Research** system books — loose plot notes, source
material.  But the *invariants* of the world (it's winter
in this hemisphere; the capital is three days' ride from
the coast; the war ended a generation ago) are a different
kind of thing: they're the ground truth every chapter must
stay consistent with.  1.2.21 gives them a dedicated
**Facts** system book and wires the AI to treat it as the
authoritative reference.

Four parts, one dependency chain (F.1 → F.2 → F.3 → F.4),
plus docs.

## Architecture seams (verified)

* **System books** — one source of truth: `SYSTEM_BOOKS`
  (`src/store/mod.rs:29`) + a `SYSTEM_TAG_*` const.
  `ensure_system_books()` auto-creates on open; user/system
  separation is already `system_tag.is_some()` everywhere.
  Notes/Research are the model (free-form prose).
* **AI scope** — the `AiMode` enum (`src/tui/inference.rs:45`):
  `None → Selection → Paragraph → Subchapter → Chapter →
  Book`.  `build_ai_mode_context()` (`app.rs:12558`) is the
  single function turning a scope into context text.
* **Chat pre-seed** — `chat_history: Vec<ChatTurn>`
  (`ChatTurn::User|Assistant`), replayed in
  `spawn_chat_stream` (`src/ai/stream.rs:35`).
* **Multilingual prompts** — the `*_default_prompt(lang_iso)`
  5-language pattern (`app.rs:~19716`) + `resolve_prompt` /
  `active_prompt_language` / `iso_from_long`.  Clone
  show-don't-tell.
* **Free chord** — `Ctrl+B Shift+X` is unbound; joins the
  Shift-family diagnostic cluster (Shift+T sdt, Shift+H
  rhythm, Shift+M rewrite).

## Phase F.1 — The Facts system book

Add `("facts", "Facts")` to `SYSTEM_BOOKS` (after
`research`) + `pub const SYSTEM_TAG_FACTS`.  Update the
doc-comments that enumerate the system-book set.  No
schema, no overlay — it's free-form prose like Notes (see
Decision 2).  `ensure_system_books()` creates it on the
next open; verify it renders in the tree and `inkhaven

## Phase F.2 — Facts AI scope

`AiMode::Facts`, cycled **after `Book`** (so F9 reads
`… → Chapter → Book → Facts → None`, i.e. Facts sits
between Book and Selection in the wrap).  `next()` /
`label()` / quick-ref text.  A `build_ai_mode_context()`
branch that gathers every Facts-book paragraph
(`system_book_id(SYSTEM_TAG_FACTS)` → `collect_subtree` →
`get_content`) into a context block, formatted like the
Chapter/Book branch but headed `── Facts reference (N) ──`.

## Phase F.3 — Facts-scope chat pre-seed + fact-analysis prompt

When the Facts scope is active, pre-seed the conversation
so the author can interrogate their world's invariants:

* a multilingual **system prompt** —
  `facts_scope_system_prompt(lang_iso)` — that frames the
  model as a facts-analysis / fact-checking assistant
  grounded in the supplied Facts reference, and
* the Facts-book paragraphs loaded as the opening
  `ChatTurn` history so the model already "has" them.

5-language coverage (en/ru/de/fr/es), resolved the same way
as every other prompt.

## Phase F.4 — "Fact check" chord (`Ctrl+B Shift+X`)

`Action::FactCheck` (serde `editor.fact_check`) +
label/description/binding/dispatch; handler
`start_fact_check()` cloning the show-don't-tell flow.  Per
Decision 1, on fire it:

* **auto-locks the AI scope to Paragraph ("local")** — the
  check is about *this* paragraph, never a whole-book send;
* **grounds against the Facts book** — when Facts is
  non-empty, its content is injected as a ground-truth
  reference block ahead of the paragraph, so the model can
  flag contradictions ("the manuscript says snow, but your
  Facts say this region is tropical").  Empty Facts → a
  plain local fact-check.

Adds `fact_check_default_prompt(lang_iso)` (5 languages),
streams the verdict to the AI pane.  KEYBINDING.md row.

## Phase F.5 — Tutorial + notes

Tutorial 63 walking the whole loop (collect facts → Facts
scope chat → fact-check a paragraph), CONFIGURATION /
KEYBINDING entries, release-notes implementation log.

## Decisions

1. **The fact-check chord grounds against the Facts book
   and auto-locks scope to local (Paragraph).**  When you
   fact-check a paragraph, the effective scope is forced to
   the local paragraph and the Facts book is injected as
   the authoritative reference — so it checks *this* prose
   against *your* established facts, not the whole
   manuscript against general knowledge.  Falls back to a
   generic local check when the Facts book is empty.
2. **No prose overlay / theme colour for Facts.**  It's
   free-form prose like Notes, not an entity lexicon like
   Characters/Places, so Facts entries don't light up words
   in the manuscript.  (A "fact mention" overlay is an easy
   later add if wanted.)

## Out of scope (later)

* A deterministic (non-AI) contradiction scan of prose
  against structured facts — would need a Facts schema;
  this cycle keeps Facts free-form.
* A `Ctrl+Y`-style Facts lexicon-inference lookup chord.

## Facts — follow-ups

Selected after the 1.2.21 build review (the user's call); captured here
for a later cycle.  Expands and supersedes the brief "Out of scope"
list above.  Ordered by leverage.

### FF.1 — Semantic fact-search modal (explicit RAG)

**Problem.**  Both the Facts scope seed (F.3) and the fact-check chord
(F.4) inject **every** Facts paragraph, every turn.  For a richly-built
world (hundreds of facts) that overflows the context window and burns
tokens.

**Design (user's call — explicit, not auto-RAG).**  A new chord opens
a **Facts search modal**: type a query → semantic search over the
Facts-book paragraphs → ranked matches → feed only the matching facts
to the AI as grounding.  User-driven retrieval rather than
dump-everything.

* Reuse the existing embeddings + HNSW vector index — the
  similar-paragraph picker (`Ctrl+V S`, Tutorial 16) is the closest
  model for the modal + ranked list.
* Subsumes the earlier "relevant-facts lookup" idea and the "token
  controls" idea — this *is* the relevance filter, made interactive.
* **Open decisions for impl:**
  * How results feed the AI — pick-and-send selected entries, or
    auto-send top-K above a similarity threshold (offer both: Enter =
    send selected, a key = send all shown).
  * Integration with the F.3 scope seed: for a large Facts book, the
    Facts scope could seed only the top-K relevant to the open
    paragraph (or defer entirely to this modal) instead of seeding
    everything.  Keep the full seed for small books.
  * Pick a free chord (verify at impl time) — candidate `Ctrl+B
    Shift+S` (S for Search facts); confirm it's unbound first.
  * Needs a public `Store::embed(text)` accessor (also wanted by the
    deferred C.3.b continuity work).

### FF.2 — Whole-manuscript fact-check scan

A `fact-contradiction` `doctor --scan` class: walk every chapter /
paragraph, check each against the Facts book (RAG-filtered per FF.1 to
keep cost sane), and report Info-severity findings — the batch
companion to the one-paragraph `Ctrl+B Shift+X` chord.  `--json` for CI
gates, like the other narrative scans.  AI-backed per paragraph, so
note the cost; sampling / RAG-filtering / a cache mitigates it.  See
the structure note below — a deterministic pass becomes possible if
facts gain optional structure.

### FF.3 — Fact extraction from prose

The reverse direction, mirroring `inkhaven continuity extract`: an AI
pass that reads the manuscript and proposes the world-invariant facts
it has *implicitly* established ("'three days' ride' appears twice —
add as a fact?"), presented for review and accept-into the Facts book.
Solves the cold-start problem (an empty Facts book does nothing).

* CLI `inkhaven facts extract` + a TUI review/accept flow (y/N per
  candidate, like `inkhaven recover`).
* Dedupe candidates against existing Facts entries (stem / embedding
  similarity) so a re-run doesn't re-propose what's already there.
* Approach sketch: chunk the manuscript by chapter, prompt the model
  to emit candidate facts as a structured list (category + statement +
  the source paragraph), collect, dedupe, present.

### FF.4 — Tier 2 bundle

* **FF.4a — Freshness / re-seed.**  The F.3 seed snapshots the facts
  when you enter the scope; editing the Facts book mid-session leaves
  the chat stale.  Re-seed on Facts-book change (or a manual "reload
  facts" key); the `⟦Facts⟧` marker already makes the seed detectable
  for replacement.
* **FF.4b — Force Local inference for fact-checking.**  Fiction facts
  must not be overridden by the model's real-world knowledge
  ("equatorial regions *can* get snow at altitude…").  The Facts scope
  + chord should default to `Local` (grounded only in the supplied
  facts), not inherit the F10 `Full` toggle.  Possibly a config knob
  (`editor.facts_force_local`, default true).
* **FF.4c — Facts scaffolder + genre templates.**  Like the Language
  book's `b`-scaffold: seed a starter skeleton (Climate, Geography,
  Calendar / Chronology, Politics, Economy, Tech / Magic rules, …),
  genre-aware.  Turns an empty Facts book into fill-in-the-blanks.
* **FF.4d — Actionable fact-check output.**  The verdict is plain text
  today.  Make it navigable — jump to the contradicting *fact* and to
  the offending *phrase* in the paragraph (reuse the diagnostics
  navigation pattern, Tutorial 27); optionally structured markers the
  AI pane can parse.

### FF.5 — Facts ↔ source linking + backlinks

Link a fact to where it came from and what depends on it, reusing the
existing paragraph-link machinery (`linked_paragraphs`, `Ctrl+V
A/I/L/K`, wiki-links — Tutorial 19):

* fact → its **Notes / Research** source (provenance), and
* fact ↔ the **manuscript paragraphs** that rely on it (backlinks).

Then "this fact changed" can surface the N dependent paragraphs to
re-check — the natural pairing with FF.4a freshness and the FF.2 scan.

### FF.6 — Status-bar facts chip

A quiet `facts: N` count chip, toggled by config like the worldbuilding
glossary chip (`editor.show_glossary_chip`) and the POV chip — so the
Facts book's presence + size is visible at a glance.

### Cross-cutting decision — free-form vs optional structure

Facts are free-form prose today (Decision 2), which is right for
collection.  But FF.2 (a cheap *deterministic* contradiction pass) and
FF.4d (structured, navigable output) get much sharper if a fact can
carry **optional** light structure — e.g. a leading tagged line
(`#climate equatorial, no winter`) the way Threads paragraphs front
HJSON.  Keep prose the default; consider an optional structured form.
Decide this **before** building FF.2, since it shapes the scan.

# Inkhaven 1.2.22 — Project-wide find & replace

The edit a novelist needs most often is the one Inkhaven couldn't do:
change something *across the whole book*. Find/replace worked only on the
open paragraph; the concordance was read-only. Renaming a character over 40
chapters was impossible without leaving the editor.

1.2.22 adds **project-wide find & replace** — and does it **safely**:
nothing changes without review, and every touched paragraph is snapshotted
first. It's also the last 1.2 before the 1.3 *editorial pass* cycle: the
review-gated apply machinery here is the substrate that cycle's AI-proposed
edits will reuse.

Tests 1169 → 1186. Zero new Rust dependencies — the matcher rides the
`regex` crate already in-tree. One new tutorial
([64](../Tutorials/64-project-find-and-replace.md)).

## In the editor

Open Find & Replace with `Ctrl+R`, type your pattern and replacement, then
**`Ctrl+B`** toggles the scope from *this paragraph* to *the whole book*.
**Enter** scans every user-book paragraph and opens a **review modal**:

- Every match is shown **in context** with the hit highlighted, grouped by
  paragraph.
- **`Space`** skips (or un-skips) the match under the cursor, **`a`** keeps
  all, **`n`** skips none — per-match control, nothing applied blindly.
- **`Enter`** applies only the kept matches; **`Esc`** cancels.

Each changed paragraph is **snapshotted before the write** (annotated
`replace: X → Y`), so `F6` is your undo.

## From the command line

`inkhaven replace <pattern> <replacement>` mirrors it with a
preview-then-apply gate for scripted / CI renames:

```text
$ inkhaven replace "Anne" "Anna" --dry-run
…  »Anne« looked up …
replace: 37 matches in 24 paragraphs — dry run, nothing changed

$ inkhaven replace "Anne" "Anna" --yes
replace: applied 37 replacements in 24 paragraphs; 24 snapshots taken (restore via F6 in the editor)
```

A bare `inkhaven replace …` refuses to write and just reports the count, so
it's always safe. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--regex` (with `$1`…
captures), `--substring`, `--ignore-case`, `--book <name>`,
`--include-system`.

## The safe-by-design choices

- **Lexical, not semantic** — literal / whole-word / opt-in regex over a
  linear scan of paragraph bodies. Find-replace wants *exhaustive exact*
  matches with byte positions, which a vector index can't do; the scan
  never touches the embeddings, and there's no second full-text index to
  maintain.
- **Whole-word by default** — kills the `Will`/`will`, `Mark`/`market`
  footgun. `--substring` (CLI) for raw substring matching.
- **User books only by default** — a manuscript rename won't silently
  rewrite your Notes / Research / Facts. `--include-system` opts in.
- **Always reversible** — snapshot-before-write on every touched paragraph;
  the CLI dry-run previews, the editor reviews per match.

## Also in 1.2.22

Three consolidation-audit items (a shared reading-time formatter, a shared
sentence splitter, a shared chapter-prose walk) were examined and **closed
as intentional non-duplicates** — on inspection they share only a
superficial shape and diverge in substance (rounding/format, boundary
algorithm, conversion/formatting), so merging would change behaviour or add
abstraction for negative benefit. The divergence is now documented at each
site so the audit isn't re-attempted.

## New surfaces

- CLI: `inkhaven replace`.
- Editor: `Ctrl+B` in the Find & Replace modal toggles whole-book scope and
  opens the review. See [`KEYBINDING.md` §3.10](../KEYBINDING.md) and
  [Tutorial 64](../Tutorials/64-project-find-and-replace.md).

# Inkhaven 1.2.22 — Project-wide editing & pre-1.3 tidy-up

_The last 1.2.  Two jobs: ship one solid author feature, and leave the
ground clean (and pre-poured) for the 1.3 "Editorial Pass" cycle.  The
headline is **project-wide find & replace, review-gated** — the #1
unmet structural-edit need, which doubles as the apply-with-review
substrate 1.3's agentic editing will stand on.  Around it: pay down the
consolidation tail and clear the last stability carryover._

## Why this is the right final 1.2

Across 1.2.x we built a deep single-author tool, but two gaps remain
that 1.3 wants closed first:

1. **No safe way to edit across the book.**  Find/replace is
   per-paragraph (`src/tui/search_replace.rs`); the concordance is
   read-only.  Renaming a character across 40 chapters is impossible
   without it — and the *review-gated apply-with-snapshots* machinery
   it needs is exactly what 1.3's agentic editor (AI proposes edits,
   author approves) will reuse.  Build it now → authors get the feature
   and 1.3 inherits the substrate.
2. **Loose ends.**  A few consolidation carryovers and one stability
   item are cheaper to clear now than to carry across a major boundary.

## Decisions (locked)

1. **Matching is lexical, not semantic, and there is no FTS index.**
   Literal substring by default, **word-boundary** toggle (on by
   default in the TUI — kills the `Will`/`will` footgun), **opt-in
   regex**, optional case-insensitive.  A manuscript is one book (a few
   MB); find-replace needs *exhaustive exact* matches with byte
   positions, which an inverted index can neither rank-replace nor do
   for substring/regex/word-boundary — so it's a **linear scan** over
   paragraph bodies.  **No Tantivy** (removed in 1.2.16, HNSW-only
   since; re-adding means a second index to sync, for zero benefit).
   The vector index is never touched by replace.  **Zero new deps** —
   the `regex` crate is already in-tree (it backs the per-paragraph
   `search_replace.rs`).
2. **Nothing applies unreviewed, everything is reversible.**  TUI: a
   review modal with per-match accept/skip.  CLI: `--dry-run` preview
   then explicit `--yes`.  Every touched paragraph is **snapshotted
   before the write** (the existing snapshot path), writes are atomic
   (`io_atomic`).  Undo = the snapshots.
3. **Scope is user books by default.**  System books (Notes / Research
   / Facts / Characters / …) are excluded unless `--include-system`
   (or a modal toggle) — a manuscript rename shouldn't silently rewrite
   your Facts/Notes.  Optional `--book <name>` narrows further.
4. **Paragraphs only.**  HJSON-data and Script leaves are out of scope
   for replace this round.

## Phase R — Project-wide find & replace (headline)

### R.1 — The matcher + match model (pure)

New `src/replace.rs` (pure, unit-tested): the match/apply primitives,
no I/O.

* `ReplaceOpts { regex: bool, word_boundary: bool, ignore_case: bool }`.
* `find_matches(text: &str, pattern: &str, repl: &str, opts) -> Vec<Hit>`
  where `Hit { line, col, byte_range, matched: String, preview: String }`
  (`preview` = KWIC context — reuse the concordance's snippet shaping).
  Literal → escaped regex or `match_indices`; word-boundary → `\b`
  wrap; regex → compiled `regex::Regex`.  Invalid regex → a clean
  `Err`, surfaced to the user (mirrors `search_replace.rs` today).
* `apply(text, hits_accepted, repl) -> String` — apply accepted hits
  **right-to-left by byte offset** so earlier replacements don't
  invalidate later positions.  Regex captures (`$1`) honoured in repl.

Tests: literal vs word-boundary (`Mark`/`market`), regex + captures,
case-insensitive, multi-match-per-line right-to-left apply, no-op when
nothing accepted, invalid-regex error.

### R.2 — Project scan

A walk that runs `find_matches` over every in-scope paragraph and
returns `Vec<ParaMatches { para_id, title, slug_path, hits }>`.

* User-book paragraphs only by default (`hierarchy` children with
  `system_tag.is_none()` → `collect_subtree` → `NodeKind::Paragraph`),
  bodies via `store.get_content` (the path `facts_scan` / export already
  use).  `--book` / `--include-system` adjust the set.
* Linear, no index.  Over-read is fine — we already do full walks for
  export / audiobook / `facts scan`.

### R.3 — Review modal (TUI)

`Modal::ReplaceReview { pattern, repl, opts, matches, marked, cursor,
scroll }` — clone the two-phase shape of the `Modal::FactsSearch` modal
(query/edit ↔ results, `Space` multi-select) shipped in 1.2.21.

* Entry: extend the existing find/replace flow (`search_replace.rs`)
  with a **scope toggle** (paragraph ↔ book); on "book", after the
  pattern + replacement are entered, run R.2 and open the review.
  Reuses the existing input UI — minimal new chrome.
* Render: each match in KWIC context with the matched span highlighted
  + a `[x]`/`[ ]` mark box; header shows `pattern → repl` + the active
  opts; footer the keys.  Group rows by paragraph (breadcrumb headers).
* Keys: `↑↓` navigate, `Space` toggle, `a` mark-all / `A` none,
  `w` word-boundary, `i` ignore-case (re-runs the scan), `Enter` apply
  marked, `Esc` cancel.
* No matches → status "no matches"; nothing marked + Enter → no-op.

### R.4 — Snapshot + atomic apply

For each paragraph with ≥1 accepted hit: build the new body with
`replace::apply`, **snapshot the paragraph first** (the
`snapshot_impl` / store snapshot path, annotated e.g. `before replace:
"Anne"→"Anna"`), then `io_atomic::write` the `.typ` +
`store.update_paragraph_content`.  Reload the open buffer if it was
touched.  Summary: `replaced N occurrence(s) in M paragraph(s) —
snapshots taken (F6 to restore)`.

### R.5 — CLI `inkhaven replace`

`inkhaven replace <pattern> <replacement> [--regex] [--word]
[--ignore-case] [--book <name>] [--include-system] [--dry-run]
[--yes]`.

* `--dry-run` prints every match (KWIC + `slug:line`) and the count,
  changes nothing — CI / script-safe, the way to preview before
  trusting a bulk rename.
* Without `--yes`, refuse to write (print the count + "re-run with
  `--yes` to apply").  With `--yes`, apply all matches with the same
  snapshot-before-write as the TUI.
* Per-match accept/skip is **TUI-only**; the CLI is preview +
  apply-all-with-snapshots (the scripted/CI path).  Reuses R.1–R.2 +
  the R.4 apply.

## Phase D — Consolidation tail (pre-1.3 hygiene)

Net-negative LOC, low risk, so 1.3's aggregator builds on tidy ground.

* **D.7** — unify reading-time (`text_utils::format_reading_time`,
  fixed 250 wpm, vs the configurable `tui/reading_time`) onto the
  configurable one; share the sentence-split boundary logic between
  `continuity.rs` and `sentence_rhythm.rs` (keep their distinct return
  shapes as thin wrappers).
* **D.3.b** — the store-side `append_branch_prose` shape shared by
  `cli::epub` + `cli::audiobook`; unify only the genuinely-identical
  part (they diverge on xhtml+`<h2>` vs plain).
* **D.8 (optional)** — extract the repeated "walk user-book chapters /
  paragraphs" into one shared helper (continuity / tension / facts_scan
  each re-implement `user_book_chapters`).  Direct 1.3 prep — the
  editorial pass iterates exactly this.

## Phase M — Stability carryover

* **M.1** — cap the crash-report action-ring `detail` length
  (`src/crash/`).  The last open item from the 1.2.15 stability bar; a
  cheap defensive bound to leave 1.2 clean.  (M3 script-modal-spoofing
  stays deferred — theoretical for a single-user local tool.)

## Out of scope — owned by 1.3 / 2.0

* **Unified `Finding` type + the Editorial Pass aggregator** — the
  heart of 1.3; doing it here would blur the release boundary.
* **Agentic editing** (AI proposes edits applied through the review
  path) — 2.0; R.3/R.4 is the substrate it will reuse.
* **Semantic-scoped replace** ("replace only in chapters about X") —
  stretch; the scan + a vector pre-filter, deferred.
* **Tantivy / a second full-text index** — explicitly not (see
  Decision 1).
* Replace in HJSON-data / Script leaves; multi-file regex across
  non-prose.

## Recommended scope for 1.2.22

**Phase R (R.1–R.5) + D.7 + D.3.b + M.1.**  D.8 if time allows.  A
coherent "last 1.2": one headline author feature that bridges to 1.3,
plus a clean-desk pass.

## Implementation log

_(entries land here as the work lands)_

### R.1 — pure matcher (landed)

New `src/replace.rs` — the lexical match/apply primitives, no I/O:

* `ReplaceOpts { regex, word_boundary, ignore_case }` — `Default` is
  literal + whole-word (the safe default; no `Will`/`will` surprise).
* `find_matches(text, pattern, repl, opts) -> Result<Vec<Hit>, _>` —
  builds one `regex::Regex` (literal → `regex::escape`; word-boundary →

  the context line.  Empty pattern → `EmptyPattern`; bad regex →
  `BadRegex`.
* `apply(text, accepted)` — splices the accepted subset right-to-left by
  byte offset so earlier edits don't shift later ones; char-boundary
  guarded.

# Inkhaven 1.2.23 — Stability & fixes

The last 1.2 housekeeping pass before the 1.3 *Editorial Pass* cycle. No
new headline feature — a crash-behaviour fix, a whole-tree panic-surface
re-audit, SQL hardening across the storage layer, the deferred find &
replace polish, and one consolidation. The goal: a clean, calm base for
1.3.

Tests 1186 → 1190. Zero new Rust dependencies.

## Broken pipe no longer writes a crash report

Piping inkhaven's stdout into a truncating reader (`inkhaven … | head`)
made the print macros panic with `Broken pipe (os error 32)` — Rust
ignores SIGPIPE — and the crash hook turned that normal shell event into
a spurious `inkhaven-crash-<UTC>.hjson` in the working directory.

Fixed in the panic hook with a **Step 0** that detects the print-macro
broken-pipe panic (`is_broken_pipe_panic` — narrow: requires the
`failed printing to std…` prefix *and* a broken-pipe error, so a disk-full
or any other output failure still surfaces a report), restores the
terminal, and exits cleanly. No SIGPIPE reset — that would risk killing
the long-running TUI on any internal/subprocess pipe close — so the editor
is untouched. Verified: `inkhaven … --dry-run | head` exits 0 with no
crash file.

## Panic-surface re-audit

Four parallel auditors swept the whole tree. It is broadly clean to the
1.2.15 bar — no reachable `panic!`/`unreachable!`, no lock-poison
surfaces, no production `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` on user-data paths. The
real findings clustered into one recurring class — **UTF-8 byte-boundary
slicing using an offset taken from a lowercased/transformed copy** — plus
a write-durability item. All fixed:

- **`config::parse_color`** — a multibyte char in a 3- or 6-byte hex
  theme value (e.g. `"#aé"`) split a UTF-8 char and panicked, reachable
  from *any* HJSON theme field. Now gated with `is_ascii()` (regression
  test added).
- **`jump_cursor_to_text`** — a `to_lowercase()` byte offset sliced the
  original line; non-English folds (Turkish İ, ẞ, ligatures) before the
  match panicked. Reachable via fact-check navigation. Fixed by slicing
  the lowercased string.
- **`doctor_scan`** naming scan — same class: a lowercased offset sliced
  the original prose. Reachable via `inkhaven doctor` on multilingual
  prose. Fixed with an `is_char_boundary` guard.
- **`store/mod.rs`** — four `std::fs::write` sites (paragraph/script
  templates, seeded body, image bytes) routed through `io_atomic::write`
  for torn-write safety, matching the house standard.

## SQL hardening

The storage layer is now free of string-interpolated SQL. The JSON +
blob stores (`storage/engine.rs`) and the progress store
(`progress/store.rs`) migrated their `format!` + `sql_escape` SELECTs onto
bound parameters via a new `select_all_with`; the JSON document binds as a
parameter and casts in-SQL (`CAST(? AS JSON)`). Both copies of
`sql_escape` are removed. Never an injection vector before (the only
interpolated value was serde-serialized JSON), but the binding approach is
robust by construction. A new adversarial round-trip test stores a
document full of quotes, backslashes, and a `'; DROP TABLE …` string and
confirms it round-trips intact with the table whole.

## Find & replace polish

The project-replace review modal (1.2.22) now lets you change the matching
mode in place: **`w`** toggles whole-word, **`i`** ignore-case, **`x`**
regex — each re-runs the scan, and the header shows the active mode. So
the editor reaches the same regex / substring / case modes the CLI's
`inkhaven replace` flags do, starting from the safe whole-word default.

## Consolidation

`continuity`, `tension`, and `facts_scan` each carried a byte-identical
manuscript walk; the triplicate is now one `Hierarchy::user_book_chapters()`
method (net-negative LOC). Direct 1.3 prep — the Editorial Pass iterates
exactly this walk.

## Carried forward to 1.3

- **M.1** — cap the crash-report action-ring `detail` length (the last
  open 1.2.15 stability item).
- The **find & replace modal live click-through** (engine + key wiring are
  unit/CLI-verified; only the on-screen interaction is unconfirmed).
- Low-priority stability items reported by the audit: `backup`/`config`
  non-atomic sentinel saves, `backup::restore` per-entry atomicity.
- Older carryovers: ePub inline images + popup footnotes; the 1.2.19
  continuity/anachronism follow-ups; audiobook polish.

# v1.2.3 — multi-format export · similar-paragraph mode · writing goals · Bund polish

Mid-cycle release on the `1.2.3` branch. Three broad themes:

1. **Multi-format export** — markdown / TeX / EPUB in addition
   to Typst / PDF, generated in-process. No `pandoc`, no
   `tex live` install needed.
2. **Writing-progress subsystem** — append-only event log,
   configurable goals (daily words, streak, per-book deadlines,
   status-ladder targets), status-bar widget, Ctrl+V G modal.
3. **Bund + editor polish** — the floating output pane, the
   `Ctrl+Z ?` script picker, the `ink.input` prompt modal, a
   second editor for similar-paragraph comparison, dynamic
   Quick Help.

## Headline changes

### Multi-format export

CLI:

```sh
inkhaven export markdown -o draft.md
inkhaven export tex      -o draft.tex
inkhaven export epub     -o draft.epub
```

- **markdown** — in-process Typst → markdown converter
  (`src/export/markdown.rs`). Headings, lists, emphasis,
  `#image(…)` with caption. Unknown directives are kept
  verbatim inside inline-code spans.
- **tex** — via the new [`tylax`](https://crates.io/crates/tylax)
  dependency (pure Rust, Apache-2.0). Adds a minimal
  `\documentclass{book}` preamble if tylax didn't emit one.
- **epub** — single-chapter EPUB3 zip built with the existing
  `zip` + `pulldown-cmark` deps. mimetype stored uncompressed
  (readers reject the archive otherwise).

**`--book-name` flag** — required when a project hosts more
than one user book. Matches case-insensitively against title,
falls back to slug. System books (Help / Scripts / Typst /
Prompts / Places / Characters / Notes / Artefacts / Research)
are excluded from every export path — they're inkhaven
internals, not manuscript content.

**Ctrl+B O extras** — new `output.extra_formats: []` HJSON knob.
Listed formats land next to the PDF with the same stem; errors
logged but never abort the take.

**Ctrl+V markdown extraction** — `Ctrl+V 1` (editor: buffer),
`Ctrl+V 2` (editor: containing subchapter subtree), `Ctrl+V 1`
(tree: cursor's node + descendants). All write to launch cwd
as `<slug>-YYYYDDMM-HHMM.md`.

Tutorial: [`15-multi-format-export.md`](../Tutorials/15-multi-format-export.md).

### Writing-progress tracking + goals

Self-contained subsystem at `src/progress/` with its own DuckDB
file at `<project>/progress.db`.

- **Event log** — `writing_events` (every save / status promotion
  carries `word_delta` + `total_words` + book id) +
  `writing_baselines` (per-day morning snapshot per user book +
  project-wide).
- **`today_words` semantics** — current total − today's baseline
  (diff vs morning, not sum-of-deltas). Honest about
  delete-then-rewrite.
- **Streak with grace** — `streak_grace_per_week` allows N
  missed days inside the rolling 7-day window before the streak
  breaks.
- **Per-book targets** — `target_words` + `deadline` (ISO date);
  required pace falls out of arithmetic. Past-due deadlines
  collapse to "the remaining gap, all at once".
- **Status-ladder targets** — trailing-7-days promotion counts
  against per-status goals (`ready: 1`, `final: 3`, …).
- **HJSON** — new `goals:` stanza in `inkhaven.hjson`.

Status-bar widget on the right edge of the status row:
```
today 1,247/1500w · streak 3d · story 12,300/80,000w (pace 165w/d)
```

**Ctrl+V G** opens `Modal::Progress` — two-column layout with
today / streak / per-book / status ladder on the left and a
30-day `ratatui::Sparkline` on the right. `r` refreshes.

`ratatui-plt` was scoped — and dropped — because it's GPL-3.0
and would force inkhaven (Apache-2.0/MIT) to GPL. The built-in
ratatui charting widgets are sufficient for v1.

Tutorial: [`17-writing-goals.md`](../Tutorials/17-writing-goals.md).

### Similar-paragraph mode

`Ctrl+V S` saves the current buffer, runs a vector-similarity
search against every other paragraph (current id filtered, only
paragraphs surfaced), opens a picker. Pick a hit and it loads
into a new `secondary` slot — the AI pane is repurposed as a
second editor.

- **Side-by-side editing** — both editors live; `Tab` swaps
  keyboard focus. Implementation is a `mem::swap` wrapper around
  `handle_editor_key` + `save_current` so all existing editor
  handlers keep working unchanged.
- **Slug-path footer** in each pane in similar mode.
- **Ctrl+V S again** saves both buffers and drops the secondary,
  AI pane returns.

Tutorial: [`16-similar-paragraphs.md`](../Tutorials/16-similar-paragraphs.md).

### Bund: floating output pane

Multi-line script output stops clobbering the status bar.

```bund
"Report" ink.pane.show
"Header"           println
"Row 1: foo"       println
"Row 2: bar"       println
```

While the pane is open `print` / `println` reroute there.
`Ctrl+C` clears, `Esc` closes.

New words: `ink.pane.show`, `ink.pane.close`, `ink.pane.clear`,
`ink.pane.line` — all `editor_read` category (non-destructive UI).

### Bund: Ctrl+Z ? script picker

Discovery chord. Lists `Script` nodes under the cursor's nearest
enclosing branch (Book / Chapter / Subchapter); `A` toggles to
the `Scripts` system book; `Enter` evaluates the chosen script
through the Adam VM. Output flows into the floating pane when
open, otherwise the status bar.

Falls back to the `Scripts` book automatically when the branch
scope is empty — one less keystroke for the most common case.

### Bund: ink.input prompt modal

```bund
:hook.greet ( name -- )
  "Hello, " swap concat println
;

"What's your name?" "greet" ink.input
```

Modal opens, user types, `Enter` pushes the string and fires
the named hook. `Esc` cancels without firing.

Hook-driven rather than synchronous so autosave / inference
polling / Typst build timers keep ticking while the prompt is
open.

### Dynamic Quick Help (Ctrl+B H)

The "Meta chords" and "Bund chords" sections of the
quick-reference panel are now synthesised from
`KeyBindings::active()` instead of hardcoded `&'static str`
tables. User overrides via `keys.bindings` and runtime
`ink.key.*` mutations flow into Ctrl+B H without a rebuild.

Each row uses the new `Action::description()` — a
user-friendly sentence ("Take the book — build then copy the
PDF and any configured extras into the launch cwd.") rather
than the terse status-bar `label()`.

User-bound Bund lambdas surface as
`User-bound Bund lambda <name> (registered via ink.key.bind_lambda).`

## Other changes

- Bund stack helpers now lowercase status strings consistently
  in `record_status_change`.
- `Action::BundOpenScriptPicker` variant added to `keybind::Action`
  enum; default binding is `bund_sub` `?`.
- Modal renderer dispatch table gains `BundPane`, `ScriptPicker`,
  `SimilarPicker`, `Progress`, `BundInput` arms.
- `Action::description()` shipped for every action including the
  `BundLambda(name)` runtime-only variant.

## Migration notes

- **HJSON additions** — `output: {}` and `goals: {}` are both
  `#[serde(default)]`, so 1.2.2 configs continue to work.
- **`progress.db`** is created on first launch under the project
  root. Delete it to reset writing-progress history; the next
  launch recreates an empty store.
- **Default export behaviour changed**: `inkhaven export <fmt>`
  (no `--book-name`) previously concatenated paragraphs from
  every top-level book including system books. In 1.2.3 it
  scopes to user books only; with multiple user books it
  requires `--book-name`. This is a behaviour fix — system-book
  content (Help reference, Typst reference, prompts) was almost
  certainly never wanted in your exported manuscript.
- **`tylax 0.3`** added as a dependency, `default-features = false`
  to drop the bundled CLI. Adds ~2 MB to the release binary.

## Files added

- `src/export/{mod,markdown,tex,epub}.rs` — 4 new files, ~800 LOC
  total.
- `src/progress/{mod,store,aggregates,word_count}.rs` — 4 new
  files, ~700 LOC total.
- `Documentation/Tutorials/{15,16,17,18}-*.md` — 4 new tutorials.

## Stats

- 158 tests pass (10 new across progress + markdown).
- One license-driven dep dropped (`ratatui-plt` GPL-3.0).
- Approximate diffstat: +3,500 LOC across src + Documentation.

# v1.2.4 — wiki-links · navigation pack · Scrivener import · 22 new features

The 1.2.4 cycle is the largest single-release feature batch
since 1.1. Five broad themes:

1. **Knowledge graph** — wiki-links + backlinks as metadata
   (Ctrl+V A / I / L / K), AI-inference integration.
2. **Navigation pack** — fuzzy paragraph picker (Ctrl+V P),
   bookmarks (Ctrl+V B / M), AI prompt history, prefix-ranked
   slash-command picker.
3. **Snapshot diff + safety net** — F6 V diff view, pre-restore
   safety snapshot on Enter.
4. **Goals & tracking deepening** — per-paragraph word-count
   targets + auto-promote, active-time tracking, per-book bar
   chart, `--status=<floor>` export.
5. **Single-binary Scrivener import** — pure-Rust `.scriv`
   ingestion with RTF→Typst conversion.

Plus a long tail of polish: F-key migration into the bindings
table, save-as picker, theme persistence to HJSON, five new
Bund hooks, `ink.fs.*` words, tree multi-select with bulk T/O,
`inkhaven stats`, startup splash, Windows CI re-enabled.

## Headline changes

### Wiki-links and backlinks (metadata-only)

Four chords add typed references between paragraphs as
metadata — never embedded in the Typst source, never leaking
into PDF / EPUB:

| Chord     | Direction | What |
|-----------|-----------|------|
| `Ctrl+V A` | Outgoing  | Add a link FROM the open paragraph TO a tree-picked one. |
| `Ctrl+V I` | Incoming  | Add a link FROM a tree-picked paragraph TO the open one. |
| `Ctrl+V L` | Outgoing  | Picker listing the open paragraph's outgoing links. Enter opens; D removes. |
| `Ctrl+V K` | Incoming  | Backlinks picker — paragraphs that link TO the open one. Enter opens; D removes the source's outgoing link. |

Three guards fire at add time: self-link rejection, duplicate
detection, and cycle detection (`"You can not create circular
references"` — DFS over the candidate target's outgoing
closure). The cycle check is what makes outgoing-link metadata
safe to walk for AI inference.

AI integration: when scope is Paragraph (F9 cycles), inkhaven
appends each linked paragraph to the prompt context wrapped in
`── Linked paragraph: <title> ──` delimiters.

Status-bar widget appends `links N` when ≥ 1 outgoing link.

Storage: `Node.linked_paragraphs: Vec<Uuid>`, serde-default
empty. Stale targets are filtered from pickers silently.

Tutorial: [`19-wiki-links.md`](../Tutorials/19-wiki-links.md).

### Snapshot diff + pre-restore safety snapshot

In the F6 snapshot picker:

- **`V`** on a row — opens a side-by-side line diff of the
  snapshot vs the live buffer. Powered by the `similar` crate's
  Myers algorithm; consecutive Delete→Insert pairs fuse into a
  single Changed row (yellow `~`) so a one-line rewrite renders
  as one row instead of two. Esc returns to the picker via a
  `return_to: Box<Modal>` stash.
- **`Enter`** — restores the snapshot, but **first** takes a
  fresh snapshot of the live buffer. The pre-restore safety
  snapshot lands in the same history list. Failing to create
  the safety snapshot aborts the load — the whole point is
  data safety.

Recovery flow: hit F6 again, the safety snapshot is at the
top, Enter restores it. The "restore you didn't want" is
itself now a safety snapshot — the chain stays intact
indefinitely.

Tutorial: [`20-snapshot-diff.md`](../Tutorials/20-snapshot-diff.md).

### Navigation pack

- **`Ctrl+V P` fuzzy picker** — type-to-filter modal over
  every paragraph in the project (system books filtered).
  Three-tier scoring: title-starts-with > title-contains >
  slug-contains. Enter opens via the same `open_search_result`
  flow as the search overlay (autosaves previous buffer, tree
  cursor follows).
- **`Ctrl+V B` / `Ctrl+V M`** — toggle bookmark on open
  paragraph; bookmark picker (`★`-prefixed list, title-sorted,
  D removes). Bookmarks persist (`Node.bookmark: bool`).
- **AI prompt Up-arrow history** — capped at 500, dedupes
  consecutive sends, any edit clears the cursor. The
  shell-style behaviour whose absence in 1.2.3 was an
  oversight.
- **Slash-command prefix ranking** — `/sum` now ranks
  `summarize` (name prefix) above any prompt that happens to
  contain `sum` mid-word. Tier scoring: name-starts > desc
  word-starts > anywhere-substring.

Tutorial: [`21-navigation.md`](../Tutorials/21-navigation.md).

### Per-paragraph word-count goals + auto-promote

- **`Ctrl+V T`** opens a goal-target modal for the open
  paragraph (empty input clears). Persisted as
  `Node.target_words: Option<i32>`.
- **Auto-promote** — when `goals.auto_promote_on_target` is
  set (default `false`) and a save crosses the target, the
  paragraph's status promotes one rung up the ladder. Records
  in `Node.target_hit_at_status` to fire exactly once per
  (paragraph, status) pair — re-editing past the target after
  reverting status won't auto-promote again unless you change
  the target.
- **Editor footer** shows `title_breadcrumb · 412/500 · ▏▏▏▏▏░░`
  in the goal row when a target is set. Title path, not
  slug-path.
- **Tree pane** keeps a 1-char status pip; the full gauge
  moved to the editor footer (long titles were clipping in
  the tree).

Five new Bund hooks fire alongside:
`hook.on_goal_hit`, `hook.on_streak_break`,
`hook.on_status_promoted`, `hook.on_assemble`, `hook.on_take`.

### Active-time tracking

`writing_events` adds an `active_seconds_in_range` aggregate
computed with a `LAG` window + `SUM(LEAST(gap_seconds, 300))`.
Translation: each save→save gap is summed but capped at 5
minutes per gap, so a half-hour AFK break doesn't count.

Status-bar surfaces `45m` of today's active time, `goals.active_minutes_daily`
gates an explicit per-day target.

### Per-book bar chart

The Ctrl+V G progress modal grows a per-book bar chart pane
(ratatui's built-in `BarChart`, license-clean). Each user
book's per-day word delta over the trailing 14 days. Stays
within the same modal — `r` refreshes everything.

### `inkhaven export --status=<floor>`

```sh
inkhaven export tex --status=ready -o final.tex
```

Filters to paragraphs whose status sits at or above the rung.
Lowercased ladder names — `napkin`, `first`, `second`,
`third`, `final`, `ready`. Unset = include everything (1.2.3
behaviour). System books are still excluded.

### Save-as picker for Ctrl+V markdown extraction

Ctrl+V 1 / 2 / 3 now open a `Modal::SaveMarkdown` with the
default path pre-filled. Bare Enter writes there (mimics
1.2.3 behaviour); editing the path writes to the picked
location. F2-style filename picker but inlined.

### Ctrl+V is a first-class meta key, F-keys in keybind table

- `view_prefix: "Ctrl+V"` in `inkhaven.hjson`'s `keys` block —
  rebindable like the Bund prefix.
- 12 view-sub actions appear in HJSON `keys.bindings` under
  `view_sub` and accept lambda binds via `ink.key.bind_view_sub`.
- 10 top-level F-keys (F1 through F10 + Shift-F variants)
  moved from hardcoded matches into `Layer::TopLevel` of the
  `KeyBindings` table. HJSON overlays accept single-token
  chords (`"f7": "view.add_link"` rebinds F7 to outgoing-link
  add).
- `Ctrl+B H` quick reference is updated to surface View and
  TopLevel layers; user lambdas appear with their registered
  name.

### Theme persistence to HJSON

Live theme edits via `ink.theme.set` / Ctrl+B T cycling now
persist to `inkhaven.hjson`. New helper `set_key_in_hjson_block`
edits the existing `theme: { ... }` block in place, preserving
comments and order. Persisting falls back to a status-bar
warning if the file is read-only.

### Bund stdlib gaps closed

| Word | What |
|------|------|
| `ink.editor.replace_all ( old new -- count )` | In-buffer find/replace. |
| `ink.search.load ( query -- )` | Run semantic search + load first hit into the editor. |
| `ink.ai.send_blocking ( prompt -- response )` | Synchronous AI send (blocks the script; UI keeps repainting). |
| `ink.ai.poll ( -- response-or-empty )` | Poll the async AI response slot — empty string when none ready. |
| `ink.paragraph.set_target ( words -- )` / `ink.paragraph.target ( -- words )` | Per-paragraph word target on the current paragraph. |
| `ink.fs.read ( path -- string )` | Read a file. Default-allowed (`fs_read`). |
| `ink.fs.write ( path content -- )` | Write a file. Default-**denied** (`fs_write` — `policy.allow.fs_write` must be true). |

`ink.fs.write` is default-denied because a script that can
write anywhere on the user's disk is a different security
class from one that can edit the open buffer. Opt in
explicitly in `bund.policy.allow.fs_write = true`.

### Tree multi-select + bulk T/O chords

- **`Space`** in the tree pane marks/unmarks the cursor row.
  Status bar shows `marked N`. **`Esc`** clears all marks.
- **`T`** cycles node type — `paragraph → json → script`. With
  marks, applies to every marked leaf; without marks, to the
  cursor row only.
- **`O`** cycles status — `napkin → first → second → third →
  final → ready → napkin` (configurable). With marks, bulk
  promotes/demotes every marked paragraph.

`Ctrl+B I` (reindex) and `Del` (delete) now also read the
mark set when present. `Ctrl+B R` (rename) is intentionally
single-row only — renames are per-row by design.

Tutorial: [`22-tree-multiselect.md`](../Tutorials/22-tree-multiselect.md).

### Scrivener importer (single-binary)

```sh
inkhaven import-scrivener ~/Scrivener/Tides.scriv --dry-run
inkhaven import-scrivener ~/Scrivener/Tides.scriv
```

Pure-Rust pipeline:

- **`quick-xml = 0.36`** parses `.scriv/Files/Data/<id>/binder.xml`
  into a `BinderItem { uuid, kind, title, children }` tree.
  Modern Scrivener UUIDs are passed through; legacy integer
  IDs get a deterministic `Uuid::new_v5` hash so re-imports
  produce stable UUIDs.
- **`rtf-parser-tt = 0.5`** parses each Text document's RTF
  body. The walker emits Typst markup: `**bold**`, `_italic_`,
  paragraph breaks. Typst meta chars are escaped. Tables /
  footnotes / images are dropped with a per-paragraph error
  entry; the prose survives.
- **Mapping rules**: Draft → Book, depth-1 Folder → Chapter,
  deeper Folder → Subchapter, Text → Paragraph. Outside-Draft
  top-level folders route by title: Places / Locations /
  Settings → `Places`; Characters / Cast → `Characters`;
  Notes / Research → `Notes` (merged); Artefacts / Artifacts /
  Items → `Artefacts`. Everything else is `SkipSubtree`.
- **Flags**: `--draft-as-book <title>`, `--skip-research`,
  `--dry-run`. Per-item error containment — one bad RTF blob
  doesn't abort the whole import.

Tutorial: [`23-scrivener-import.md`](../Tutorials/23-scrivener-import.md).

### Secondary-editor autosave

When similar-paragraph mode (Ctrl+V S) opens the secondary
editor, both buffers now autosave on idle and on Ctrl+V S
exit. The secondary slot stops being a write-only black hole.
Implementation uses `Option::take()` to avoid aliasing
borrows in `tick_autosave`.

### Per-paragraph file rename follows title rename

`Store::rename_node` for paragraphs now also renames the `.typ`
file on disk. Before 1.2.4, a paragraph renamed in the TUI
stayed `untitled.typ` until manually reindexed; now the file
name follows the title slug immediately.

### `inkhaven stats` CLI

```sh
inkhaven stats --book-name "Tides"
```

Per-paragraph table: title, slug, status, word count, target
percentage, last modified. Same `--book-name` semantics as
`export`. System books excluded.

### Startup splash with project pulse

Default-on (`editor.startup_splash: true`). At launch shows a
7-second floating pane:

```
inkhaven 1.2.4
  Today        1,247 / 1,500 words  (▏▏▏▏▏░░)
  Active       45m / 60m
  Streak       3 days
  Books        2 user · 9 system · 412 paragraphs
```

Auto-closes after 7 seconds; any key dismisses early. Set
`editor.startup_splash: false` to skip.

### Windows CI re-enabled

The release matrix's Windows entry, commented out since the
fontconfig build failure in 1.2.1, is back. New "Install
Windows build dependencies" step uses vcpkg to install
`fontconfig:x64-windows-static-md`, exports `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` +
`VCPKGRS_TRIPLET` to `$GITHUB_ENV`. `continue-on-error: true`
specifically for the Windows target so a regression there
doesn't block Linux/macOS releases.

## Other changes

- `KeyBindings::view_prefix` field + `view_sub: Vec<BindingEntry>`
  + `top_level: Vec<BindingEntry>` + `resolve_view_sub` /
  `resolve_top_level` helpers.
- `Modal` enum grows `ParagraphTarget`, `Progress`,
  `SnapshotDiff`, `SaveMarkdown`, `LinkPicker`, `BacklinkPicker`,
  `BookmarkPicker`, `FuzzyParagraphPicker`.
- `LinkPickDirection { Outgoing, Incoming }` swap-on-commit
  pattern handles symmetric outgoing / incoming flows in one
  code path.
- `compute_line_diff` + `fuzzy_filter_entries` helpers in
  `tui/app.rs`.
- New CLI subcommands: `Stats`, `ImportScrivener`. `Export`
  gains `--status`.

## Migration notes

- **HJSON additions** — `goals.daily_active_minutes`,
  `goals.auto_promote_on_target`, `goals.status_ladder`,
  `keys.view_prefix`, `editor.startup_splash` all `#[serde(default)]`.

# v1.2.5 — Typst goes in-process

The headline of 1.2.5 is one HJSON line:

```hjson
typst_compile: { engine: "inprocess" }
```

Flip it and inkhaven stops shelling out to the host's `typst`
binary for builds. The full compiler — `typst` + `typst-pdf` +
`typst-kit` (fonts + `@preview` packages) — is linked into
every 1.2.5 binary and runs inside the inkhaven process.
Structured `SourceDiagnostic`s replace stderr blobs. The
external CLI stays the default; the switch is a runtime
decision.

Around that one switch:

1. **Diagnostics** — `typst-syntax` parse check on save / idle
   (Phase 1, always on). Optional full-compile semantic check
   when `engine = "inprocess"`. `Ctrl+V N` jumps the cursor
   between them.
2. **Render preview** — `Ctrl+V R` rasterises the open
   paragraph and floats it on top of the editor. `← / →`
   navigate pages, `S` saves the current page, `A` saves all
   pages.
3. **TUI integration** — splash + `Esc`-cancel + autosave
   before `Ctrl+B A / B / O`. The new engine is a peer of the
   external CLI in every flow.
4. **`inkhaven doctor`** — health report: binary, engine,
   fonts, package cache, project shape, actionable warnings.
5. **Logo in credits** — `Ctrl+B V` now banners the embedded
   `logo.png` above the version + dependency list.

## Headline changes

### In-process compile engine (`engine = "inprocess"`)

```hjson
typst_compile: {
  engine: "inprocess"
}
```

Replaces the `Child::spawn("typst", ...)` path with
`typst::compile::<PagedDocument>` + `typst_pdf::pdf`. The
compile runs on a worker thread; the foreground TUI keeps
animating the spinner. Both engines write the PDF to the same
path.

* **Fonts** — bundled `embed-fonts` set (Computer Modern +
  Linux Libertine, ~10 MB) plus the user's system fonts via
  `typst-kit`'s fontdb searcher. Either source toggleable via
  `bundle_fonts` / `use_system_fonts`.
* **`@preview/<pkg>` resolution** — first fetch is online,
  subsequent uses hit the OS cache directory
  (`~/Library/Caches/typst/packages` on macOS, etc.). Disable
  with `packages_enabled: false` for hermetic builds.
* **Diagnostics** — structured `SourceDiagnostic`s with span
  info, formatted into stderr-shaped strings so the existing
  AI error-analysis hook works unchanged.

### Typst-syntax parse diagnostics (Phase 1)

```hjson
typst_compile: {
  diagnostics:              true   // default
  diagnostics_idle_seconds: 2
}
```

Pulls in `typst-syntax` (parser only — no eval, layout,
render, fonts, package resolver). On every save and on every
`diagnostics_idle_seconds` of editor idle, re-parses the open
paragraph. First parse error lands on the status bar:

```
typst: line 12:5 — expected `}`, found end of file
```

Engine-independent — works the same in `external` and
`inprocess`. Bund and HJSON content types are skipped.

### Semantic diagnostics (opt-in)

```hjson
typst_compile: {
  semantic_diagnostics: true   // needs engine = "inprocess"
}
```

When both flags are on and the parse check passes, a full
`typst::compile` runs against the open paragraph in isolation
and surfaces semantic errors (`#unknown_func` → "unknown
variable", type mismatches, missing-font references). Costs
~20–200 ms per check on warm caches.

**False positives are expected** for paragraphs that reference
book-level definitions. Leave off when manuscripts lean on
preamble-defined helpers.

### Ctrl+V N — diagnostic navigation

Jump the editor cursor to the next typst diagnostic in the
open buffer. Wraps at the end. Status bar reports
`diag 2/5 line 12:5 — <message>`. Pairs with the parse +
semantic checks above for a tight type-save-fix loop.

### Ctrl+V R — render paragraph preview

```
Ctrl+V R                         → save buffer → compile in-process → float PNG preview
  Inside the preview:
    ← / → (or ↑ / ↓)             → previous / next page
    Home / End                   → first / last page
    S                            → save current page at 4.0 px/pt (~288 dpi) via picker
    A                            → save all pages → `<base>-page-001.png`, `-002.png`, …
    Esc                          → close back to editor
```

Cancelling the save picker (Esc) restores the preview with
navigation state intact. Successful writes close back to the
editor.

Requires a terminal with graphics support (kitty / iterm2 /
sixel via ratatui-image). Terminals without graphics surface a
status-bar hint instead of opening an empty modal.

### TUI integration

- **Splash + Esc-cancel** — Ctrl+B B / Ctrl+B O paint a
  centered splash with spinner + book + active engine +
  elapsed seconds. **Esc** cancels: external sends SIGTERM,
  in-process flips a cancel flag (worker thread keeps running
  until typst finishes naturally; foreground unblocks
  immediately). AI error-analysis path is skipped on cancel.
- **Autosave before A / B / O** — assemble, build, take all
  save the primary editor (and the secondary editor in
  similar-paragraph mode) before walking `.typ` files. No
  more "I just pressed Ctrl+B B and the build used yesterday's
  saved version".
- **Engine visibility** — three surfaces:
  * `inkhaven doctor` reports it explicitly.
  * `Ctrl+B V` credits pane carries a `Typst engine` row.
  * The compile splash shows it above `Elapsed:`.

### `inkhaven doctor`

```sh
inkhaven doctor
```

Three sections + warnings: **Binary** (version, repo,
rust-version), **Typst engine** (engine summary, external
typst path, every related HJSON knob), **Package cache**
(path, entries, size), **Project** (hierarchy shape + word
counts when run inside an initialised project), **Notes**
(actionable warnings like `typst is NOT on PATH` or `engine
has BOTH bundle_fonts AND use_system_fonts disabled`).

Pipe-friendly plain-text output — no colour, no TTY tricks.

### Story view — Ctrl+V W

Build a visual graph of the current user book and float it on
top of the editor. Pipeline:

1. Walk the book's hierarchy + count leaves under every node.
2. Lay it out as a **twopi-style radial tree** (book at centre,
   each depth on a concentric ring; sibling wedges sized
   proportional to subtree leaf counts). Lexicon nodes
   (Characters / Places / Artefacts) land on an outer ring at
   the angle of their first mentioned paragraph, with a small
   5°-bucket nudge so co-located names don't stack.
3. Emit SVG by hand — different shape per node kind (book =
   folder, chapter = box, subchapter = octagon, typst
   paragraph = ellipse, hjson = note, script = parallelogram,
   image = chevron; Characters = egg, Places = diamond,
   Artefacts = hexagon). Long titles word-wrap to multiple
   lines (max 22 chars per line × 4 lines, then `…`); each
   node's bounding box scales to fit its wrapped label so text
   never overlaps the boundary. Solid grey edges for the
   structural skeleton, dashed purple for `linked_paragraphs`
   wiki-links, dashed green for lexicon mentions. Edge
   endpoints are truncated by each node's own circumscribing
   radius (which now varies with label size) so arrowheads
   touch the shape, not the centre.
4. `resvg` + `tiny-skia` rasterises the SVG to a PNG. System
   fonts are loaded once into a process-wide
   `usvg::fontdb::Database` (the default empty fontdb made
   labels invisible).
5. ratatui-image protocol displays it in a `Modal::StoryView`
   that floats over the editor.

The radial layout is a hand-rolled twopi implementation
(layout-rs's only mode is Sugiyama hierarchical, which crowded
deep books). Bypassing layout-rs also dropped a ~1k-LOC dep.

Inside the modal:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `S` | Save PNG via picker — default `<book-slug>-story-YYYYDDMM-HHMM.png` |
| `Esc` | Close back to the editor |

The save picker re-uses the same `return_to` stash pattern the
SaveRenderedPng picker uses — Esc on the picker restores the
preview unchanged. No re-render on save; the PNG bytes the
preview displays are exactly what lands on disk.

Lexicon mention detection is case-insensitive substring match
over each paragraph's body — fast on book-sized graphs (a few
hundred ms on a typical book + ~50 lexicon nodes). Only
lexicon nodes that ARE mentioned appear in the graph; the rest
stay hidden so the picture doesn't fill with orphan icons.

### Node tagging system

```hjson
// no config required — tags live in node metadata
```

Three entry points, one project-wide tag namespace:

* **`Ctrl+B ]`** — open the floating tag picker scoped to the
  open editor paragraph. `↑↓` select, `Space` multi-selects,
  `T` applies the selected tags (or the cursor tag if nothing
  selected), `A` prompts for a new tag (auto-selected on add),
  `D` deletes a tag project-wide (y/n confirm shows blast
  radius), `Esc` closes.
* **`Ctrl+B }`** — search-by-tag picker. `Enter` on a tag
  opens a second pane listing every paragraph that carries
  it, with a typeable filter input. `Enter` on a paragraph
  opens it in the editor (autosaves prev; tree cursor
  follows).
* **`g`** in the tree pane — same picker as `Ctrl+B ]` but
  the apply target is the marked set (or the cursor row when
  no marks). `T` applies the selected tag set across every
  marked paragraph in one go.

Tags are stored as `Node.tags: Vec<String>` (serde-default
empty). Free-form strings; case is preserved on save, deduped
case-sensitively in the picker; whitespace trimmed; empty tags
rejected. Project-wide deletion walks every node and rewrites
the metadata blob, reporting `removed from N paragraph(s)` on
the status bar.

### Embedded logo in credits

`include_bytes!("../../logo.png")` ships the project logo
straight in the binary. Decoded lazily into a static
`OnceLock<Option<DynamicImage>>`. `Ctrl+B V` (credits) banners
it above the version + dependency list. Terminals without
graphics support collapse the banner to 0 rows; the rest of
the pane is unchanged.

# v1.2.6 — Tools for the working novelist

1.2.6 is a big release. Where 1.2.5 was a single headline
(in-process Typst), this one moves on multiple fronts at
once. The unifying theme: turn inkhaven from a TUI for
writing into a TUI for **publishing** — every feature that
landed this cycle helps the author cross the gap between a
draft and a shippable manuscript.

Six theme groups carried the cycle:

1. **Tagging is a first-class metadata layer.**  Project-
   wide picker, rename, search, tag-filtered export, and
   tree-pane pips. Scrivener keywords come across as tags
   on import.
2. **Diagnostics get an editor surface.**  Red `●` gutter
   markers, an F8 list modal, Ctrl+V N / Shift+N
   navigation, and a Ctrl+F12 AI-explain chord that
   sends the diagnostic + ±5 context lines to the model.
3. **AI as a writing partner, not a tool.**  F12 critique
   (mode-aware), opt-in per-paragraph memory, and a
   side-by-side diff modal that gates every buffer-
   replacing apply.
4. **Snapshots learn to label themselves.**  F5 pops an
   annotation prompt; F6 surfaces it in the picker.
5. **The story view splits into two scopes.**  Ctrl+V w
   (lowercase) for the paragraph-focused mini view;
   Ctrl+V Shift+W for the full book.
6. **A story timeline.**  Calendar-aware events,
   chronological picker (Ctrl+V e), a swim-lane view
   (Ctrl+V t) with scope navigation, and an AI health
   critique. New CLI subcommands; new Bund stdlib +
   hooks. Phase 1–4 all in 1.2.6 — opt-in via
   `timeline.enabled: true`.

Around those: a Bund stdlib for tags + events + story
view + 1-based cursor positioning; new hooks
(`hook.on_diagnostic`, `hook.on_event_added`,
`hook.on_event_orphaned`); a render-preview live zoom;
seven new walkthrough tutorials (25–31); and a
companion book — the **Book of Inkhaven** — that
collects the whole user surface into one printed +
markdown artefact.

The branch carries 25 commits and ~6,000 lines of new
code. 249 tests + 5 ignored pass throughout.

## Headline changes

### Tags as a project-wide metadata layer

```
Ctrl+B ]   — tag picker on the open paragraph
g (tree)   — same picker, applies to multi-selection
Ctrl+B }   — project-wide tag search
```

Inside the picker:

```
Space   toggle the cursor tag
A       add a new tag (one-line prompt)
R       rename project-wide (merges if name exists)
D       delete project-wide (confirm + count)
T       commit marked tags onto the target
```

Tag pips render in the tree pane as compact `#tag` chips
after the progress dot. Up to two visible + a `+N` count.

CLI: `inkhaven export --tag <name>` filters the export to
paragraphs carrying that tag. AND-combines with `--status`.

Bund: five `ink.tag.*` words (list, list_for, search,
add, remove). Reads under `store_read`; writes under
`store_write`.

Scrivener: keyword import (modern Scrivener 3.x
`<KeywordRef>` + older inline `<Keywords>`) lands as
inkhaven tags automatically.

### Diagnostics get an editor surface

Gutter `●` (red, bold) appears in the line-number column
of every line that carries a typst diagnostic. Both parse
(always on) and semantic (requires `engine = "inprocess"`)
diagnostics surface here.

```
F8                  diagnostics list modal — Enter jumps cursor
Ctrl+V N / Shift+N  next / previous diagnostic in the open buffer
Ctrl+F12            AI explain the diagnostic at cursor
                    (was F11; macOS grabs F11 — see below)
```

`hook.on_diagnostic ( uuid count first-message -- )`
fires on state changes (clean → errored, count change,
top message change). Debounced — no spam on idle ticks.

`ink.editor.set_cursor ( row col -- )` is the 1-based
counterpart to the existing 0-based `ink.editor.goto`.
Matches typst's diagnostic line/col convention so a
hook can auto-jump to the first error without offset
arithmetic.

### AI critique + per-paragraph memory + diff modal

Three additions that compound:

```
F12                  AI critique (mode-aware)
                       plain edit  → critique-edit prompt
                       split-edit  → critique-changes prompt

ai: {
  per_paragraph_memory: true   # default false
  diff_review_on_apply: true   # default true
}
```

`per_paragraph_memory` records every Paragraph-scoped
turn onto the open paragraph's `Node.ai_memory` field;
subsequent Paragraph-scope prompts prepend it to the
chat history. Effect: a paragraph carries its own
conversation with the model. Come back days later, the
context restores.

`diff_review_on_apply` (default true) routes every
buffer-replacing apply (`r` and `g` in the AI pane)
through a side-by-side diff modal:

```
a / A / Enter   accept — apply and refocus the editor
r / R           reject — buffer unchanged
e / E           alias for `a`
↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn   scroll
Esc             same as reject
```

Smart extraction: the AI's reply is scanned for a
discrete corrected block before applying. Tries
`<<<CORRECTED>>>` markers, relaxed Unicode bracket pairs
(`«»`, `≪≫`), trailing code fence, and `Corrected:`
heading in order. If any matches, only the block lands —
not the commentary around it. Models that drift from
the canonical marker shape (deepseek, occasionally
gemini under load) get caught by the relaxed pass.

`F5` opens a one-line prompt before creating the

│  Snapshot `The Storm` — annotation:                       │
│  › before the lighthouse rewrite│                         │
│   Enter commits (empty = no note) · Esc cancels           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The buffer to snapshot is captured at prompt-open time so
you can keep typing in the editor without affecting what
gets saved. Empty annotation commits without a note —
